Part II — Business Rules & Constraints

Business Rules Specification

Inventory Management System

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-BR-001
Document Title Business Rules — Inventory Management System
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Senior Business Analyst
Source Document BRD-IMS-001 (Business Requirements Document, Version 1.0)
Date July 5, 2026
Scope Business policies only — no technical validation logic, system constraints, or implementation detail

Purpose

This document extracts and elaborates all 32 industry business rules defined in the approved BRD (Section 13). Each rule is expressed as an enforceable business policy governing how the organization manages inventory, independent of how any system implements it.

Rule Category Legend

Category Description
Inventory Stock availability, commitment, replenishment, and network balance
Purchasing Procurement, inbound supply, and supplier accountability
Warehousing Receiving, storage, movement, and fulfillment execution
Products Product master data, lifecycle, classification, and commercial positioning
Users Governance, accountability, segregation of duties, and authorization
Reporting Performance measurement, audit, and management oversight

Business Rules Catalog

Availability and Customer Commitment

BR-001 — ATP-Only Customer Commitment

Attribute Detail
Rule Name ATP-Only Customer Commitment
Business Rule Statement The organization must sell and promise stock only against available-to-promise (ATP) quantity. On-hand quantity that is reserved, committed, quarantined, or otherwise unavailable must not be quoted or committed to customers.
Business Reason On-hand quantity includes stock already reserved or committed to other orders. Quoting or selling against total on-hand causes overselling — confirming orders the business cannot fulfill. ATP is the only honest measure of what can still be promised to new customers.
Related Business Process BP-10 (Inventory Status Monitoring), BP-16 (Order Availability Confirmation)
Related Functional Requirements FR-024 (Display ATP quantity), FR-041 (Confirm order availability before commitment), FR-025 (Display reserved and committed stock)
Rule Category Inventory

BR-002 — Reservation at Order Confirmation

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Reservation at Order Confirmation
Business Rule Statement Stock must be reserved at the point of order confirmation. Once a customer order is confirmed for fulfillment, the required quantity must be committed against on-hand stock and removed from ATP until fulfilled or released.
Business Reason The gap between order confirmation and physical picking creates a window where the same stock can be sold to multiple customers. Reservation converts a commercial commitment into an operational hold, preventing double-allocation.
Related Business Process BP-17 (Inventory Reservation)
Related Functional Requirements FR-042 (Reserve inventory for confirmed orders), FR-025 (Display reserved and committed stock), FR-043 (Release inventory reservations)
Rule Category Inventory

BR-003 — Verified Pick Before Shipment

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Verified Pick Before Shipment
Business Rule Statement The organization must not ship or deduct inventory until pick verification is complete. Orders may only be marked shipped after the correct items are physically retrieved, verified against the order, packed, and handed to the carrier.
Business Reason Inventory should not be deducted and orders should not be marked shipped until the correct items are physically retrieved, verified, packed, and handed to the carrier. Premature shipment recording creates inaccurate stock and false delivery expectations.
Related Business Process BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship)
Related Functional Requirements FR-044 (Support pick, pack, and ship workflow), FR-029 (Record all inventory movements with full history)
Rule Category Warehousing

BR-028 — Backorder Customer Acknowledgment

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Backorder Customer Acknowledgment
Business Rule Statement A backorder requires explicit customer acknowledgment before it is recorded. Customers must be informed of the delay, expected fulfillment timing, and their option to cancel or accept partial delivery.
Business Reason A backorder is a mutual agreement to wait — not an internal note that an order cannot ship. Customers must be informed of the delay, the expected fulfillment date, and their right to cancel. Silent backorders destroy trust.
Related Business Process BP-19 (Partial Fulfillment & Backorder Management)
Related Functional Requirements FR-045 (Handle partial fulfillment), FR-046 (Manage backorders and replenishment priority)
Rule Category Inventory

Inbound and Procurement

BR-004 — Verify Before Inventory Acceptance

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Verify Before Inventory Acceptance
Business Rule Statement Inbound goods must be verified before acceptance into inventory. Quantity, product identity, and condition must be confirmed against the purchase order or authorized receipt documentation before stock is recorded as on-hand.
Business Reason Arrival at the dock is not receipt. Until quantity, product identity, and condition are verified against the purchase order, the business does not know what it actually received. Recording unverified quantities corrupts inventory from the point of entry.
Related Business Process BP-07 (Goods Receipt & Verification)
Related Functional Requirements FR-015 (Receive and verify inbound goods), FR-003 (Support product identifier lookup)
Rule Category Warehousing

BR-005 — Put-Away Before Availability

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Put-Away Before Availability
Business Rule Statement Received stock is not available for sale or fulfillment until put-away is complete. Stock verified at the receiving dock does not increase ATP until it is placed in its designated storage location and put-away is confirmed.
Business Reason Stock sitting in the receiving area is physically in the building but not operationally available. Pickers cannot find it efficiently, it may be damaged in transit areas, and it is not in its designated storage location. Availability begins when put-away is confirmed.
Related Business Process BP-09 (Stock Put-Away & Storage)
Related Functional Requirements FR-018 (Manage put-away and stock availability timing), FR-024 (Display ATP quantity)
Rule Category Warehousing

BR-006 — Document Receipt Discrepancies

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Document Receipt Discrepancies
Business Rule Statement Receipt discrepancies must be documented before acceptance. Short shipments, over-shipments, wrong items, and damage must be recorded at the point of receipt with supporting evidence before quantities are accepted into inventory.
Business Reason Short shipments, over-shipments, wrong items, and damage must be recorded at the point of receipt — when evidence exists and the carrier or supplier is present. Undocumented acceptance waives the business's right to claim and hides supplier performance problems.
Related Business Process BP-08 (Receipt Discrepancy Resolution)
Related Functional Requirements FR-016 (Document and resolve receipt discrepancies), FR-011 (Maintain standard reason codes)
Rule Category Purchasing

BR-007 — Purchase Order Required for Supplier Receipt

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Purchase Order Required for Supplier Receipt
Business Rule Statement A valid purchase order is required before receiving supplier goods. Supplier shipments must be matched to an authorized purchase order before acceptance, except where an explicitly approved ad-hoc receipt exception applies.
Business Reason A purchase order is the authorized commercial commitment that defines what was ordered, at what price, and from whom. Receiving without a PO breaks financial controls, enables unauthorized purchases, and prevents three-way matching.
Related Business Process BP-05 (Purchase Order Placement), BP-07 (Goods Receipt & Verification)
Related Functional Requirements FR-017 (Enforce PO reference for supplier receipts), FR-013 (Record purchase order commitments)
Rule Category Purchasing

BR-008 — Three-Way Match Before Payment

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Three-Way Match Before Payment
Business Rule Statement Supplier payment must not be authorized until a three-way match is confirmed among the purchase order, goods receipt, and supplier invoice within defined tolerance. Payment for unordered, unreceived, or mispriced goods is prohibited.
Business Reason Payment must be authorized only when the purchase order (what was ordered), goods receipt (what was received), and supplier invoice (what is billed) agree within defined tolerance. This prevents paying for unordered, unreceived, or mispriced goods.
Related Business Process BP-05 (Purchase Order Placement), BP-08 (Receipt Discrepancy Resolution), BP-30 (Inventory Valuation & Financial Reconciliation)
Related Functional Requirements FR-013 (Record purchase order commitments), FR-015 (Receive and verify inbound goods), FR-016 (Document and resolve receipt discrepancies), FR-089 (Support financial inventory reconciliation)
Rule Category Purchasing

Replenishment and Stock Policy

BR-009 — Reorder at Reorder Level

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Reorder at Reorder Level
Business Rule Statement Replenishment action must be triggered at or before the defined reorder level. When available stock reaches the reorder threshold, a replenishment review or purchase action must be initiated the same business day.
Business Reason The reorder level is calculated to allow enough time for replenishment to arrive before stock reaches zero, accounting for lead time and demand during that period. Delaying action past the reorder level guarantees a stockout during lead time.
Related Business Process BP-03 (Stock Policy & Threshold Definition), BP-21 (Low-Stock Alert Review), BP-22 (Replenishment Planning & Requisition)
Related Functional Requirements FR-008 (Define stock policy and replenishment thresholds), FR-051 (Generate low-stock and out-of-stock alerts), FR-052 (Review and acknowledge stock alerts)
Rule Category Inventory

BR-010 — Safety Stock Protection

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Safety Stock Protection
Business Rule Statement Safety stock must not be bypassed without an authorized exception. Safety stock buffers may not be consumed for routine fulfillment or reallocated without documented approval and a replenishment plan.
Business Reason Safety stock is a deliberate buffer protecting against demand and supply uncertainty. Consuming safety stock to fulfill routine orders or reallocating it without replenishment plan removes the organization's protection against the next disruption.
Related Business Process BP-03 (Stock Policy & Threshold Definition), BP-17 (Inventory Reservation), BP-24 (Inter-Location Transfer Request)
Related Functional Requirements FR-056 (Enforce safety stock protection rules), FR-008 (Define stock policy and replenishment thresholds)
Rule Category Inventory

Network Balance

BR-011 — Network Check Before Purchase

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Network Check Before Purchase
Business Rule Statement Network availability must be checked before placing a new purchase order. When a location experiences shortage, excess stock at other locations must be evaluated for transfer before initiating new procurement.
Business Reason A local stockout may be solvable with a transfer from another location that holds excess. Purchasing new stock when the network already owns sufficient quantity wastes capital, increases carrying cost, and worsens network imbalance.
Related Business Process BP-21 (Low-Stock Alert Review), BP-24 (Inter-Location Transfer Request), BP-26 (Network Stock Rebalancing)
Related Functional Requirements FR-028 (Display expected inbound and network-wide availability), FR-053 (Generate replenishment suggestions), FR-058 (Request inter-location stock transfers)
Rule Category Inventory

BR-012 — Protect Source Location Minimum

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Protect Source Location Minimum
Business Rule Statement An inter-location transfer must not deplete the source location below its minimum threshold. Transfer quantity must be limited to stock the source can spare while maintaining its own service level.
Business Reason Sending stock to fix one location's shortage must not create a shortage at the source. Transfers require verification that the sending location can spare the quantity while maintaining its own service level.
Related Business Process BP-24 (Inter-Location Transfer Request), BP-25 (Inter-Location Transfer Execution)
Related Functional Requirements FR-063 (Enforce source location minimum on transfers), FR-058 (Request inter-location stock transfers), FR-060 (Execute and record inter-location transfers)
Rule Category Warehousing

Quality and Rotation

BR-013 — Quarantine Exclusion from Sellable Stock

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Quarantine Exclusion from Sellable Stock
Business Rule Statement Quarantined stock must be excluded from sellable availability. Inventory under quality hold, investigation, or recall must not be included in ATP or committed to customer orders.
Business Reason Quarantined inventory is held pending quality investigation, regulatory clearance, or recall response. Including quarantined stock in sellable availability risks shipping defective, contaminated, or non-compliant products to customers.
Related Business Process BP-14 (Stock Adjustment & Write-Off), BP-20 (Outbound Exception Handling)
Related Functional Requirements FR-038 (Manage quarantine and hold stock status), FR-024 (Display ATP quantity)
Rule Category Inventory

BR-014 — FEFO Rotation for Shelf-Life Products

Attribute Detail
Rule Name FEFO Rotation for Shelf-Life Products
Business Rule Statement First-expired, first-out (FEFO) rotation is required for products with defined shelf life. Fulfillment must prioritize stock with the earliest expiration date.
Business Reason Products with expiration dates must ship in order of earliest expiry first. Shipping newer stock while older stock expires in the warehouse causes write-offs, customer safety issues, and regulatory violations.
Related Business Process BP-09 (Stock Put-Away & Storage), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship)
Related Functional Requirements FR-044 (Support pick, pack, and ship workflow), FR-029 (Record all inventory movements with full history)
Rule Category Products

BR-015 — FIFO Rotation for Standard Goods

Attribute Detail
Rule Name FIFO Rotation for Standard Goods
Business Rule Statement First-in, first-out (FIFO) rotation is required for non-perishable standard goods. Oldest received stock must be picked and shipped before newer stock for the same SKU.
Business Reason Oldest stock should move first to minimize obsolescence, packaging degradation, and model-year expiration. Consistent FIFO prevents aged inventory from sitting indefinitely while new stock cycles normally.
Related Business Process BP-09 (Stock Put-Away & Storage), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship)
Related Functional Requirements FR-044 (Support pick, pack, and ship workflow), FR-029 (Record all inventory movements with full history)
Rule Category Products

BR-016 — Minimum Remaining Shelf Life at Receipt

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Minimum Remaining Shelf Life at Receipt
Business Rule Statement Products with shelf-life requirements must meet minimum remaining shelf life (MRSL) at receipt. Inbound deliveries that do not meet MRSL policy must be rejected or dispositioned before acceptance into sellable inventory.
Business Reason Receiving product too close to expiration guarantees write-off before sale. Minimum remaining shelf life requirements protect the business from accepting stock with insufficient selling window.
Related Business Process BP-07 (Goods Receipt & Verification), BP-08 (Receipt Discrepancy Resolution)
Related Functional Requirements FR-015 (Receive and verify inbound goods), FR-016 (Document and resolve receipt discrepancies)
Rule Category Products

BR-017 — Lot or Batch Capture for Traceable Products

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Lot or Batch Capture for Traceable Products
Business Rule Statement Lot or batch identity must be captured for traceable products at receipt and through all subsequent inventory movements. Traceable products must not be received, transferred, or shipped without lot or batch attribution.
Business Reason Lot capture at every transaction point enables targeted recall, quality investigation, and regulatory compliance. Without lot data, the only option in a defect scenario is a full product-line recall.
Related Business Process BP-07 (Goods Receipt & Verification), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-25 (Inter-Location Transfer Execution)
Related Functional Requirements FR-029 (Record all inventory movements with full history), FR-015 (Receive and verify inbound goods)
Rule Category Products

Inventory Control and Governance

BR-018 — Blind Cycle Counting

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Blind Cycle Counting
Business Rule Statement Cycle counts must be performed blind. Counters must not be shown the system's expected quantity before recording the physical count result.
Business Reason Counters who see the system's expected quantity before counting may consciously or unconsciously match it, defeating the purpose of verification. Blind counting produces unbiased accuracy measurement.
Related Business Process BP-11 (Cycle Counting)
Related Functional Requirements FR-031 (Perform blind cycle counts), FR-030 (Schedule and assign cycle counts)
Rule Category Inventory

BR-019 — Independent Count Approval

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Independent Count Approval
Business Rule Statement The person who performed a count must not approve adjustments arising from their own count. Count variances require review and approval by an independent authorized person.
Business Reason Segregation of duties prevents fraud and undetected error. When the same person counts, investigates, and approves, there is no independent verification of the variance or its cause.
Related Business Process BP-13 (Count Variance Investigation & Approval)
Related Functional Requirements FR-034 (Investigate and approve count adjustments), FR-084 (Enforce segregation of duties)
Rule Category Users

BR-020 — Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes
Business Rule Statement Every inventory adjustment requires a reason code. No stock correction, increase, or decrease may be applied without a categorized business reason.
Business Reason Adjustments without categorized reasons are analytically useless. The business knows quantity changed but not why — preventing shrinkage analysis, trend identification, and targeted corrective action.
Related Business Process BP-14 (Stock Adjustment & Write-Off), BP-15 (Shrinkage & Loss Management)
Related Functional Requirements FR-035 (Process stock adjustments with mandatory reason codes), FR-011 (Maintain standard reason codes)
Rule Category Inventory

BR-021 — Independent Approval for Material Adjustments

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Independent Approval for Material Adjustments
Business Rule Statement Adjustments above the defined financial or quantity threshold require independent approval by an authorized person who did not initiate the underlying transaction.
Business Reason High-value or high-quantity adjustments carry greater financial and fraud risk. Independent approval by an authorized person who did not perform the underlying transaction provides oversight proportional to the impact.
Related Business Process BP-14 (Stock Adjustment & Write-Off), BP-13 (Count Variance Investigation & Approval)
Related Functional Requirements FR-037 (Enforce adjustment approval thresholds), FR-084 (Enforce segregation of duties)
Rule Category Users

BR-022 — Investigate Before Adjusting

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Investigate Before Adjusting
Business Rule Statement Count and inventory variances must be investigated before an adjustment is applied. Adjustments may only be approved after root cause analysis or documented investigation effort.
Business Reason Adjustments fix the record; investigation fixes the process. Applying adjustments without understanding why the variance occurred guarantees the same discrepancy will reappear on the next count.
Related Business Process BP-13 (Count Variance Investigation & Approval)
Related Functional Requirements FR-033 (Identify and report count variances), FR-034 (Investigate and approve count adjustments)
Rule Category Inventory

BR-023 — Documented Write-Off Authorization

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Documented Write-Off Authorization
Business Rule Statement Inventory write-off requires documented evidence and authorization. Write-offs must include supporting documentation and approval by an authorized person before inventory value is removed.
Business Reason Write-offs permanently remove inventory value from the business. Unauthorized or undocumented write-offs enable fraud, inflate remaining inventory inaccurately, and create audit exposure.
Related Business Process BP-14 (Stock Adjustment & Write-Off), BP-15 (Shrinkage & Loss Management)
Related Functional Requirements FR-036 (Process inventory write-offs with authorization), FR-011 (Maintain standard reason codes)
Rule Category Users

BR-024 — Physical Inventory Freeze

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Physical Inventory Freeze
Business Rule Statement A physical inventory freeze applies during a full wall-to-wall count. Receiving, shipping, transfers, and adjustments must be suspended for the counted location until the count is completed and verified.
Business Reason Movements during a full count change the quantity being counted, making the snapshot unreliable. A freeze ensures the counted quantity is stable and auditable.
Related Business Process BP-12 (Full Physical Inventory Count)
Related Functional Requirements FR-032 (Conduct full physical inventory count), FR-033 (Identify and report count variances)
Rule Category Warehousing

BR-032 — Class A Priority Monitoring

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Class A Priority Monitoring
Business Rule Statement Class A products require the highest count frequency and monitoring intensity. Priority SKUs must receive more frequent cycle counts, availability monitoring, and replenishment attention than lower-classification products.
Business Reason Not all products warrant equal operational effort. Class A items drive the majority of revenue and customer impact. Higher count frequency and monitoring intensity on A items prevents stockouts and accuracy failures where they matter most.
Related Business Process BP-04 (ABC Product Classification), BP-11 (Cycle Counting), BP-21 (Low-Stock Alert Review)
Related Functional Requirements FR-009 (Classify products by ABC priority), FR-030 (Schedule and assign cycle counts), FR-051 (Generate low-stock and out-of-stock alerts)
Rule Category Products

Returns and Commercial

BR-025 — Return Authorization Required

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Return Authorization Required
Business Rule Statement Customer returns require authorization before acceptance. Returned goods must not be received at the warehouse without a valid return authorization linked to the original order and return policy.
Business Reason Unauthorized returns cannot be linked to original orders, may violate return policy, and give the warehouse no advance notice. Authorization connects the physical return to the commercial transaction and expected resolution.
Related Business Process BP-27 (Customer Return Intake)
Related Functional Requirements FR-064 (Authorize and record customer returns), FR-067 (Track return processing status)
Rule Category Inventory

BR-026 — Inspect Returns Before Restocking

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Inspect Returns Before Restocking
Business Rule Statement Returned goods must be inspected before restocking. Products may only be returned to sellable inventory after condition assessment confirms they meet resale quality standards.
Business Reason Not all returns are resalable. Used, damaged, or defective products placed back in sellable inventory will be shipped to the next customer as new — generating repeat returns, complaints, and brand damage.
Related Business Process BP-28 (Return-to-Stock or Disposal Decision)
Related Functional Requirements FR-065 (Receive and inspect returned goods), FR-066 (Restock or write off returned inventory)
Rule Category Warehousing

BR-027 — No Reorder of Discontinued Products

Attribute Detail
Rule Name No Reorder of Discontinued Products
Business Rule Statement Discontinued products must not be reordered. Once a product is marked discontinued, new purchase orders and replenishment requisitions for that SKU are prohibited.
Business Reason Discontinued status means the business has decided to exit the product. Reordering discontinued SKUs creates obsolete inventory that must eventually be written off, and conflicts with supersession plans.
Related Business Process BP-01 (Product Master Data Management), BP-22 (Replenishment Planning & Requisition)
Related Functional Requirements FR-002 (Manage product status lifecycle), FR-054 (Create and track purchase requisitions)
Rule Category Products

BR-029 — Promotional Stock Ring-Fencing

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Promotional Stock Ring-Fencing
Business Rule Statement Promotional stock must be ring-fenced during a campaign. Inventory allocated to a promotion or launch must not be consumed by non-promotional orders without commercial leadership approval.
Business Reason Promotional inventory is positioned for a specific campaign period and channel. Allowing non-promotional orders to consume promotional stock defeats the campaign plan and leaves promoted channels without supply.
Related Business Process BP-31 (Promotional & Launch Stock Readiness)
Related Functional Requirements FR-057 (Support promotional stock readiness review), FR-080 (Deliver campaign and launch readiness alerts)
Rule Category Products

Ownership and Trade

BR-030 — Bonded Inventory Customs Clearance

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Bonded Inventory Customs Clearance
Business Rule Statement Bonded inventory must not be released into domestic sellable stock without customs clearance. Duties and regulatory release must be confirmed before bonded goods are made available for sale or fulfillment.
Business Reason Bonded warehouse stock is under customs control. Duties and taxes have not been paid. Releasing bonded goods into domestic commerce without customs authorization is illegal and creates financial and regulatory liability.
Related Business Process BP-07 (Goods Receipt & Verification), BP-09 (Stock Put-Away & Storage)
Related Functional Requirements FR-038 (Manage quarantine and hold stock status), FR-018 (Manage put-away and stock availability timing)
Rule Category Purchasing

BR-031 — Consignment Ownership at Consumption

Attribute Detail
Rule Name Consignment Ownership at Consumption
Business Rule Statement Consignment stock is not owned by the organization until a defined consumption or sale event occurs per supplier agreement. Consignment inventory must not be treated as owned stock for valuation or fulfillment until ownership transfers.
Business Reason Consignment inventory is physically at the buyer's location but owned by the supplier until the buyer consumes, sells, or issues it per agreement. Treating consignment as owned inventory overstates assets and triggers incorrect financial recording.
Related Business Process BP-30 (Inventory Valuation & Financial Reconciliation), BP-07 (Goods Receipt & Verification)
Related Functional Requirements FR-075 (Support inventory valuation summary views), FR-089 (Support financial inventory reconciliation)
Rule Category Purchasing

Interdependent Rule Combinations

The BRD identifies the following rule combinations that must operate together to be effective:

Combination Business Purpose
BR-001 + BR-002 ATP defines what is available; reservation locks it against confirmed commitments
BR-004 + BR-006 Verification confirms what arrived; documentation preserves supplier accountability
BR-018 + BR-019 Blind counting detects variance; independent approval prevents fraud
BR-020 + BR-022 Investigation finds root cause; reason code captures it for analysis
BR-014 + BR-016 FEFO manages rotation; MRSL prevents accepting stock too close to expiry
BR-011 + BR-012 Network check enables transfer; source protection prevents new shortages

Validation Rules Specification

Inventory Management System

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-VR-001
Document Title Validation Rules — Inventory Management System
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Senior Business Analyst
Source Documents BRD-IMS-001, Functional Requirements (FR-001–FR-090), Business Rules (BR-001–BR-032), Acceptance Criteria
Date July 5, 2026
Scope Data validation and business validation only — no implementation, API, or database design

Purpose

This document defines validation rules that must be satisfied when users interact with inventory management capabilities. Each rule is tied to a functional requirement and feature. Rules express what must be validated from a business perspective, not how the system enforces it technically.

Validation Rule Fields

Field Description
Validation ID Unique identifier (VR-001, VR-002, …)
Related Feature Primary feature from Feature Catalog (F-01–F-30)
Related FR Functional requirement identifier
Validation Rule The condition that must be satisfied
Error Condition When validation fails
User Message Plain-language message presented to the user
Business Reason Why the rule exists

Domain 1: Master Data & Governance

FR-001 — Create and Maintain Product Master Records (F-01)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-001 F-01 SKU, product name, and unit of measure are required on every product record. Any required attribute is missing or blank. Required product information is missing. Enter SKU, product name, and unit of measure before saving. Incomplete product records cause ordering, receiving, and fulfillment errors across the network.
VR-002 F-01 SKU must be unique across the product catalog. Submitted SKU already exists on another active or inactive product. This SKU already exists. Use a unique SKU or update the existing product record. Duplicate SKUs fragment stock visibility and undermine a single product identity (BR-001 context).
VR-003 F-01 Only authorized users may create or modify product master records. User lacks product maintenance authority. You are not authorized to create or change product records. Product master data quality requires controlled ownership by the Inventory Controller function.

FR-002 — Manage Product Status Lifecycle (F-01)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-004 F-01 Discontinued products must not be eligible for new replenishment or purchase. User attempts to reorder or replenish a discontinued product. This product is discontinued and cannot be reordered. Prevents obsolete inventory accumulation and conflicting assortment decisions (BR-027).
VR-005 F-01 Product status changes must record prior status, new status, user, and date. Status change submitted without auditable attribution. Product status could not be saved. A valid status and authorization are required. Status history supports lifecycle accountability and audit review.
VR-006 F-01 Inactive or discontinued products must be blocked from new reservations unless policy explicitly permits. Reservation or fulfillment attempted on non-active product without exception. This product is not active and cannot be committed to new orders. Prevents customer commitments against products the business has withdrawn from sale.

FR-003 — Support Product Identifier Lookup (F-01)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-007 F-01 Lookup by SKU, barcode, or assigned identifier must match an existing product record. Identifier does not match any product. No product found for this identifier. Verify the SKU or barcode and try again. Prevents implicit creation of products during operational transactions.
VR-008 F-01 Stock context shown during lookup must respect the user's authorized location scope. User requests stock detail for an unauthorized location. You do not have access to inventory at this location. Aligns visibility with operational accountability and location ownership.

FR-004 — Detect and Resolve Duplicate Product Records (F-01)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-009 F-01 New product submissions must be checked for matching or conflicting SKU, barcode, or highly similar name. Potential duplicate detected and user proceeds without resolution. A similar product already exists. Review the existing record before creating a new product. Prevents parallel identities for the same physical product (PP-07).
VR-010 F-01 Merging duplicate products requires Inventory Controller authorization when both records have on-hand stock. Unauthorized merge attempted on stocked products. Product merge requires Inventory Controller approval when stock exists on both records. Protects stock integrity during catalog consolidation.

FR-005 — Configure and Maintain Inventory Locations (F-02)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-011 F-02 Location name, type, and operational status are required. Required location attributes missing. Required location information is missing. Enter name, type, and status before saving. Locations are the foundation for all stock assignment and reporting.
VR-012 F-02 Deactivated locations must not accept new receipts, reservations, or fulfillments except authorized disposition activity. Transaction attempted at deactivated location. This location is not active for new inventory activity. Prevents stock and transactions at locations that are closed or not yet ready.
VR-013 F-02 Location activation for transactions requires approved opening balance when go-live policy applies. Operational transaction at location without approved opening balance. This location cannot process transactions until opening stock is verified and approved. Go-live with unverified balances embeds errors that undermine trust (BA-16).

FR-006 — Manage Location Hierarchy (F-02)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-014 F-02 A location cannot be assigned as its own parent or ancestor. Circular hierarchy proposed. Invalid hierarchy: a location cannot be placed under itself or its own child. Circular hierarchies break network roll-up and reporting.
VR-015 F-02 Each location may have only one parent in the hierarchy at a time. Multiple conflicting parent assignments. This location already belongs to another hierarchy branch. Resolve the assignment before saving. Ensures unambiguous network structure for accountability and reporting.

FR-007 — Plan Location Closure and Stock Disposition (F-02)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-016 F-02 Location closure must be blocked while on-hand stock remains unless a disposition plan is documented or explicitly waived by an authorized approver. Closure attempted with remaining stock and no plan. This location still holds inventory. Complete stock disposition or obtain closure approval before deactivating. Prevents stranded inventory and orphaned records when locations exit the network.
VR-017 F-02 New inbound and fulfillment activity must be blocked at a location in closure status except authorized disposition transactions. Standard operational transaction at closing location. This location is closing. Only authorized disposition activities are permitted. Protects closure integrity while stock is being cleared.

FR-008 — Define Stock Policy and Replenishment Thresholds (F-03)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-018 F-03 Reorder level, minimum threshold, and safety stock must be zero or positive numeric values. Negative or non-numeric threshold entered. Threshold values must be zero or greater. Enter valid numbers for all thresholds. Invalid thresholds produce false alerts or missed replenishment signals.
VR-019 F-03 Minimum threshold must not exceed reorder level unless business policy explicitly allows inverted configuration. Illogical threshold combination submitted. Minimum threshold cannot be higher than reorder level. Adjust values to match stock policy. Illogical thresholds cause incorrect low-stock detection and replenishment timing (BR-009).
VR-020 F-03 Threshold changes must include an effective date and retain prior values in history. Threshold saved without effective date or history loss. Stock policy could not be saved. An effective date is required for threshold changes. Historical thresholds explain past alert behavior and support audit review.

FR-009 — Classify Products by ABC Priority (F-03)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-021 F-03 ABC classification must be one of: A, B, or C. Invalid classification value submitted. Invalid product class. Select A, B, or C. Standard classification enables consistent operational prioritization (BR-032).
VR-022 F-03 Classification may only be assigned to active or inactive products, not to invalid or unknown product references. Classification applied to non-existent product. Product not found. Classification can only be applied to valid product records. Ensures classification drives count and alert rules for real catalog items.

FR-010 — Establish Opening Stock Balance at Location Go-Live (F-02)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-023 F-02 Opening balance quantities must be non-negative numbers for each counted SKU. Negative or non-numeric opening quantity entered. Opening quantity must be zero or greater. Correct invalid count entries before submitting. Negative opening balances corrupt inventory from go-live.
VR-024 F-02 Every opening balance SKU must exist in the product catalog before location activation. Opening balance references unknown SKU. Unknown product in opening balance. Resolve catalog gaps before activating this location. Opening balances must tie to a single trusted product identity.
VR-025 F-02 Location activation requires authorized approval of the complete opening balance package. Activation attempted before approver sign-off. Opening balance must be approved before this location can go live. Verified baselines are required for credible inventory control at cutover.

FR-011 — Maintain Standard Reason Codes (F-17)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-026 F-17 Adjustments, write-offs, and receipt discrepancies require selection of an active reason code before submission. Transaction submitted without reason code. A reason code is required. Select the reason for this inventory change. Uncategorized adjustments prevent shrinkage analysis and audit substantiation (BR-020).
VR-027 F-17 Retired reason codes must not be selectable for new transactions. Retired code used on new transaction. This reason code is no longer active. Select a current reason code. Retired codes remain on history only; active list reflects current policy.

FR-012 — Manage Inventory Governance Policies (F-03)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-028 F-03 Only one governance policy version may be effective for a given parameter at any point in time. Overlapping effective policy versions detected. Conflicting policy versions exist. Publish a single effective policy before proceeding. Ambiguous policy causes inconsistent approvals and control failures.
VR-029 F-03 Policy parameters referenced by workflows must be defined before dependent transactions are processed. Transaction evaluated against undefined policy value. Required business policy is not configured. Contact operations leadership to define policy values. Prevents silent defaults on financially material decisions.

Domain 2: Inbound & Receiving

FR-013 — Record Purchase Order Commitments (F-07)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-030 F-07 Purchase order must include product, ordered quantity, supplier reference, receiving location, and expected delivery date. Required PO field missing. Required purchase order information is missing. Complete all mandatory fields before saving. Incomplete POs cannot support receiving verification or inbound visibility.
VR-031 F-07 PO lines must reference active products and active receiving locations. Discontinued product or deactivated location on PO line. This product or location is not valid for ordering. Select an active product and receiving location. Prevents procurement against invalid catalog or network entities.
VR-032 F-07 Ordered quantity must be greater than zero. Zero or negative PO quantity. Order quantity must be greater than zero. Zero-quantity orders add no inbound supply value and corrupt replenishment planning.

FR-014 — Plan and Communicate Expected Inbound Deliveries (F-07)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-033 F-07 Expected delivery date must be a valid calendar date not in the distant past for new schedules. Invalid or unreasonably past delivery date entered. Enter a valid expected delivery date. Invalid dates undermine receiving preparation and availability projections.
VR-034 F-07 Inbound schedule views must be limited to locations the user is authorized to access. User views unauthorized location schedule. You do not have access to inbound schedules for this location. Protects location-scoped operational data.

FR-015 — Receive and Verify Inbound Goods (F-05)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-035 F-05 Accepted receipt quantity must be greater than zero and must not exceed physically verified quantity. Zero, negative, or unsubstantiated accepted quantity. Enter a valid accepted quantity greater than zero. Recording unverified quantities creates phantom inventory (BR-004).
VR-036 F-05 Received product must match the PO line product identity. Product on receipt does not match PO line. Product received does not match the purchase order. Correct the product or document a discrepancy. Wrong-item receipt corrupts inventory and supplier accountability.
VR-037 F-05 Only verified accepted quantity may increase on-hand balance; rejected or damaged quantity must be recorded separately. Full PO quantity accepted when portion is damaged or rejected. Record accepted and rejected quantities separately. Only accepted stock may enter inventory. Separates sellable stock from disputed or unsellable goods (BR-006).

FR-016 — Document and Resolve Receipt Discrepancies (F-05)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-038 F-05 Open discrepancies must be documented with type, variance quantity, and notes before disputed quantity is finalized. Discrepancy closed without required documentation. Document the discrepancy type and quantity before resolving this receipt. Undocumented discrepancies waive supplier accountability (BR-006).
VR-039 F-05 Disputed quantity must remain excluded from sellable availability until resolution is approved. Disputed stock made available before resolution. Disputed quantity cannot be made available until the discrepancy is resolved. Prevents fulfillment from stock that is not confirmed received.

FR-017 — Enforce Purchase Order Reference for Supplier Receipts (F-05)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-040 F-05 Standard supplier receipts require a valid open purchase order reference. Receipt attempted without PO or valid ad-hoc exception. A valid purchase order is required to receive this shipment. Obtain PO confirmation or authorized ad-hoc approval. Maintains procurement control and supports financial matching (BR-007).
VR-041 F-05 Receipt against a PO line must not exceed remaining open quantity plus approved tolerance. Receipt quantity exceeds allowable open PO quantity. Received quantity exceeds the remaining purchase order quantity. Adjust quantity or obtain over-receipt approval. Prevents silent over-receipt that affects payment and inventory accuracy.
VR-042 F-05 Ad-hoc receipts require documented approver and business reason. Ad-hoc receipt without authorization. Emergency receipt requires authorized approval and a documented reason. Authorized exceptions only; unaudited receipts break financial controls.

FR-018 — Manage Put-Away and Stock Availability Timing (F-06)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-043 F-06 Put-away quantity must not exceed received quantity still in receiving status. Put-away total exceeds received quantity. Put-away quantity cannot exceed the quantity received. Verify counts before confirming put-away. Prevents availability inflation beyond physically received stock (BR-005).
VR-044 F-06 ATP must not increase until put-away is confirmed for the corresponding quantity. Availability updated before put-away confirmation. Stock is not yet available. Complete put-away before this quantity can be promised or picked. Stock in the receiving area is not operationally locatable (BR-005).

FR-019 — Receive Return and Non-PO Inbound Stock (F-05)

Validation ID Related Feature Validation Rule Error Condition User Message Business Reason
VR-045 F-05 Customer return receipts require a valid return authorization reference. Return received without valid authorization. A valid return authorization is required to accept this return. Links physical returns to commercial transactions (BR-025).
VR-046 F-05 Return receipt quantity must not exceed authorized return quantity. Received return quantity exceeds authorization. Received quantity exceeds the authorized return amount. Verify the return authorization. Prevents acceptance of unauthorized or excess returns.
VR-047 F-05 Sellable ATP must not increase from return receipt until inspection passes when inspection is required. Restock to available before inspection completion. Returned goods must pass inspection before being added to sellable stock. Protects customers from receiving used or damaged goods as new (BR-026).

Document ID: SRS-VR-001 | Version 1.0 | July 5, 2026

Business Constraints Specification

Inventory Management System

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-BC-001
Document Title Business Constraints — Inventory Management System
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Senior Business Analyst
Source Documents BRD-IMS-001 (Section 18), Business Constraints Discovery Artifact
Date July 5, 2026
Scope Business and operational constraints only — not technical architecture, infrastructure, or implementation design

Purpose

This document identifies the 38 business constraints that bound how the Inventory Management System initiative may be delivered and operated. Constraints are fixed business conditions — not optional preferences. Each constraint is expressed in operational terms: what the organization can and cannot do while running inventory management as a business capability.

Constraint Categories

Prefix Category Count
BC Budget 6
TC Time 6
LC Legal 5
OC Operational 8
ORC Organizational 7
TEC Technology — Business Level 6

Severity Classification

Severity Constraints
Blocking BC-01, TC-02, OC-01, ORC-07
High BC-02, BC-05, TC-01, TC-03, TC-04, ORC-01, ORC-03, ORC-05, TEC-01, TEC-04
Medium BC-03, BC-04, BC-06, TC-05, TC-06, LC-01, LC-02, LC-03, OC-02, OC-04, OC-07, OC-08, ORC-02, ORC-04, ORC-06, TEC-02, TEC-05, TEC-06
Low LC-04, LC-05, OC-03, OC-05, OC-06

1. Budget Constraints

BC-01: Fixed Total Initiative Budget

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID BC-01
Description The IMS initiative must be delivered within a fixed total budget approved by executive leadership, covering software, services, training, change management, and first-year operational support. No additional funding is guaranteed if overruns occur.
Business Justification Inventory improvement must demonstrate return within approved capital and operating investment limits. Executive leadership has committed a defined envelope tied to business case ROI — not an open-ended transformation program.
Affected Business Processes All processes (BP-01 – BP-32); particularly BP-29 (Performance Reporting), BP-31 (Promotional Readiness), and Phase 2/3 processes deferred by scope prioritization
Consequences if Violated Scope reduction or project pause; P1 objectives (BO-01, BO-03, BO-19) at risk; Phase 2/3 capabilities (replenishment automation, financial alignment, network rebalancing) indefinitely deferred; stakeholder trust in program governance erodes

BC-02: No Additional Warehouse Headcount Budget

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID BC-02
Description The business case does not include budget for additional warehouse or inventory control headcount in the first 12 months. Efficiency must come from improved processes and system support, not new hires.
Business Justification The initiative is funded as a productivity and control investment, not a staffing expansion. Leadership expects existing teams to operate more effectively with better visibility and standardized workflows.
Affected Business Processes BP-07 (Goods Receipt), BP-09 (Put-Away), BP-11 (Cycle Counting), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-21 (Low-Stock Alert Review), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation)
Consequences if Violated Unfunded headcount creates budget overrun (BC-01 conflict); existing staff overwhelmed during rollout; adoption fails (BO-21); manual parallel tools persist (BO-22); accuracy and movement recording objectives (BO-02, BO-03) not sustained

BC-03: Capital Expenditure vs. Operating Expenditure Limits

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID BC-03
Description Finance has defined separate caps for capital expenditure (licenses, implementation) and operating expenditure (subscriptions, support, training). Spending cannot be reclassified between categories without CFO approval.
Business Justification Corporate financial policy requires predictable classification of investment versus recurring cost for balance-sheet and budget planning. IMS spending must fit established fiscal governance.
Affected Business Processes BP-05 (Purchase Order Placement), BP-22 (Replenishment Planning), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation) — indirect; primarily affects procurement timing of delivery activities
Consequences if Violated Delivery delayed to next fiscal period; training or go-live support deferred; misaligned spend blocks vendor payment; project timeline slips against TC-02 and TC-05 milestones

BC-04: Training and Change Management Budget Ceiling

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID BC-04
Description A fixed budget is allocated for training, communications, and change management. This budget cannot be reallocated from development or licensing budgets.
Business Justification Change investment is necessary but bounded. Leadership requires demonstrable efficiency in rollout — scalable training models rather than unlimited per-location bespoke programs.
Affected Business Processes All operational processes at rollout; especially BP-07, BP-11, BP-14, BP-18, BP-24 where floor adoption is critical
Consequences if Violated Incomplete role training; location managers reject standardized processes (BO-03); user adoption below 90% (BO-21); parallel spreadsheets and paper logs continue (BO-22); rework and support costs increase without budget to absorb them

BC-05: No Budget for External System Replacement

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID BC-05
Description The IMS budget does not fund replacement of finance, sales, HR, or ERP systems. IMS must operate within the current enterprise application landscape.
Business Justification IMS addresses inventory control as a targeted capability gap — not a full enterprise platform replacement. Finance, sales, and HR systems remain authoritative in their domains.
Affected Business Processes BP-05 (Purchase Order Placement), BP-16 (Order Availability), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation), BP-31 (Promotional Readiness)
Consequences if Violated Scope creep into ERP/CRM territory; stakeholder resistance from system owners; delivery failure on inventory-specific objectives; duplicated master data across systems; BO-18 and BO-20 remain unachievable without agreed interim reconciliation

BC-06: Ongoing Operational Cost Limit

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID BC-06
Description Annual recurring cost for licenses, support, and maintenance after go-live must remain within a CFO-approved operating budget threshold, typically capped relative to current inventory carrying cost.
Business Justification Sustainable inventory management must not impose recurring cost that exceeds the economic value of improved control. Ongoing spend must be defensible against working-capital and carrying-cost benefits.
Affected Business Processes BP-02 (Location Setup) — future location onboarding; BP-29 (Performance Reporting) — executive visibility scope
Consequences if Violated New locations cannot be onboarded without separate approval; feature tiers or user counts restricted; network-wide rollout (TC-03) stalls; long-term scalability of BO-01 and BO-14 constrained

2. Time Constraints

TC-01: 18-Month Business Vision Horizon

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TC-01
Description All SMART business objectives and phased outcomes must be achievable within 18 months of project initiation, aligned with the short-term business vision.
Business Justification Leadership committed to measurable inventory improvement within a defined planning horizon. Beyond 18 months, priorities may shift and funding is not assured.
Affected Business Processes All processes; Phase 3 processes especially BP-26 (Network Rebalancing), BP-29 (KPI Reporting), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation), BP-31 (Promotional Readiness)
Consequences if Violated Objectives BO-09, BO-10, BO-18, BO-20, BO-23, BO-24 measured as failed despite incomplete delivery; steering committee loses confidence; initiative descoped or restarted

TC-02: MVP Delivery Within 6 Months

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TC-02
Description Minimum Viable Product must be live at the first primary location within 6 months of project kickoff to meet Phase 1 vision and P1 SMART objectives.
Business Justification Early credible control is the strategic intent of Phase 1. Delayed go-live prolongs stockouts, inaccurate records, and fulfillment failures that the initiative was created to resolve.
Affected Business Processes BP-01 – BP-18, BP-24 – BP-25, BP-29 (core reports), BP-32 (audit trail) — MVP process set
Consequences if Violated P1 objectives missed: trusted view (BO-01), movement recording (BO-03), audit trail (BO-19), sales self-service (BO-16), adoption (BO-21), manual tool retirement (BO-22); executive sponsorship weakens; business continues absorbing current-state losses

TC-03: Sequential Location Rollout Window

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TC-03
Description Primary locations must be onboarded sequentially over approximately 6 months following first go-live, with a minimum 4-week gap between deployments — not simultaneous network-wide cutover.
Business Justification Support capacity, change absorption, and lessons-learned application require controlled rollout. Simultaneous deployment would overwhelm operations and SMEs (ORC-01).
Affected Business Processes BP-02 (Location Setup), BP-10 (Status Monitoring), BP-24 – BP-26 (Network Balance), BP-29 (Reporting)
Consequences if Violated Inconsistent processes across locations persist (BO-03); network visibility incomplete until ~month 12 (BO-01); cross-location imbalance correction delayed (BO-14); hypercare support fails; accuracy and adoption vary by site

TC-04: Peak Season Blackout Periods

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TC-04
Description Go-live, major upgrades, and intensive training cannot occur during defined peak business periods (e.g., holiday season, fiscal year-end, major promotional events) at each location.
Business Justification Peak periods generate disproportionate revenue and customer commitments. Operational disruption during peak directly damages fill rate, on-time delivery, and brand reputation.
Affected Business Processes BP-16 – BP-19 (Order Fulfillment), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-31 (Promotional Readiness), BP-07 (Receiving)
Consequences if Violated Fill rate and on-time delivery drop (BO-05, BO-15); stock-related cancellations increase (BO-08); customer complaints and revenue at risk; rollout calendar slips 3–6 months; staff cannot complete training before peak

TC-05: SMART Objective Measurement Deadlines

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TC-05
Description Business objectives have fixed measurement milestones at months 3, 6, 9, 12, and 18 post-initiation. Enabling capabilities must be live before their measurement window opens.
Business Justification Accountability to the business case requires time-bound outcomes. Objectives without aligned delivery dates cannot be governed or rewarded.
Affected Business Processes Process-to-objective mapping: BP-10/16 (BO-01, BO-16); BP-11/13 (BO-02); BP-07/18/25 (BO-03); BP-18/19 (BO-05, BO-08); BP-21/22 (BO-07, BO-13); BP-30 (BO-18, BO-20)
Consequences if Violated False "red" KPI status when capability not yet delivered; premature descoping of objectives; steering committee makes decisions on misleading data; team morale and sponsor confidence decline

TC-06: Baseline Measurement Lead Time

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TC-06
Description Pre-implementation baseline data for SMART objectives must be collected 30–60 days before first go-live, consuming part of the overall project timeline.
Business Justification Improvement claims require credible before-and-after comparison. Without baseline, ROI and objective achievement cannot be substantiated to leadership or auditors.
Affected Business Processes BP-29 (Performance Reporting), BP-11/12/13 (Accuracy), BP-18/19 (Fulfillment), BP-15 (Shrinkage)
Consequences if Violated BO-04, BO-06, BO-07, BO-09, BO-11 targets unprovable; steering committee cannot validate success; external audit challenges benefit claims; late baseline compresses build and test window (conflicts with TC-02)

3. Legal Constraints

LC-01: Data Protection and Privacy Regulations

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID LC-01
Description The business must comply with applicable data protection laws (e.g., GDPR, local privacy regulations) for personal data in user accounts, audit logs, and customer-linked order and return records.
Business Justification Legal obligation to protect employee and customer personal data. Non-compliance exposes the organization to regulatory penalties, legal action, and reputational harm.
Affected Business Processes BP-16 – BP-19 (customer-linked fulfillment), BP-27 – BP-28 (Returns), BP-32 (Audit & Control Review)
Consequences if Violated Regulatory fines and enforcement actions; required data deletion or access restrictions disrupt audit trail (BO-19); customer data breaches damage trust; legal hold on system use pending remediation

LC-02: Financial Record Retention Requirements

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID LC-02
Description Inventory transaction records, adjustment logs, valuation substantiation, and audit evidence must be retained for the minimum period required by tax and corporate law — typically 5–7 years.
Business Justification Statutory and audit requirements mandate preservation of financial and inventory substantiation records. Early destruction invalidates audit defense and tax compliance.
Affected Business Processes BP-14 (Adjustments & Write-Offs), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation), BP-32 (Audit & Control Review), BP-07 (Goods Receipt), BP-25 (Transfer Execution)
Consequences if Violated Audit findings and qualified opinions; inability to defend inventory valuations in tax review; regulatory penalties; BO-19 (audit trail) and BO-18 (valuation alignment) fail at external audit

LC-03: Employment and Labor Law

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID LC-03
Description Changes to work procedures, performance measurement, and mandatory transaction recording introduced by IMS must comply with employment contracts, collective bargaining agreements, and labor regulations.
Business Justification Workforce practices are legally governed. Unilateral imposition of new performance or recording requirements without proper consultation creates labor relations and legal risk.
Affected Business Processes BP-07, BP-09, BP-11, BP-18 (floor work procedures); BP-32 (accountability policies)
Consequences if Violated Union grievances or work stoppages at affected locations; rollback of mandatory recording policies (BO-03, BO-22 fail); go-live delay at unionized sites; HR and legal remediation costs

LC-04: Supplier and Commercial Contract Terms

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID LC-04
Description Purchase order formats, delivery documentation, and receipt dispute processes must remain compatible with existing supplier contracts. Suppliers cannot be required to adopt new processes without contract amendment.
Business Justification Supplier relationships are contractually bound. Receiving and procurement workflows must work with current commercial terms — the IMS initiative does not renegotiate the supplier base.
Affected Business Processes BP-05 (Purchase Order Placement), BP-07 (Goods Receipt), BP-08 (Receipt Discrepancy Resolution)
Consequences if Violated Supplier refusal to deliver or document shipments; receipt disputes unresolvable; inbound supply disruption; emergency procurement increases (BO-12); BR-006 and BR-007 controls weakened

LC-05: Consumer Protection and Trade Regulations

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID LC-05
Description Customer-facing availability and delivery commitments based on IMS data must comply with consumer protection laws on accurate product representation, cancellation rights, and delivery obligations.
Business Justification B2B and B2C customers have legal protections against misleading availability and unfair commercial practices. ATP-based commitments must be defensible.
Affected Business Processes BP-16 (Order Availability Confirmation), BP-19 (Partial Fulfillment & Backorder), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship)
Consequences if Violated Customer complaints to regulators; chargebacks and compensation claims; contractual penalties with B2B customers; reputational damage; BO-08 (cancellations) and BO-15 (on-time delivery) worsen

4. Operational Constraints

OC-01: No Operational Shutdown for Go-Live

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID OC-01
Description Warehouses and stores must continue receiving, fulfilling, and shipping orders during and after go-live. No full operational shutdown is permitted for system transition.
Business Justification Customer commitments and revenue depend on continuous fulfillment. A shutdown-based cutover is commercially unacceptable for a distribution and retail operator.
Affected Business Processes BP-07 (Receiving), BP-17 – BP-18 (Reservation & Fulfillment), BP-24 – BP-25 (Transfers), BP-10 (Status Monitoring)
Consequences if Violated Lost sales and customer cancellations; carrier and supplier penalties; emergency manual fulfillment at higher cost; opening balance errors from rushed cutover (BO-02); rollback required with extended dual-system operation

OC-02: Daily Fulfillment Service Levels Must Be Maintained

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID OC-02
Description Agreed customer fulfillment service levels (fill rate, dispatch timeliness) must not materially degrade during implementation and rollout.
Business Justification Customer contracts and brand promise depend on reliable fulfillment. The IMS program must improve control without becoming a cause of service failure.
Affected Business Processes BP-16 – BP-20 (Order Fulfillment), BP-17 (Reservation), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship)
Consequences if Violated BO-05 (fill rate), BO-06 (cycle time), BO-15 (on-time delivery) regress; NPS on fulfillment drops (KPI-27); B2B penalties; steering committee halts rollout; revert to manual processes

OC-03: Physical Warehouse Layout and Storage Are Fixed

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID OC-03
Description Warehouse layouts, racking, and storage zones will not be restructured as part of the IMS initiative. Physical infrastructure remains as-is.
Business Justification Facility investment is outside IMS funding and timeline. Accuracy and efficiency gains must come from process discipline and visibility, not capital warehouse redesign.
Affected Business Processes BP-09 (Put-Away), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-11 (Cycle Counting)
Consequences if Violated Unfunded facility projects distract from IMS; bin-level optimization deferred; pick path inefficiency persists; accuracy improvements slower than planned (BO-02) if layout is root cause

OC-04: Existing Product Portfolio and SKU Count

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID OC-04
Description IMS must accommodate the current active product catalog and projected SKU growth over 18 months without requiring product range reduction.
Business Justification Commercial strategy continues to expand assortment and channels. Inventory control must scale with the business — not force assortment rationalization as a prerequisite.
Affected Business Processes BP-01 (Product Master), BP-03 (Stock Policy), BP-04 (ABC Classification), BP-10 (Status Monitoring)
Consequences if Violated Forced SKU reduction damages sales; catalog cutover errors; threshold and alert programs unmanageable; BO-07 (priority stockouts) on excluded products; data migration failure at go-live

OC-05: Current Supplier and Carrier Relationships

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID OC-05
Description Inbound and outbound logistics continue through existing approved suppliers and carriers. The IMS project does not include supplier renegotiation or carrier replacement.
Business Justification Supply chain partnerships are long-term commercial relationships. Receiving and shipping workflows must align with current partner capabilities and lead times.
Affected Business Processes BP-05 – BP-09 (Inbound), BP-18 (Shipment Handoff), BP-23 (Inbound Supply Tracking)
Consequences if Violated Unplanned partner changes disrupt supply; receiving documentation mismatch; inbound delays invalidate replenishment thresholds (BO-13); carrier tracking gaps persist

OC-06: Returns Volume Within Manual Handling Capacity

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID OC-06
Description Customer returns volume is expected to remain processable through basic return workflows without a dedicated returns operation for the first 12 months. If volume exceeds ~5% of outbound, scope review is required.
Business Justification Returns handling capacity is sized for current business volume. Full reverse-logistics maturity is Phase 2 — not day-one operational capacity.
Affected Business Processes BP-27 (Customer Return Intake), BP-28 (Return-to-Stock or Disposal)
Consequences if Violated Returns backlog; incorrect restock or write-off; customer refund delays; warehouse floor congestion; BO-11 (shrinkage) worsens from mishandled returns; scope exception and unfunded work required

OC-07: Cycle Counting Without Operational Disruption

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID OC-07
Description Physical inventory verification required for accuracy objectives must be performed without shutting down receiving, picking, or shipping at any location.
Business Justification Continuous operations are non-negotiable (OC-01, OC-02). Accuracy programs must use rolling cycle counts — not full shutdowns — except scheduled full counts planned outside peak.
Affected Business Processes BP-11 (Cycle Counting), BP-12 (Full Physical Count), BP-13 (Variance Investigation)
Consequences if Violated Forced shutdown conflicts with OC-01; accuracy targets delayed (BO-02); count variances increase from concurrent movements; local managers refuse count program (ORC-05); audit substantiation weak

OC-08: Multi-Location Network with Existing Transfer Practices

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID OC-08
Description Inter-location transfers follow existing approval practices and freight arrangements. The project does not introduce new logistics infrastructure or transfer service level agreements.
Business Justification Network redistribution depends on current freight capacity and approval culture. IMS standardizes recording — not physical logistics network redesign.
Affected Business Processes BP-24 (Transfer Request), BP-25 (Transfer Execution), BP-26 (Network Rebalancing)
Consequences if Violated Unfunded logistics investment expected; transfer SLAs assumed but not met; BO-14 (imbalance reduction) delayed; emergency transfers continue outside system; source locations stockout from uncontrolled transfers (BR-012 risk)

5. Organizational Constraints

ORC-01: No Dedicated Full-Time Project Team

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID ORC-01
Description The project relies on part-time contribution from business SMEs (~20% allocation). No dedicated full-time business operations lead is assigned exclusively to the initiative.
Business Justification Operational leaders must continue running daily business. The organization cannot spare full-time inventory SMEs without compromising fulfillment and replenishment.
Affected Business Processes All processes requiring SME definition: BP-01, BP-03, BP-07, BP-11, BP-14, BP-21, BP-32
Consequences if Violated Slow decisions delay TC-02; UAT incomplete; policies undefined at go-live; floor users adopt workarounds; requirements errors discovered post-go-live; accuracy and adoption objectives fail

ORC-02: Single Product Owner Authority

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID ORC-02
Description Product prioritization is centralized under one Product Owner with steering committee oversight. Department heads cannot unilaterally add scope for their function.
Business Justification Twenty-nine stakeholder groups create conflicting demands. Central prioritization protects MVP delivery and budget (BC-01) against local optimization.
Affected Business Processes Scope affects all processes; escalations common for BP-05, BP-31, BP-26, BP-30 when deferred
Consequences if Violated Scope creep breaches BC-01; MVP date missed (TC-02); fragmented product with inconsistent workflows (BO-03); steering committee loses governance confidence

ORC-03: Change Resistance in Warehouse Culture

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID ORC-03
Description Warehouse teams rely on informal practices — spreadsheets, paper logs, tribal knowledge — and history shows resistance to mandated system use without management enforcement.
Business Justification Cultural inertia is a known organizational reality, not a failure of intent. Adoption requires enforcement policy, not only training and tooling.
Affected Business Processes BP-07, BP-09, BP-11, BP-14, BP-18, BP-25 — all floor-recording processes
Consequences if Violated Dual systems persist (BO-22 fails); movement recording below 98% (BO-03); accuracy stays at ~78% (BO-02); audit trail incomplete (BO-19); pilot failure poisons network rollout (TC-03)

ORC-04: Limited Internal IT Business Support Capacity

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID ORC-04
Description Internal technology support has limited capacity for business process design support, bulk user provisioning, and post-go-live business hypercare. Primary IT focus remains existing enterprise systems.
Business Justification IT resources are committed to maintaining current finance, sales, and infrastructure systems. IMS operational support must be business-led at go-live.
Affected Business Processes BP-32 (user access and audit); rollout of all transactional processes
Consequences if Violated User provisioning delays location go-live; access errors block floor operations; post-go-live issues unresolved; business hypercare unfunded; adoption stalls (BO-21)

ORC-05: Decentralized Location Management Structure

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID ORC-05
Description Each warehouse and store is managed locally with operational autonomy. Central mandates require regional or executive endorsement for enforcement.
Business Justification The operating model delegates day-to-day accountability to site managers. Network standardization is a cultural and governance challenge — not automatic with system deployment.
Affected Business Processes BP-02 (Location Setup), BP-03 (Stock Policy), BP-11 (Cycle Counting), BP-24 (Transfers), BP-29 (Location Performance)
Consequences if Violated Location-to-location process variation continues (BO-03); network KPIs not comparable; some sites never adopt; BO-14 (imbalance) uncorrected; executive dashboard misleading (BO-01)

ORC-06: Finance and Operations Reporting Alignment Gap

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID ORC-06
Description Finance and operations use different data sources and reconciliation practices for inventory. No established single reconciliation process exists between operational and financial records.
Business Justification Historical organizational silos separated operational stock records from general ledger inventory. IMS alone cannot create alignment — cross-department process must be designed.
Affected Business Processes BP-14 (Adjustments & Write-Offs), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation), BP-29 (Reporting)
Consequences if Violated BO-18 (valuation variance ≤2%) unachievable; month-end close remains 7+ days (BO-20); finance distrusts operational data; manual reconciliation continues (BO-04 fails); audit findings on inventory substantiation

ORC-07: No Formal Inventory Management Function Today

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID ORC-07
Description The business lacks a mature, centralized inventory management function with defined policies, KPIs, and single-point accountability. Control is distributed across warehouse, purchasing, and finance.
Business Justification Growth outpaced governance design. The initiative assumes creation of Inventory Controller accountability — a structural gap that must be closed for sustained control.
Affected Business Processes BP-01, BP-03, BP-04, BP-11, BP-13, BP-15, BP-21, BP-32 — all governance-heavy processes
Consequences if Violated Policies unwritten and unenforced; no owner for accuracy program (BO-02); replenishment remains reactive (BO-13); shrinkage unanalyzed (BO-11); project delivers software without organizational capability; chronic inaccuracy persists

6. Technology Constraints — Business Level

Expressed as business operating boundaries, not technical implementation limits.

TEC-01: Must Coexist With Existing Enterprise Systems

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TEC-01
Description IMS operates alongside existing finance, sales, and HR systems without replacing them. Users continue working across multiple systems daily.
Business Justification Enterprise systems remain authoritative in their domains per BC-05. IMS is the inventory system of record — not the enterprise platform of record.
Affected Business Processes BP-05 (PO with finance), BP-16 (orders from sales systems), BP-30 (valuation to finance), BP-27 (returns with CS systems)
Consequences if Violated Stakeholder conflict and duplicate data entry; users revert to legacy tools; BO-16 limited to IMS-native workflows; finance alignment delayed (BO-18); initiative perceived as failed ERP attempt

TEC-02: No Budget for Dedicated Warehouse Hardware

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TEC-02
Description The business will not purchase dedicated warehouse hardware (rugged scanners, handhelds, label printers) as part of IMS. Users access the system via existing company computers and devices.
Business Justification Hardware investment is a separate capital decision. IMS rollout must be achievable with assets already deployed at sites.
Affected Business Processes BP-07 (Receiving), BP-11 (Cycle Counting), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship)
Consequences if Violated Unbudgeted capex request (BC-03 conflict); floor process slower than planned (BO-06); barcode benefits limited; users skip scanning steps; receipt and pick errors persist (BO-02, BO-05)

TEC-03: Standard Web Browser Access Required

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TEC-03
Description All users must access IMS through a standard web browser on company-approved devices without installing specialized desktop applications.
Business Justification Corporate IT standardizes on browser-based applications for supportability and security. Proprietary client software is not approved for this initiative.
Affected Business Processes All user-facing processes; floor operations at BP-07, BP-11, BP-18 most affected
Consequences if Violated IT blocks deployment; locations without reliable connectivity cannot operate (floor downtime); adoption limited to office roles; warehouse recording compliance drops (BO-03)

TEC-04: No Real-Time External Channel Integration in MVP

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TEC-04
Description Sales channels (e-commerce, B2B portal, marketplaces) will not receive automated real-time inventory feeds from IMS in the first 12 months. Channel availability updates follow existing manual processes.
Business Justification Channel integration requires separate business case and partner agreements. MVP focuses on internal operational truth before external synchronization.
Affected Business Processes BP-10 (Status Monitoring), BP-16 (Availability Confirmation) — external channel context
Consequences if Violated Unplanned integration work breaches BC-01 and TC-02; channel overselling continues (BO-08); marketplace penalties; BO-16 applies only to internal sales — external channels remain inaccurate

TEC-05: Manual Data Exchange With Finance System

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TEC-05
Description Inventory valuation and movement data transfer to finance through scheduled export or manual reconciliation in the first 12 months — not automated general ledger posting.
Business Justification Finance system integration is out of IMS scope (BC-05). Interim operating model must close books using agreed manual reconciliation until Phase 3 automation.
Affected Business Processes BP-14 (Adjustments & Write-Offs), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation)
Consequences if Violated Finance team unprepared for new data volume; month-end delays continue (BO-20); valuation variance stays at ~8% (BO-18); duplicate or lost adjustments; audit trail gaps if exports not archived (LC-02)

TEC-06: User Access Limited to Company Network and Approved Devices

Attribute Detail
Constraint ID TEC-06
Description Access to inventory data — stock levels, valuation, movement history — is restricted to company-managed devices and approved network access per corporate security policy.
Business Justification Inventory data is commercially and financially sensitive. Corporate security policy prohibits unmanaged device access to operational and valuation information.
Affected Business Processes BP-10 (Visibility), BP-16 (Sales Availability), BP-29/30 (Management & Finance Reporting)
Consequences if Violated Security policy breach; data leakage of stock positions or valuation; remote sales and regional managers cannot access ATP without VPN; workaround spreadsheets reappear (BO-22); regulatory exposure (LC-01)

Constraint Interaction Summary

Constraints frequently compound. The following interactions have amplified operational impact:
