Budget + Organization BC-02 + ORC-01 Same staff run daily ops and project — burnout and adoption failure
Operational + Time OC-01 + TC-04 Narrow rollout windows; missed blackout = delayed network benefits 6+ months
Organization + Technology ORC-03 + TEC-01 Resistant users juggle IMS plus legacy systems without integration
Legal + Operations LC-02 + TEC-05 Manual finance exports must still meet 5–7 year retention
Operational + Organization OC-07 + ORC-05 Rolling counts need local manager cooperation at every decentralized site
Governance gap + Time ORC-07 + TC-02 Go-live without Inventory Controller — policies undefined, accuracy fails

Document ID: SRS-BC-001 | Version 1.0 | July 5, 2026

Business Exception Scenarios Specification

Inventory Management System

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-EX-001
Document Title Business Exception Scenarios — Inventory Management System
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Senior Business Analyst
Source Documents BRD-IMS-001, Business Events Catalog (BE-01–BE-59), Business Workflows (WF-01–WF-32), Common Inventory Management Scenarios, Business Rules (BR-001–BR-032)
Date July 5, 2026
Scope Business exception behavior only — not technical error handling, system faults, or implementation recovery

Purpose

This document identifies exception scenarios — situations that deviate from the standard happy-path inventory process and require defined business judgment, escalation, and response. Exceptions are normal operational events, not system failures. Each scenario describes what the business should do when the exception occurs.

How to Read Each Exception

Field Meaning
Exception ID Unique identifier (EX-001, EX-002, …)
Business Scenario What is happening from a business perspective
Trigger Event or condition that causes the exception
Expected Business Response What the organization should do — policies and actions
Responsible Actor Primary role accountable for resolution
Business Impact Consequences if not handled correctly

Related Business Event Reference

Where applicable, exceptions map to the Business Events Catalog (BE-xx) and Business Processes (BP-xx).

Domain 1: Master Data & Governance Exceptions

EX-001 — Duplicate Product Identity Detected

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-001
Business Scenario A new product submission matches or closely resembles an existing SKU, barcode, or product name, risking parallel product identities for the same physical item.
Trigger Inventory Controller or stakeholder attempts to create or update a product record (BE-02, BE-01).
Expected Business Response Halt new record creation; compare existing and proposed records side by side; merge or correct the existing record rather than create a duplicate; document justification if a genuinely new SKU is confirmed.
Responsible Actor Inventory Controller
Business Impact Fragmented stock records; inaccurate ATP; duplicate purchasing; reconciliation effort; unreliable network visibility

EX-002 — Discontinued Product With Open Activity

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-002
Business Scenario A product marked for discontinuation still has open purchase orders, active reservations, or remaining on-hand stock requiring disposition.
Trigger Product discontinuation requested (BE-03).
Expected Business Response Block new replenishment per BR-027; warn stakeholders of dependent open POs and reservations; define runout timeline for remaining stock; cancel or amend open POs; fulfill or release existing reservations per policy; plan clearance or write-off for residual quantity.
Responsible Actor Inventory Controller (with Purchasing Manager and Operations Director)
Business Impact Obsolete inventory accumulation; customer orders for withdrawn products; trapped working capital; conflicting assortment decisions

EX-003 — Location Closure With Remaining Stock

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-003
Business Scenario A warehouse or store approved for closure still holds on-hand inventory that must be dispositioned before deactivation.
Trigger Inventory location change approved for closure (BE-04).
Expected Business Response List all remaining stock; execute disposition plan (transfer out, sell-through, write-off); block new inbound and fulfillment except authorized disposition; obtain Operations Director sign-off before location deactivation.
Responsible Actor Operations Director
Business Impact Stranded inventory; orphaned records; financial misstatement; lost asset value

EX-004 — Opening Balance Dispute at Go-Live

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-004
Business Scenario Physical opening count results for a new or cutover location are challenged by local management or finance before location activation.
Trigger Opening stock balance submitted for approval (BP-02, BP-12).
Expected Business Response Suspend location activation; conduct recount or independent verification for disputed SKUs; resolve catalog gaps for unknown products; require authorized approver sign-off on final baseline before operational transactions begin.
Responsible Actor Inventory Controller
Business Impact Go-live with embedded errors; chronic inaccuracy from day one; distrust in system data; cascading fulfillment failures

Domain 2: Inbound & Procurement Exceptions

EX-005 — Supplier Short-Shipment

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-005
Business Scenario Supplier delivers fewer units than ordered on a purchase order, especially for a product already low or committed to customer orders.
Trigger Receipt verification finds quantity below PO expected quantity (BE-15).
Expected Business Response Record only verified received quantity; document short-shipment discrepancy; exclude disputed quantity from sellable stock; escalate with supplier for balance; recalculate ATP and customer commitments; hold payment pending three-way match resolution per BR-008.
Responsible Actor Receiving Clerk (document) → Purchasing Manager (supplier resolution)
Business Impact Phantom inventory if PO quantity accepted silently; stockouts on committed orders; supplier accountability lost; payment for undelivered goods

EX-006 — Damaged Goods at Receiving

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-006
Business Scenario Inbound shipment arrives with visible damage — crushed cartons, broken units, or temperature excursion — making some or all units unsellable.
Trigger Receiving clerk inspects packaging and product condition (BE-14, BE-15).
Expected Business Response Segregate damaged goods; accept only sellable units into inventory; photograph and document damage; initiate supplier or carrier claim; quarantine damaged quantity; exclude damaged stock from ATP per BR-013.
Responsible Actor Receiving Clerk → Warehouse Manager
Business Impact Defective goods sold to customers; returns and brand damage; unrecoverable supplier claims without dock evidence; inflated on-hand balances

EX-007 — Wrong Item Received Against Purchase Order

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-007
Business Scenario Physical product delivered does not match the purchase order line — different SKU, variant, or entirely wrong merchandise.
Trigger Product identity verification fails during goods receipt (BE-15).
Expected Business Response Reject mismatched product from inventory acceptance; document wrong-item discrepancy; notify purchasing and supplier; accept only correct items if partial shipment; do not record wrong SKU as on-hand.
Responsible Actor Receiving Clerk → Buyer
Business Impact Inventory records show stock that cannot be fulfilled; customer orders fail at pick; supplier dispute without documentation; payment for wrong goods

EX-008 — Receipt Without Valid Purchase Order

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-008
Business Scenario Supplier truck arrives with no matching open purchase order, or emergency delivery requires receipt outside standard procurement.
Trigger Receiving initiated without PO reference (BE-14).
Expected Business Response Hold shipment until purchasing confirms valid PO or grants authorized ad-hoc exception with documented approver and reason per BR-007; record exception for audit; do not accept standard supplier receipt without authorization.
Responsible Actor Receiving Clerk → Purchasing Manager
Business Impact Unauthorized spending; maverick buying; three-way match failure; audit control weakness

EX-009 — Over-Shipment Beyond Tolerance

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-009
Business Scenario Supplier delivers more units than ordered beyond the business-defined receipt tolerance.
Trigger Received quantity exceeds PO open quantity plus tolerance (BE-15).
Expected Business Response Flag over-receipt; require Warehouse Manager or Purchasing Manager approval before acceptance; document decision to accept excess, return excess, or create supplemental PO; adjust payment only for accepted quantity.
Responsible Actor Receiving Clerk → Warehouse Manager / Purchasing Manager
Business Impact Unplanned inventory investment; payment for unapproved goods; storage capacity strain; supplier assumes over-shipment is always accepted

EX-010 — Inbound Delivery Delayed Past Customer Promise

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-010
Business Scenario Purchase order or transfer shipment is delayed past the date already communicated to customers waiting on backorders or scheduled deliveries.
Trigger Supplier or carrier reports delay; expected delivery date passes without receipt (BE-39).
Expected Business Response Update expected arrival internally; proactively notify affected customers of revised dates; escalate with supplier; evaluate network transfer or alternate supply for critical commitments; reassess backorder queue priorities.
Responsible Actor Buyer → Customer Service Representative
Business Impact Silent delay destroys customer trust; backorder cancellations; contract penalties; emergency procurement at premium cost

EX-011 — Supplier Lead Time Extension

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-011
Business Scenario Supplier communicates longer lead times due to capacity, material, or logistics disruption, invalidating current reorder points and safety stock.
Trigger Demand or supply condition changed (BE-06); supplier notification during inbound tracking (BE-39).
Expected Business Response Recalculate reorder levels and safety stock for affected products; place orders earlier; inform sales of longer delivery windows; evaluate alternate suppliers for critical SKUs; document policy revision effective date.
Responsible Actor Inventory Controller → Purchasing Manager
Business Impact Preventable stockouts despite alerts; false confidence in replenishment timing; working capital shock if reactive safety stock increase

Domain 3: Inventory Control & Accuracy Exceptions

EX-012 — Material Cycle Count Variance

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-012
Business Scenario Cycle count finds physical quantity differs from recorded balance beyond defined tolerance.
Trigger Count variance identified after blind count submission (BE-24).
Expected Business Response Order recount if needed; investigate root cause before adjustment per BR-022; document investigation notes; route to independent approver per BR-019; apply adjustment with mandatory reason code per BR-020.
Responsible Actor Warehouse Manager → Inventory Controller
Business Impact Recurring variances if root cause ignored; accuracy metrics meaningless; audit findings; undetected shrinkage or process failure

EX-013 — Phantom Inventory (Record Shows Stock, Shelf Empty)

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-013
Business Scenario System shows positive available quantity but product cannot be found physically — empty pick location, bare shelf, or customer cannot locate item.
Trigger Pick exception reported (BE-33); customer or sales inquiry; verification count flagged (BE-21).
Expected Business Response Conduct physical search including overflow and mislabeled locations; if not found, adjust inventory with shrinkage or count correction reason code immediately; correct ATP to prevent further overselling; investigate root cause (theft, misplacement, unrecorded movement).
Responsible Actor Warehouse Manager → Inventory Controller
Business Impact Continued overselling; pick failures; customer embarrassment; lost sales despite "in stock" status; eroded data trust

EX-014 — Unexplained Shrinkage Trend at Location

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-014
Business Scenario A location shows rising shrinkage, write-offs, or negative adjustments exceeding its historical norm and network average without a single large incident.
Trigger Significant loss or adjustment event; monthly shrinkage review (BE-26, BE-27).
Expected Business Response Analyze trends by SKU, reason code, and shift; conduct process and security review; increase count frequency for affected categories; assign corrective action owner; escalate to Internal Auditor if suspected fraud.
Responsible Actor Inventory Controller → Operations Director
Business Impact Escalating unexplained loss; margin erosion; audit material weakness; chronic accuracy failure at location

EX-015 — Quality Hold on Received Lot

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-015
Business Scenario Inbound lot fails inspection, receives supplier quality alert, or is flagged for investigation before release to sellable stock.
Trigger Quality concern at receipt or post-receipt inspection.
Expected Business Response Move lot to quarantine; exclude from ATP immediately per BR-013; investigate with supplier; disposition as release, return, rework, or write-off with documented authorization; reassess customer orders depending on quarantined lot.
Responsible Actor Warehouse Manager → Inventory Controller
Business Impact Shipping defective or non-compliant product; regulatory exposure; customer safety risk; recall scope expansion

EX-016 — Full Physical Count Material Variance

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-016
Business Scenario Full wall-to-wall count produces location-wide variance exceeding acceptable threshold for financial substantiation.
Trigger Full physical count completed (BE-22, BE-23).
Expected Business Response Investigate significant line items; escalate to Operations Director and Finance; apply approved adjustments with full documentation; identify systemic causes; agree corrected baseline with finance before close.
Responsible Actor Inventory Controller → Operations Director / Finance Manager
Business Impact Financial misstatement; audit qualification; delayed month-end close; loss of inventory baseline credibility

Domain 4: Order Fulfillment Exceptions

EX-017 — Customer Order Exceeds Available-to-Promise

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-017
Business Scenario Customer order or sales quote requests quantity greater than current ATP at the fulfillment location, including cumulative effect of multiple orders against limited stock.
Trigger Customer order or quote received (BE-28); large or strategic order submitted (BE-29).
Expected Business Response Confirm only fulfillable quantity against ATP per BR-001; offer partial shipment, backorder with customer acknowledgment per BR-028, alternate location, or revised delivery date; do not confirm full order without documented plan; reserve only accepted quantity per BR-002.
Responsible Actor Sales Representative / Customer Service Representative
Business Impact Overselling; order cancellations; pick failures; customer complaints; expedited shipping costs; damaged sales credibility

EX-018 — Pick Failure — Stock Not Found at Location

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-018
Business Scenario Picker cannot locate reserved quantity at the designated storage location despite positive system record.
Trigger Pick exception reported during fulfillment (BE-33).
Expected Business Response Conduct immediate physical search; if unfound, trigger phantom inventory response (EX-013); re-pick if found elsewhere; initiate partial fulfillment or order line cancellation if unrecoverable; do not ship without verified pick per BR-003.
Responsible Actor Warehouse Picker / Packer → Warehouse Manager
Business Impact Shipment delay; wrong inventory record persists; customer promise missed; cascading pick queue disruption

EX-019 — Damaged Item Discovered During Pick

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-019
Business Scenario Product retrieved for order is damaged, expired, or otherwise unsellable at the pick point.
Trigger Picker reports condition exception during pick verification (BE-33).
Expected Business Response Quarantine damaged unit; process stock adjustment or write-off with reason code; attempt re-pick from alternate stock if available; substitute only with authorized approval; notify customer service if order affected.
Responsible Actor Warehouse Picker / Packer → Warehouse Manager
Business Impact Wrong or damaged goods shipped if ignored; customer return; brand damage; compounding record inaccuracy

EX-020 — Concurrent Demand for Last Available Units

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-020
Business Scenario Multiple customers, channels, or locations simultaneously require the last available units of a product — total demand exceeds remaining ATP.
Trigger Multiple simultaneous availability confirmations or reservations against depleting ATP (BE-28, BE-30).
Expected Business Response Apply documented allocation priority rules (contract obligation, customer tier, order date, channel priority); hard-reserve allocated quantity; communicate honestly with deprioritized parties; record allocation decision and rationale; do not award stock ad hoc under pressure.
Responsible Actor Inventory Controller / Sales Manager
Business Impact Arbitrary fulfillment; B2B contract breach; channel conflict; customer disputes; revenue loss on strategic accounts

EX-021 — Customer Order Cancelled After Reservation

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-021
Business Scenario Customer cancels order or reduces quantity after stock was reserved but before shipment.
Trigger Customer order cancelled (BE-35).
Expected Business Response Release reservation to restore ATP; return picked but unshipped goods to stock if applicable; record cancellation reason; notify operations if material quantity restored; update fulfillment status for customer service.
Responsible Actor Customer Service Representative → Warehouse Manager
Business Impact Stock artificially locked to dead orders; false stockouts; reduced sellable availability; fulfillment queue clutter

EX-022 — Partial Fulfillment Required

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-022
Business Scenario Full order quantity cannot be fulfilled at reservation or pick time, but customer policy allows partial delivery.
Trigger Insufficient stock at fulfillment (BE-34).
Expected Business Response Identify fulfillable vs. unfulfillable quantity; obtain customer acknowledgment before partial ship per BR-028; ship available portion; place remainder on backorder with ETA or cancellation option; alert purchasing for replenishment.
Responsible Actor Customer Service Representative → Warehouse Manager
Business Impact Complete order hold loses partial revenue; silent partial ship without acknowledgment causes disputes; backorder queue unmanaged

EX-023 — Authorized Product Substitution Required

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-023
Business Scenario Primary ordered SKU is unavailable at pick, but an approved alternate product could satisfy the customer need.
Trigger Pick exception or availability shortfall with defined substitute relationship (BE-33).
Expected Business Response Present only pre-approved substitute options; obtain customer acceptance and authorized approval; reserve and ship substitute SKU; record substitution on order with original and fulfilled product reference; adjust inventory for actual product shipped.
Responsible Actor Warehouse Manager → Sales Manager / Customer Service Representative
Business Impact Unauthorized substitute causes margin loss, warranty issues, or customer rejection; order remains unfulfilled if substitution declined without plan

Domain 5: Replenishment Exceptions

EX-024 — False Positive Low-Stock Alert

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-024
Business Scenario Low-stock alert fires but investigation shows adequate stock, inbound supply en route, or data timing issue — no genuine replenishment need.
Trigger Low-stock alert issued (BE-36); purchasing daily review.
Expected Business Response Validate against ATP, open POs, and in-transit transfers; dismiss alert with documented reason; review threshold configuration if recurring false positives; do not place duplicate purchase order.
Responsible Actor Buyer / Purchasing Manager
Business Impact Duplicate procurement; excess inventory; alert fatigue; ignored genuine alerts later

EX-025 — Emergency Stockout on Priority SKU

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-025
Business Scenario Class A or priority product reaches zero ATP with active customer demand or open commitments.
Trigger Emergency stockout declared (BE-10); stock threshold breached at zero (BE-19).
Expected Business Response Escalate urgently to purchasing and operations leadership; check network for transfer before new purchase per BR-011; initiate expedited PO or emergency transfer; communicate realistic re-availability to sales and customer service; document root cause for post-incident review.
Responsible Actor Purchasing Manager → Operations Director
Business Impact Lost sales; customer cancellations; premium freight costs; revenue at risk on priority products; reputational damage

EX-026 — Safety Stock Override Requested

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-026
Business Scenario Reservation, transfer, or fulfillment request would consume safety stock below policy buffer without a replenishment plan.
Trigger Reservation or transfer evaluation against safety stock (BE-30, BE-41).
Expected Business Response Block routine consumption of safety stock per BR-010; require authorized exception with approver, documented reason, and replenishment plan; record exception for governance review; deny if no recovery plan exists.
Responsible Actor Operations Director / Inventory Controller
Business Impact Next demand or supply shock causes immediate stockout; safety investment wasted; chronic crisis replenishment

Domain 6: Network Balance & Transfer Exceptions

EX-027 — Local Stockout With Network Excess Elsewhere

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-027
Business Scenario One location is out of stock on a product while other network locations hold available excess quantity.
Trigger Network imbalance identified (BE-42); low-stock at one site with surplus elsewhere.
Expected Business Response Verify network ATP; initiate inter-location transfer request before new purchase per BR-011; approve transfer if source can spare stock per BR-012; communicate revised availability to sales.
Responsible Actor Regional / Store Manager → Operations Director
Business Impact Duplicate purchasing; excess at one site while another stockouts; trapped capital; lost local sales

EX-028 — Transfer Would Breach Source Minimum

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-028
Business Scenario Approved or requested transfer quantity would deplete the source location below its minimum threshold or safety stock.
Trigger Inter-location transfer requested or approved (BE-41, BE-43).
Expected Business Response Reduce transfer to maximum spareable quantity per BR-012; reject or modify request with documented reason; suggest alternate source location if available; do not approve transfer that creates source stockout.
Responsible Actor Operations Director / Warehouse Manager (source)
Business Impact Cascading stockouts across network; emergency replenishment at source; net worsening of network availability

EX-029 — In-Transit Transfer Receipt Variance

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-029
Business Scenario Destination receives fewer units than dispatched, or goods arrive damaged in transit between locations.
Trigger Transfer shipment received with variance (BE-46).
Expected Business Response Document receipt variance; investigate loss or damage in transit; adjust source and destination records accordingly; process write-off or claim if applicable; close transfer only when quantities reconciled.
Responsible Actor Receiving Clerk (destination) → Warehouse Manager
Business Impact Stock lost between locations; both sites show incorrect balances; accountability gap; unresolved in-transit aging

EX-030 — Emergency Transfer Request

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-030
Business Scenario Location urgently needs stock — key customer order, promotional event, or unexpected spike — faster than supplier replenishment allows.
Trigger Inter-location transfer requested with urgency flag (BE-41).
Expected Business Response Verify source ATP and minimum threshold; obtain expedited approval; execute pick and ship with documented freight authorization; track in-transit until receipt confirmed; review why standard replenishment failed.
Responsible Actor Regional / Store Manager → Operations Director
Business Impact Customer promise missed if transfer delayed; premium freight unbudgeted; source location risk if minimum not protected

Domain 7: Returns Exceptions

EX-031 — Return Received Without Authorization

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-031
Business Scenario Warehouse receives returned goods without a valid return authorization linked to an original order.
Trigger Returned goods arrive at dock (BE-48) without matching authorization.
Expected Business Response Hold goods; contact customer service to validate or issue retroactive authorization per policy; refuse acceptance if policy violation or fraud suspected; do not add to sellable stock without valid linkage per BR-025.
Responsible Actor Receiving Clerk → Customer Service Representative
Business Impact Returns cannot match orders; fraudulent returns accepted; refund without receipt; inventory records incorrect

EX-032 — Returned Product Fails Inspection

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-032
Business Scenario Returned item is used, damaged, or defective and does not meet resale quality standards.
Trigger Return inspection completed with fail outcome (BE-49).
Expected Business Response Write off or liquidate non-resalable quantity with reason code per BR-026; do not restock to sellable inventory; process customer refund or credit per original resolution agreement; capture return reason for trend analysis.
Responsible Actor Warehouse Manager → Inventory Controller
Business Impact Damaged goods resold as new; repeat returns; customer complaints; inflated sellable ATP

EX-033 — Return Quantity or Product Mismatch

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-033
Business Scenario Physical return does not match authorization — wrong product, partial quantity, or excess units.
Trigger Return receipt verification against authorization (BE-48).
Expected Business Response Document mismatch; contact customer; hold mismatched items; accept only authorized product and quantity; adjust refund or credit proportionally per policy.
Responsible Actor Receiving Clerk → Customer Service Representative
Business Impact Over-refund; inventory credited for wrong items; unresolved return status; customer dispute

Domain 8: Commercial & Promotional Exceptions

EX-034 — Promotional Demand Exceeds Forecast

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-034
Business Scenario Marketing promotion drives demand above planned levels and promotional stock depletes faster than campaign duration.
Trigger Marketing campaign scheduled with accelerating sell-through (BE-55); stock threshold breached on promoted SKUs.
Expected Business Response Ring-fence remaining promotional stock per BR-029; allocate to promoted channels; expedite replenishment or network transfer if feasible; inform marketing to adjust campaign intensity; communicate "while supplies last" if stock will not last.
Responsible Actor Marketing Manager → Purchasing Manager / Operations Director
Business Impact Campaign stockout during peak visibility; promotional ROI lost; customer disappointment at worst moment; channel conflict

EX-035 — Campaign Stock Gap Before Launch

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-035
Business Scenario Pre-launch readiness review finds current plus inbound stock insufficient for campaign targets within lead time.
Trigger Marketing campaign scheduled or new product launch date set (BE-55, BE-56).
Expected Business Response Quantify gap by SKU and location; escalate go/no-go decision to commercial and operations leadership; expedite purchasing if recoverable; delay or reduce campaign scope if not; document risk acceptance if proceeding.
Responsible Actor Marketing Manager → Operations Director
Business Impact Public launch without stock; brand embarrassment; wasted marketing spend; BO-24 promotional readiness failure

EX-036 — Channel Conflict Over Shared Inventory

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-036
Business Scenario Online, retail, wholesale, or marketplace channels compete for the same limited ATP — conflicting allocation requests for last units.
Trigger Concurrent orders from multiple channels against shared pool (BE-28).
Expected Business Response Apply leadership-defined channel priority rules; hard-allocate per EX-020; update channel-facing availability manually until integration available; escalate recurring conflicts to commercial leadership for policy review.
Responsible Actor Inventory Controller / Sales Manager
Business Impact Double-selling across channels; store associates vs. e-commerce conflict; wholesale contract breach; inconsistent customer experience

Domain 9: Financial, Governance & Compliance Exceptions

EX-037 — Operations and Finance Inventory Mismatch at Month-End

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-037
Business Scenario Operational inventory quantities or valuation do not reconcile with general ledger balance at month-end close.
Trigger Month-end financial close initiated (BE-53).
Expected Business Response Categorize variances (timing, quantity, valuation); investigate unexplained gaps; correct operational records or agree financial adjustment; complete reconciliation within close calendar; escalate material gaps to CFO.
Responsible Actor Finance Manager → Inventory Controller
Business Impact Financial misstatement; audit findings; delayed close; BO-18 and BO-20 objectives fail; operations-finance distrust persists

EX-038 — Adjustment or Write-Off Exceeds Approval Threshold

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-038
Business Scenario Proposed inventory adjustment or write-off exceeds the approver's financial or quantity authority.
Trigger Stock correction required (BE-25); significant write-off recorded (BE-54).
Expected Business Response Route to independent higher-authority approver per BR-021; require documented evidence for write-offs per BR-023; block application until approved; notify finance for material write-offs.
Responsible Actor Warehouse Manager (initiator) → Operations Director / CFO
Business Impact Unauthorized large adjustments; fraud opportunity; financial misstatement; audit material weakness

EX-039 — Segregation of Duties Violation Attempted

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-039
Business Scenario Same person attempts to perform and approve a conflicting action — count and approve own variance, receive and approve own PO variance, or self-approve material adjustment.
Trigger Control incident or policy breach identified (BE-59).
Expected Business Response Block self-approval; route to independent approver per BR-019; log policy breach or authorized exception; review role assignment for systemic conflicts; inform Internal Auditor if material or recurring.
Responsible Actor Warehouse Manager / Inventory Controller → Operations Director
Business Impact Fraud and error undetected; SOX or audit failure; invalid accuracy and adjustment records

EX-040 — Product Recall Requiring Lot Quarantine

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-040
Business Scenario Quality defect, contamination, or regulatory notice requires recall of specific lot or batch — stock may be in warehouse, in transit, or already shipped.
Trigger Supplier quality alert; regulatory notice; internal quality failure discovery.
Expected Business Response Identify all affected lot quantity through traceability records; quarantine immediately and exclude from ATP per BR-013; trace shipped units to customers; notify regulatory authorities within mandated timelines; disposition quarantined stock after investigation.
Responsible Actor Inventory Controller → Quality / Regulatory (with Operations Director)
Business Impact Consumer harm; regulatory penalties; full product-line recall if lot data missing; legal liability; brand catastrophe

EX-041 — Control Policy Breach With Authorized Exception

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-041
Business Scenario Business situation requires deviation from standard policy — ad-hoc receipt without PO, safety stock override, or emergency approval outside normal authority — with legitimate operational justification.
Trigger Control incident identified with exception path (BE-59).
Expected Business Response Document approver, policy reference, business reason, and replenishment or recovery plan; apply exception only within granted authority; log for governance review; do not normalize exception into standard practice.
Responsible Actor Operations Director / Purchasing Manager
Business Impact If undocumented: audit finding and control erosion; if denied when needed: operational paralysis during genuine emergency

Domain 10: Demand Shock & Lifecycle Exceptions

EX-042 — Flash Demand Spike From External Event

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-042
Business Scenario Unplanned external event — viral trend, competitor stockout redirect, weather — causes sudden demand depleting stock in hours or days.
Trigger Rapid ATP depletion; multiple urgent availability inquiries; stock threshold breached on unaffected forecast SKUs.
Expected Business Response Apply allocation rules immediately; assess fastest replenishment path; communicate realistic availability internally and externally; avoid overcommitment; conduct post-event review for safety stock and supplier capacity.
Responsible Actor Operations Director → Inventory Controller / Purchasing Manager
Business Impact Overselling during spike; reputational damage outlasting revenue gain; unfilled strategic customer orders; supplier also caught short

EX-043 — End-of-Season or Obsolete Stock Requiring Write-Off

Attribute Detail
Exception ID EX-043
Business Scenario Seasonal, discontinued, or slow-moving product has no remaining commercial value and must be removed from active inventory.
Trigger Scheduled aging review; product discontinued with residual stock (BE-03); overstock report review.
Expected Business Response Segregate physically; execute planned exit (markdown, outlet, donation, destroy); process authorized write-off with evidence per BR-023; update financial records; do not delay write-off inflating reported inventory.
Responsible Actor Inventory Controller → Finance Manager
Business Impact Trapped working capital; inflated operational and financial inventory; recurring carrying cost; misleading availability if stock remains "active"

Exception Response Pattern Summary

Pattern Exception IDs Core Business Discipline
Verify before recording EX-005 – EX-009, EX-031 – EX-033 Document at point of occurrence; never accept silent variance
Investigate before adjusting EX-012, EX-013, EX-014, EX-016 Root cause before number correction
Check network first EX-025, EX-027, EX-030 Transfer before purchase
ATP-only commitment EX-017, EX-020, EX-022, EX-036 Promise only fulfillable quantity
Independent approval EX-038, EX-039 Segregation of duties on material actions
Proactive communication EX-010, EX-017, EX-022, EX-025 Customer and internal honesty on delays
Quarantine and exclude EX-006, EX-015, EX-040 Non-sellable stock never in ATP
Governed exception only EX-008, EX-026, EX-041 Documented override — not normalized bypass

Business Process Decision Tables

Inventory Management System

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-DT-001
Document Title Business Process Decision Tables — Inventory Management System
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Senior Business Analyst
Source Documents BRD-IMS-001 (Section 10), Business Workflows (WF-01–WF-32), Business Exception Scenarios (EX-001–EX-043)
Date July 5, 2026
Scope Business decision logic only — not system rules, validation logic, or technical branching

Purpose

This document identifies 32 business processes that contain multiple decision paths and expresses key branching logic as decision tables. Each table maps business conditions to actions and outcomes so stakeholders can see how the organization should respond when situations differ.

How to Read Decision Tables

Column Meaning
Rule Rule identifier within the process (R1, R2, …). Rules are evaluated in priority order unless noted.
Conditions Business facts that must be true for the rule to apply. "—" means any value.
Actions What responsible actors should do when conditions are met.
Outcome Resulting process state or next workflow triggered.

Notation: Y = Yes / True · N = No / False · — = Don't care / Not applicable

Document ID: SRS-DT-001 | Version 1.0 | July 5, 2026

Business Rule Dependency Analysis

Inventory Management System

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-BRDEP-001
Document Title Business Rule Dependencies — Inventory Management System
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Senior Domain Expert
Source Documents SRS-BR-001, BRD-IMS-001 (Section 13), Business Workflows (WF-01–WF-32), SRS-DT-001
Date July 5, 2026
Scope Business rule relationships only — not system implementation, validation rules, or technical constraints

Purpose

This document analyzes dependencies among the 32 business rules (BR-001–BR-032). For each dependency it identifies the parent rule, dependent rule, dependency type, and business impact. It also catalogs conflicting and overlapping rules that require explicit policy resolution.

Dependency Type Definitions

Type Meaning
Prerequisite The parent rule must be satisfied or in force before the dependent rule can be applied meaningfully.
Sequential The parent rule governs an earlier step in the same business process; the dependent rule applies only after the parent step completes.
Compositional The dependent rule builds on or is calculated from conditions established by the parent rule.
Constraint The parent rule limits, bounds, or restricts how the dependent rule may be executed.
Exception The parent rule defines an authorized exception path to the dependent rule under defined conditions.
Reinforcement Rules apply to the same control objective from different angles; both must hold simultaneously.

Conflict / Overlap Classification

Classification Meaning
Scope Overlap Two rules govern the same business object or decision point with partially duplicate intent.
Operational Tension Both rules are valid but compete for the same resource, timing, or stock pool.
Priority Ambiguity Precedence between rules is not explicit; actors may apply them in conflicting order.
Mutual Exclusion Rules require mutually exclusive actions in the same context without a defined selector.

1. Dependency Catalog

Dependencies are grouped by business domain. Rule pairs already noted in SRS-BR-001 as interdependent combinations are included and extended.

1.1 Availability, Commitment & Fulfillment

ID Parent Rule Dependent Rule Dependency Type Business Impact
DEP-001 BR-005 Put-Away Before Availability BR-001 ATP-Only Customer Commitment Compositional ATP cannot include received-but-not-put-away stock. Violating BR-005 inflates ATP and causes BR-001 overselling — customers confirmed against stock pickers cannot locate.
DEP-002 BR-013 Quarantine Exclusion BR-001 ATP-Only Customer Commitment Compositional Quarantined, hold, and recall stock must be excluded from ATP. If BR-013 is ignored, BR-001 permits commitment to non-sellable inventory — regulatory, quality, and customer risk.
DEP-003 BR-030 Bonded Inventory Clearance BR-001 ATP-Only Customer Commitment Compositional Bonded stock is non-sellable until customs release. Same ATP exclusion logic as BR-013; failure blocks legal domestic sale while appearing available.
DEP-004 BR-001 ATP-Only Customer Commitment BR-002 Reservation at Order Confirmation Compositional BR-001 defines what quantity is promiseable; BR-002 locks that quantity at confirmation. Without BR-001's ATP definition, reservations lack a consistent baseline and double-allocation risk returns.
DEP-005 BR-002 Reservation at Order Confirmation BR-001 ATP-Only Customer Commitment Compositional Each reservation reduces ATP. BR-002 is the mechanism that keeps BR-001 accurate as orders confirm — circular but mutually defining: ATP = on-hand minus reservations and non-sellable holds.
DEP-006 BR-001 ATP-Only Customer Commitment BR-028 Backorder Customer Acknowledgment Sequential When ATP is insufficient at confirmation, BR-028 governs the customer agreement path before backorder is recorded. BR-001 prevents silent over-commitment; BR-028 governs explicit under-commitment.
DEP-007 BR-002 Reservation at Order Confirmation BR-003 Verified Pick Before Shipment Sequential Stock must be reserved before pick execution. BR-003 deducts inventory only after verified pick; BR-002 ensures the picked quantity was already committed to the correct order.
DEP-008 BR-002 Reservation at Order Confirmation BR-028 Backorder Customer Acknowledgment Sequential Partial reservation (available portion) pairs with BR-028 for the unreserved remainder. Without sequencing, partial ship may occur without customer agreement on the backorder portion.
DEP-009 BR-010 Safety Stock Protection BR-002 Reservation at Order Confirmation Constraint Reservations must not consume safety stock without authorized exception and replenishment plan. Violation depletes buffer protecting against demand/supply uncertainty — next disruption causes stockout despite apparent policy compliance.
DEP-010 BR-029 Promotional Stock Ring-Fencing BR-001 ATP-Only Customer Commitment Constraint Promotional allocation reduces ATP available to non-promotional demand. BR-029 further restricts which orders may consume ring-fenced stock beyond ATP arithmetic alone.
DEP-011 BR-029 Promotional Stock Ring-Fencing BR-002 Reservation at Order Confirmation Constraint Non-promotional orders must not reserve ring-fenced promotional stock without commercial leadership approval. Prevents campaign stock erosion through standard reservation.
DEP-012 BR-014 FEFO Rotation BR-003 Verified Pick Before Shipment Constraint Pick verification must confirm correct lot/batch per FEFO priority. Wrong lot picked violates rotation even if quantity matches — expiry write-off and compliance risk.
DEP-013 BR-015 FIFO Rotation BR-003 Verified Pick Before Shipment Constraint Same as DEP-012 for non-perishable goods — oldest receipt date must be picked first.
DEP-014 BR-017 Lot/Batch Capture BR-003 Verified Pick Before Shipment Prerequisite Traceable products require lot attribution at pick. BR-003 verification is incomplete without lot capture — recall scope cannot be determined.
DEP-015 BR-017 Lot/Batch Capture BR-014 FEFO Rotation Reinforcement FEFO requires expiry-aware lot identity; BR-017 provides the data FEFO depends on for shelf-life products.

1.2 Inbound, Receiving & Procurement

ID Parent Rule Dependent Rule Dependency Type Business Impact
DEP-016 BR-007 PO Required for Supplier Receipt BR-004 Verify Before Inventory Acceptance Prerequisite Verification is performed against an authorized PO (or approved ad-hoc exception). Without BR-007, verification lacks a reference baseline — unauthorized receipts enter inventory.
DEP-017 BR-004 Verify Before Inventory Acceptance BR-005 Put-Away Before Availability Sequential Only verified quantities proceed to put-away. Put-away without verification propagates unconfirmed stock into the availability chain (DEP-001 risk).
DEP-018 BR-004 Verify Before Inventory Acceptance BR-006 Document Receipt Discrepancies Sequential Discrepancies are identified during verification and must be documented before acceptance. BR-006 preserves evidence BR-004 discovers — undocumented acceptance waives supplier claims.
DEP-019 BR-006 Document Receipt Discrepancies BR-008 Three-Way Match Before Payment Prerequisite Documented receipt quantities are the "received" leg of three-way match. Missing discrepancy documentation causes payment for goods not received or failure to withhold payment for shorts.
DEP-020 BR-007 PO Required for Supplier Receipt BR-008 Three-Way Match Before Payment Prerequisite PO is the "ordered" leg of three-way match. Receiving without PO (BR-007 violation) makes BR-008 impossible — payment control breakdown.
DEP-021 BR-004 Verify Before Inventory Acceptance BR-008 Three-Way Match Before Payment Prerequisite Verified receipt is the "received" leg. Unverified acceptance corrupts the match and financial records simultaneously.
DEP-022 BR-016 Minimum Remaining Shelf Life at Receipt BR-004 Verify Before Inventory Acceptance Constraint MRSL check is part of condition verification for shelf-life products. Failed MRSL triggers reject/disposition before acceptance — prevents BR-014 FEFO from managing already-expired inbound stock.
DEP-023 BR-016 Minimum Remaining Shelf Life at Receipt BR-014 FEFO Rotation Reinforcement MRSL at receipt ensures sufficient selling window; FEFO during fulfillment minimizes remaining expiry at customer delivery. Jointly protect shelf-life economics.
DEP-024 BR-017 Lot/Batch Capture BR-004 Verify Before Inventory Acceptance Constraint Traceable products require lot capture at receipt as part of verification completeness.
DEP-025 BR-017 Lot/Batch Capture BR-005 Put-Away Before Availability Sequential Lot identity must be assigned before or during put-away so subsequent movements maintain traceability.
DEP-026 BR-030 Bonded Inventory Clearance BR-005 Put-Away Before Availability Constraint Bonded goods may be physically stored but must not enter sellable availability (DEP-003) until customs clearance — put-away to sellable location prohibited until cleared.
DEP-027 BR-031 Consignment Ownership at Consumption BR-004 Verify Before Inventory Acceptance Constraint Consignment receipt is physical verification without ownership transfer. Misclassifying as owned at receipt overstates assets and breaks BR-031 valuation treatment.
DEP-028 BR-031 Consignment Ownership at Consumption BR-008 Three-Way Match Before Payment Exception Consignment may not trigger standard PO-to-payment flow until consumption event per supplier agreement — BR-008 applies at ownership transfer, not physical receipt.

1.3 Replenishment & Network Balance

ID Parent Rule Dependent Rule Dependency Type Business Impact
DEP-029 BR-009 Reorder at Reorder Level BR-021 Low-Stock Alert Review (via BP-21) Sequential Reorder level breach triggers replenishment review. BR-009 mandates same-business-day action; delay guarantees stockout during lead time.
DEP-030 BR-011 Network Check Before Purchase BR-009 Reorder at Reorder Level Constraint Before executing replenishment (BR-009), network transfer must be evaluated. Skipping BR-011 causes unnecessary PO spend and worsens network imbalance while BR-009 appears satisfied.
DEP-031 BR-011 Network Check Before Purchase BR-012 Protect Source Location Minimum Reinforcement Network check (BR-011) often resolves shortage via transfer; BR-012 ensures the transfer path does not create a new shortage at source. Both required for effective network balance.
DEP-032 BR-012 Protect Source Location Minimum BR-011 Network Check Before Purchase Constraint Transfer feasibility assessment must respect source minimum. BR-011 "network has stock" is insufficient if BR-012 blocks the transferable quantity.
DEP-033 BR-010 Safety Stock Protection BR-012 Protect Source Location Minimum Reinforcement Both protect minimum stock buffers — BR-010 at policy level, BR-012 at transfer execution. Source minimum typically includes safety stock component.
DEP-034 BR-027 No Reorder of Discontinued Products BR-009 Reorder at Reorder Level Constraint BR-009 replenishment action is prohibited for discontinued SKUs. Alert may still fire but response must be runout/clearance, not reorder.
DEP-035 BR-027 No Reorder of Discontinued Products BR-011 Network Check Before Purchase Constraint Network transfer may still move discontinued stock for clearance; new procurement is blocked. Prevents obsolete inventory creation.
DEP-036 BR-032 Class A Priority Monitoring BR-009 Reorder at Reorder Level Constraint Class A SKUs receive heightened monitoring and faster escalation when approaching reorder level. BR-032 intensifies BR-009 response without changing the threshold logic.
DEP-037 BR-032 Class A Priority Monitoring BR-011 Network Check Before Purchase Reinforcement Priority SKUs require expedited network evaluation before external purchase — reduces stockout duration on high-impact items.

1.4 Inventory Control & Governance

ID Parent Rule Dependent Rule Dependency Type Business Impact
DEP-038 BR-018 Blind Cycle Counting BR-022 Investigate Before Adjusting Sequential Blind count produces unbiased variance detection that triggers investigation. Showing system quantity before count (BR-018 violation) undermines variance integrity and root cause analysis.
DEP-039 BR-022 Investigate Before Adjusting BR-020 Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes Sequential Investigation findings must be captured as reason code at adjustment. BR-020 without BR-022 produces codes without verified root cause — analytically weak.
DEP-040 BR-022 Investigate Before Adjusting BR-021 Independent Approval for Material Adjustments Sequential Investigation completes before approval decision. Approving without investigation (BR-022 violation) repeats same variance on next count.
DEP-041 BR-018 Blind Cycle Counting BR-019 Independent Count Approval Reinforcement Blind count (BR-018) detects variance; independent approval (BR-019) prevents counter from self-approving biased or erroneous counts. Joint fraud/error control.
DEP-042 BR-019 Independent Count Approval BR-021 Independent Approval for Material Adjustments Reinforcement BR-019 applies to count variances; BR-021 applies to material adjustments generally. Same segregation principle — overlapping scope (see OV-003).
DEP-043 BR-020 Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes BR-023 Documented Write-Off Authorization Compositional Write-off is a subset of adjustment requiring reason code (BR-020) plus additional evidence and authorization (BR-023).
DEP-044 BR-021 Independent Approval for Material Adjustments BR-023 Documented Write-Off Authorization Reinforcement Material write-offs require both threshold-based independent approval (BR-021) and documented evidence (BR-023).
DEP-045 BR-024 Physical Inventory Freeze BR-018 Blind Cycle Counting Constraint Full count freeze suspends movements that would change quantities during count. Cycle counts during operations (BR-018) continue under BP-11 without full freeze.
DEP-046 BR-024 Physical Inventory Freeze BR-003 Verified Pick Before Shipment Operational Tension Freeze suspends shipping until count complete. Conflicts with open order fulfillment — requires freeze scheduling and customer communication (see CF-001).
DEP-047 BR-024 Physical Inventory Freeze BR-005 Put-Away Before Availability Operational Tension Freeze suspends receiving/put-away at counted location. Inbound goods queue — delays BR-005 and downstream BR-001 ATP increase.
DEP-048 BR-013 Quarantine Exclusion BR-020 Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes Sequential Quarantine disposition (damage, recall) typically results in adjustment with mandatory reason code — links quality hold to governance trail.
DEP-049 BR-032 Class A Priority Monitoring BR-018 Blind Cycle Counting Constraint Class A products receive highest count frequency per BR-032. More frequent BR-018 application on priority SKUs.

1.5 Returns & Commercial

ID Parent Rule Dependent Rule Dependency Type Business Impact
DEP-050 BR-025 Return Authorization Required BR-026 Inspect Returns Before Restocking Sequential Authorization precedes physical receipt; inspection precedes restocking. BR-026 cannot apply to unauthorized returns accepted at dock.
DEP-051 BR-026 Inspect Returns Before Restocking BR-013 Quarantine Exclusion Sequential Failed inspection routes to quarantine or write-off — must not enter ATP until disposition. BR-026 is the gate; BR-013 maintains exclusion during hold.
DEP-052 BR-026 Inspect Returns Before Restocking BR-001 ATP-Only Customer Commitment Compositional Only inspection-passed returns increase sellable ATP. Restocking without inspection (BR-026 violation) inflates ATP with potentially unsellable goods.
DEP-053 BR-025 Return Authorization Required BR-028 Backorder Customer Acknowledgment Reinforcement Both require explicit customer agreement before recording a commercial state (return acceptance / backorder). Shared consent principle across inbound return and outbound delay.
DEP-054 BR-026 Inspect Returns Before Restocking BR-023 Documented Write-Off Authorization Sequential Non-resalable returns proceed to write-off path requiring BR-023 authorization and evidence.

1.6 Cross-Domain & Financial

ID Parent Rule Dependent Rule Dependency Type Business Impact
DEP-055 BR-004 Verify Before Inventory Acceptance BR-031 Consignment Ownership at Consumption Compositional Physical receipt verified under BR-004; ownership treatment governed separately by BR-031.
DEP-056 BR-008 Three-Way Match Before Payment BR-031 Consignment Ownership at Consumption Sequential Standard three-way match at invoice; consignment payment triggers at consumption per agreement — different timing, same control intent.
DEP-057 BR-020 Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes BR-008 Three-Way Match Before Payment Reinforcement Inventory adjustments from receipt discrepancies (reason codes) must align with received quantities used in BR-008 — financial and operational records must reconcile.
DEP-058 BR-001 ATP-Only Customer Commitment BR-031 Consignment Ownership at Consumption Constraint Consignment stock may be physically present but not owned — must be excluded from owned ATP or separately identified to prevent BR-001 misapplication.

3. Rule Dependency Chains

Critical end-to-end chains where breaking any link undermines the chain:

Chain A — Sellable Availability (Inbound to Customer)

BR-007 (PO) → BR-004 (Verify) → BR-006 (Document variance)
     → BR-005 (Put-away) → BR-013/BR-030 (Exclude non-sellable)
     → BR-001 (ATP) → BR-002 (Reserve) → BR-003 (Pick/Ship)

Business impact of chain failure: Any break causes phantom availability, overselling, or shipment of non-compliant stock.

Chain B — Replenishment Without Waste

BR-009 (Reorder trigger) → BR-011 (Network check) → BR-012 (Source minimum)
     → [Transfer] or [BR-007 PO path]

Business impact: Skipping network check wastes capital; ignoring source minimum relocates shortage.

Chain C — Count Integrity

BR-018 (Blind count) → BR-022 (Investigate) → BR-020 (Reason code)
     → BR-019/BR-021 (Independent approval)

Business impact: Skipping investigation or approval perpetuates errors and fraud exposure.

Chain D — Financial Control

BR-007 (PO) → BR-004 (Verify) → BR-006 (Document) → BR-008 (Three-way match)

Business impact: Payment for unordered, unreceived, or mispriced goods; audit failure.

4. Conflicting Rules

Rules that create genuine tension requiring explicit policy, timing, or precedence resolution.

CF-001 — BR-024 Physical Inventory Freeze vs. BR-002 / BR-003 Fulfillment

Attribute Detail
Rules in Conflict BR-024 (suspend shipping during full count) vs. BR-002 (honor reservations) vs. BR-003 (ship verified picks)
Conflict Type Operational Tension
Nature Full count freeze stops outbound movements; confirmed orders with reservations expect fulfillment.
Business Impact Customer delivery delays; reservation hold times extend; potential BR-028 backorder triggers if freeze is prolonged.
Recommended Resolution Schedule freeze during low-activity window; pre-communicate delays; complete freeze before peak; regional freeze rotation so network can fulfill from alternate locations (BR-011).

CF-002 — BR-024 Physical Inventory Freeze vs. BR-005 / BR-004 Inbound

Attribute Detail
Rules in Conflict BR-024 vs. BR-004 / BR-005
Conflict Type Operational Tension
Nature Freeze suspends receiving and put-away; supplier deliveries may arrive on schedule regardless.
Business Impact Dock congestion; delayed ATP increase; supplier detention charges; inbound backlog after freeze lifts.
Recommended Resolution Coordinate inbound schedule with count calendar; stage received goods without put-away to quarantine/staging if policy allows; or reschedule supplier deliveries.

CF-003 — BR-009 Same-Day Replenishment vs. BR-011 Network Evaluation Time

Attribute Detail
Rules in Conflict BR-009 (act same business day at reorder level) vs. BR-011 (evaluate network before purchase)
Conflict Type Priority Ambiguity
Nature Thorough network transfer evaluation may delay PO placement beyond same day; rushing BR-011 risks missing transferable stock.
Business Impact Either stockout (BR-009 delayed) or unnecessary PO (BR-011 skipped).
Recommended Resolution Define SLA: network check within same business day for Class A (BR-032); standard SKUs may place PO same day while transfer evaluation runs in parallel for next cycle.

CF-004 — BR-006 Document Before Acceptance vs. Partial Receipt Urgency

Attribute Detail
Rules in Conflict BR-006 (document all discrepancies before acceptance) vs. operational need to accept good units immediately
Conflict Type Priority Ambiguity
Nature Damaged/wrong items mixed with good stock — strict interpretation blocks all acceptance until full documentation; operations want good portion in inventory.
Business Impact Dock hold delays BR-005/BR-001; or premature full acceptance waives claims (BR-006 violation).
Recommended Resolution Accept verified good quantity with documented discrepancy on remainder — partial acceptance path in BP-08/DT-08; never accept undocumented variance.

CF-005 — BR-029 Promotional Ring-Fence vs. BR-001 / BR-002 General Fulfillment

Attribute Detail
Rules in Conflict BR-029 (promo stock reserved for campaign) vs. BR-001/BR-002 (ATP and reservation for any confirmed order)
Conflict Type Operational Tension
Nature ATP may show stock available that BR-029 reserves for promotional channel only.
Business Impact Campaign stock consumed by routine orders; promoted channel stockout; or routine orders rejected despite apparent ATP.
Recommended Resolution Treat ring-fenced quantity as separate ATP pool or hard reservation at campaign setup; BR-029 overrides general BR-001 for ring-fenced portion.

CF-006 — BR-010 Safety Stock Exception vs. BR-002 Reservation for Urgent Orders

Attribute Detail
Rules in Conflict BR-010 (no safety stock consumption without exception) vs. BR-002 (reserve at confirmation for urgent/priority orders)
Conflict Type Priority Ambiguity
Nature Urgent order confirmation may require stock below safety threshold; BR-010 blocks unless exception documented.
Business Impact Order confirmation fails despite physical stock; or safety buffer eroded without replenishment plan.
Recommended Resolution Explicit safety-stock exception workflow with approver, replenishment plan, and time limit; priority orders do not auto-bypass BR-010.

CF-007 — BR-007 PO Required vs. Emergency Ad-Hoc Receipt

Attribute Detail
Rules in Conflict BR-007 (PO required) vs. emergency receiving without pre-issued PO
Conflict Type Exception Gap
Nature BR-007 allows "explicitly approved ad-hoc receipt exception" but BR-008 three-way match assumes standard PO flow.
Business Impact Emergency stock received but payment blocked; or unauthorized receipt bypasses financial controls.
Recommended Resolution Define ad-hoc exception approver, retroactive PO process, and BR-008 alternate match rules for emergency receipts.

5. Overlapping Rules

Rules with partially duplicate scope that are complementary when coordinated, or redundant/confusing when not.

OV-001 — BR-013 Quarantine Exclusion vs. BR-030 Bonded Inventory Clearance

Attribute Detail
Overlap Type Scope Overlap
Shared Scope Stock excluded from sellable ATP
Distinction BR-013: quality hold, investigation, recall. BR-030: customs/regulatory hold.
Business Impact If treated as one status, customs-cleared bonded stock may remain blocked; or quality-hold stock may be released incorrectly.
Recommendation Maintain separate hold reasons; both exclude from ATP (DEP-002, DEP-003); disposition paths differ.

OV-002 — BR-014 FEFO vs. BR-015 FIFO

Attribute Detail
Overlap Type Mutual Exclusion (by product attribute)
Shared Scope Pick and ship rotation priority
Distinction BR-014 applies to shelf-life products; BR-015 to non-perishable standard goods.
Business Impact Applying wrong rule ships suboptimal lot — expiry write-off (BR-014) or aged stock accumulation (BR-015).
Recommendation Product master must classify rotation rule per SKU; never apply both simultaneously to same product.

OV-003 — BR-019 Independent Count Approval vs. BR-021 Independent Approval for Material Adjustments

Attribute Detail
Overlap Type Scope Overlap
Shared Scope Segregation of duties for inventory adjustments
Distinction BR-019: count-specific (counter ≠ approver). BR-021: value/quantity threshold for any adjustment.
Business Impact Low-value count variance may satisfy BR-019 but not BR-021 threshold — approver rules differ. Material non-count adjustment triggers BR-021 only.
Recommendation Apply both where applicable; BR-021 is superset for materiality; BR-019 always applies to count-originated adjustments regardless of value.

OV-004 — BR-020 Mandatory Reason Codes vs. BR-022 Investigate Before Adjusting

Attribute Detail
Overlap Type Scope Overlap
Shared Scope Adjustment governance
Distinction BR-022: process requirement (investigate first). BR-020: data requirement (reason code).
Business Impact Reason code without investigation produces categorized but unexplained adjustments; investigation without code loses analytical value.
Recommendation Enforce sequence: investigate (BR-022) → reason code reflects finding (BR-020) → approve (BR-019/BR-021).

OV-005 — BR-009 Reorder at Reorder Level vs. BR-032 Class A Priority Monitoring

Attribute Detail
Overlap Type Scope Overlap
Shared Scope Low-stock response intensity
Distinction BR-009: universal threshold trigger. BR-032: heightened frequency and escalation for Class A.
Business Impact Class A stockout if treated with same response speed as Class C; or over-procurement if Class A rules applied to all SKUs.
Recommendation BR-009 sets the trigger; BR-032 modulates response priority and monitoring cadence by classification.

OV-006 — BR-001 ATP-Only Commitment vs. BR-029 Promotional Ring-Fencing

Attribute Detail
Overlap Type Scope Overlap
Shared Scope What quantity may be promised to customers
Distinction BR-001: general ATP arithmetic. BR-029: commercial allocation restriction on subset of ATP.
Business Impact See CF-005 — double-counting available stock across channels.
Recommendation Campaign setup creates explicit ring-fence reservation reducing general ATP.

OV-007 — BR-023 Write-Off Authorization vs. BR-021 Material Adjustment Approval

Attribute Detail
Overlap Type Scope Overlap
Shared Scope Authorization for inventory value removal
Distinction BR-023: evidence and authorization specific to write-offs. BR-021: independent approver for material adjustments generally.
Business Impact Write-off may satisfy BR-023 documentation but still need BR-021 approver if above threshold; or low-value write-off may need BR-023 evidence but not BR-021 escalation.
Recommendation All write-offs require BR-023; material write-offs also require BR-021 independent approver.

OV-008 — BR-025 Return Authorization vs. BR-028 Backorder Acknowledgment

Attribute Detail
Overlap Type Scope Overlap (Principle)
Shared Scope Explicit customer consent before recording commercial inventory state
Distinction BR-025: inbound return acceptance. BR-028: outbound delay acceptance.
Business Impact Inconsistent consent standards between returns and backorders erode customer trust policy coherence.
Recommendation Unified "customer acknowledgment required" policy in training; separate process paths.

Part III — Use Cases

Use Case Catalog

Inventory Management System

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-UC-001
Document Title Use Case Catalog — Inventory Management System
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Senior Business Analyst
Source Documents BRD-IMS-001 (v1.0), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rule Catalog, v1.0)
Date July 5, 2026
Scope Business interactions only — workflow steps are documented separately

Purpose

This catalog identifies every business use case for the Inventory Management System derived from the approved Business Requirements Document and Business Rule Catalog. Each use case describes a meaningful interaction between business actors and the system to achieve a defined business goal. Detailed workflows are out of scope for this document.

BR-xxx Business Rule (SRS-BR-001 / BRD Section 13)

Domain 1: Master Data & Governance

UC-001 — Manage Product Master Data

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-001
Use Case Name Manage Product Master Data
Goal Establish and maintain accurate, unique product identity records so all inventory operations reference a single trusted SKU definition across the network.
Primary Actor Inventory Controller
Supporting Actors Operations Director, Warehouse Manager, Purchasing Manager, Sales Manager
Trigger A new product is introduced, an existing product attribute requires correction, or duplicate product records are detected.
Business Process BP-01 — Product Master Data Management
Related Functional Requirements FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, FR-004
Related Business Rules BR-027 (No Reorder of Discontinued Products)

UC-002 — Configure Inventory Locations

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-002
Use Case Name Configure Inventory Locations
Goal Define and maintain the inventory location network so stock can be assigned, tracked, and reported by warehouse, store, or distribution point.
Primary Actor Inventory Controller
Supporting Actors Operations Director, Warehouse Manager, Regional / Store Manager, Finance Manager
Trigger A new location is opened, location hierarchy changes, a location requires closure planning, or opening stock balances must be established at go-live.
Business Process BP-02 — Location & Warehouse Setup
Related Functional Requirements FR-005, FR-006, FR-007, FR-010
Related Business Rules —

UC-003 — Define Stock Policies and Thresholds

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-003
Use Case Name Define Stock Policies and Thresholds
Goal Set reorder levels, minimum thresholds, and safety stock policies so replenishment and availability monitoring reflect business service-level targets.
Primary Actor Inventory Controller
Supporting Actors Purchasing Manager, Operations Director, Warehouse Manager
Trigger A new product is onboarded, demand or lead-time assumptions change, or replenishment performance indicates threshold recalibration is needed.
Business Process BP-03 — Stock Policy & Threshold Definition
Related Functional Requirements FR-008
Related Business Rules BR-009 (Reorder at Reorder Level), BR-010 (Safety Stock Protection)

UC-004 — Classify Products by ABC Priority

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-004
Use Case Name Classify Products by ABC Priority
Goal Segment products by business importance so operational effort, count frequency, and monitoring intensity focus on high-impact SKUs.
Primary Actor Inventory Controller
Supporting Actors Operations Director, Purchasing Manager, Sales Manager, Finance Manager
Trigger Periodic classification review cycle, significant shift in product velocity or revenue contribution, or new product portfolio expansion.
Business Process BP-04 — ABC Product Classification
Related Functional Requirements FR-009
Related Business Rules BR-032 (Class A Priority Monitoring)

UC-005 — Maintain Governance Policies and Reason Codes

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-005
Use Case Name Maintain Governance Policies and Reason Codes
Goal Define standardized reason codes and inventory governance policies that govern adjustments, exceptions, and accountability across all locations.
Primary Actor Inventory Controller
Supporting Actors Operations Director, Internal Auditor, Finance Manager
Trigger New exception categories emerge, audit findings require policy updates, or reason code taxonomy needs expansion or consolidation.
Business Process BP-01 — Product Master Data Management; BP-03 — Stock Policy & Threshold Definition
Related Functional Requirements FR-011, FR-012
Related Business Rules BR-020 (Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes)

Domain 2: Inbound & Receiving

UC-006 — Place and Manage Purchase Orders

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-006
Use Case Name Place and Manage Purchase Orders
Goal Create authorized commercial commitments to suppliers that define what will be ordered, enabling controlled inbound supply and financial accountability.
Primary Actor Buyer
Supporting Actors Purchasing Manager, Supplier / Vendor, Finance Manager, Receiving Clerk
Trigger Replenishment planning identifies a purchase need, safety stock is breached, or an existing purchase order requires amendment or cancellation.
Business Process BP-05 — Purchase Order Placement
Related Functional Requirements FR-013, FR-021, FR-022
Related Business Rules BR-007 (Purchase Order Required for Supplier Receipt), BR-008 (Three-Way Match Before Payment), BR-027 (No Reorder of Discontinued Products)

UC-007 — Plan Expected Inbound Deliveries

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-007
Use Case Name Plan Expected Inbound Deliveries
Goal Communicate and track expected supplier deliveries so receiving operations and replenishment planners can anticipate inbound supply.
Primary Actor Buyer
Supporting Actors Warehouse Manager, Receiving Clerk, Supplier / Vendor, Logistics / Carrier Partner
Trigger A purchase order is confirmed, supplier communicates shipment schedule, or inbound delivery timing changes.
Business Process BP-06 — Inbound Shipment Planning
Related Functional Requirements FR-014, FR-055
Related Business Rules —

UC-008 — Receive and Verify Supplier Goods

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-008
Use Case Name Receive and Verify Supplier Goods
Goal Confirm quantity, product identity, and condition of inbound supplier shipments before stock is accepted into inventory records.
Primary Actor Receiving Clerk
Supporting Actors Supplier / Vendor, Warehouse Manager, Buyer, Logistics / Carrier Partner
Trigger A supplier shipment arrives at the receiving dock with purchase order or authorized receipt documentation.
Business Process BP-07 — Goods Receipt & Verification
Related Functional Requirements FR-015, FR-017, FR-003
Related Business Rules BR-004 (Verify Before Inventory Acceptance), BR-007 (Purchase Order Required for Supplier Receipt), BR-016 (Minimum Remaining Shelf Life at Receipt), BR-017 (Lot or Batch Capture for Traceable Products), BR-030 (Bonded Inventory Customs Clearance)

UC-009 — Document and Resolve Receipt Discrepancies

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-009
Use Case Name Document and Resolve Receipt Discrepancies
Goal Record and resolve differences between expected and received goods while preserving supplier accountability and evidence for claims.
Primary Actor Receiving Clerk
Supporting Actors Warehouse Manager, Buyer, Supplier / Vendor, Finance Manager
Trigger Verification identifies short shipment, over-shipment, wrong item, damage, or shelf-life non-compliance at receipt.
Business Process BP-08 — Receipt Discrepancy Resolution
Related Functional Requirements FR-016, FR-020
Related Business Rules BR-006 (Document Receipt Discrepancies), BR-008 (Three-Way Match Before Payment), BR-016 (Minimum Remaining Shelf Life at Receipt)

UC-010 — Perform Stock Put-Away

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-010
Use Case Name Perform Stock Put-Away
Goal Move verified received goods to designated storage locations and confirm availability for sale and fulfillment.
Primary Actor Warehouse Staff
Supporting Actors Receiving Clerk, Warehouse Manager, Warehouse Picker / Packer
Trigger Goods receipt verification is complete and stock awaits placement in storage.
Business Process BP-09 — Stock Put-Away & Storage
Related Functional Requirements FR-018
Related Business Rules BR-005 (Put-Away Before Availability), BR-014 (FEFO Rotation for Shelf-Life Products), BR-015 (FIFO Rotation for Standard Goods), BR-030 (Bonded Inventory Customs Clearance)

UC-011 — Receive Return and Non-PO Inbound Stock

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-011
Use Case Name Receive Return and Non-PO Inbound Stock
Goal Accept and record inbound stock that arrives without a standard purchase order, including customer returns and approved ad-hoc receipts.
Primary Actor Receiving Clerk
Supporting Actors Customer Service Representative, Warehouse Manager, Inventory Controller
Trigger Customer return shipment arrives, approved ad-hoc receipt is authorized, or non-PO inbound stock requires recording.
Business Process BP-07 — Goods Receipt & Verification; BP-27 — Customer Return Intake
Related Functional Requirements FR-019
Related Business Rules BR-004 (Verify Before Inventory Acceptance), BR-025 (Return Authorization Required)

UC-012 — Monitor Inventory Status

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-012
Use Case Name Monitor Inventory Status
Goal Continuously observe stock levels and status indicators across locations to detect low stock, out-of-stock, and overstock conditions proactively.
Primary Actor Inventory Controller
Supporting Actors Operations Director, Warehouse Manager, Purchasing Manager
Trigger Scheduled monitoring cycle, threshold breach, or management request for inventory health review.

UC-013 — Inquire Inventory Availability

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-013
Use Case Name Inquire Inventory Availability
Goal Provide accurate on-hand, reserved, and available-to-promise visibility to support sales conversations, customer service, and fulfillment planning without warehouse escalation.
Primary Actor Sales Representative
Supporting Actors Customer Service Representative, Sales Manager, B2B Customer, B2C Customer
Trigger Customer or internal stakeholder requests stock availability, product lookup, or network-wide availability check.
Business Process BP-10 — Inventory Status Monitoring; BP-16 — Order Availability Confirmation
Related Functional Requirements FR-023, FR-024, FR-025, FR-027, FR-028
Related Business Rules BR-001 (ATP-Only Customer Commitment)

Domain 4: Inventory Control & Accuracy

UC-014 — Perform Cycle Count

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-014
Use Case Name Perform Cycle Count
Goal Verify physical stock against system records through scheduled partial counts without disrupting full warehouse operations.
Primary Actor Warehouse Staff
Supporting Actors Inventory Controller, Warehouse Manager
Trigger Cycle count schedule assigns products or locations for counting, or Class A SKU requires elevated count frequency.
Business Process BP-11 — Cycle Counting

Related Business Rules BR-018 (Blind Cycle Counting), BR-032 (Class A Priority Monitoring)

UC-015 — Conduct Full Physical Inventory Count

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-015
Use Case Name Conduct Full Physical Inventory Count
Goal Execute a comprehensive wall-to-wall physical count at a location to establish authoritative inventory accuracy baseline.
Primary Actor Inventory Controller
Supporting Actors Warehouse Manager, Warehouse Staff, Operations Director, Finance Manager
Trigger Annual or periodic full count cycle, location go-live cutover, or audit-mandated physical verification.
Business Process BP-12 — Full Physical Inventory Count
Related Functional Requirements FR-032
Related Business Rules BR-024 (Physical Inventory Freeze)

UC-016 — Investigate and Approve Count Variances

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-016
Use Case Name Investigate and Approve Count Variances
Goal Investigate root causes of count discrepancies and obtain independent approval before adjusting system records.
Primary Actor Warehouse Manager
Supporting Actors Inventory Controller, Operations Director, Warehouse Staff
Trigger Cycle count or physical count identifies variance between system quantity and physical quantity.
Business Process BP-13 — Count Variance Investigation & Approval
Related Functional Requirements FR-033, FR-034
Related Business Rules BR-019 (Independent Count Approval), BR-021 (Independent Approval for Material Adjustments), BR-022 (Investigate Before Adjusting)

UC-017 — Process Stock Adjustments

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-017
Use Case Name Process Stock Adjustments
Goal Correct recorded inventory quantities with mandatory reason codes and appropriate authorization when physical reality differs from system records.
Primary Actor Warehouse Manager
Supporting Actors Inventory Controller, Operations Director, Warehouse Staff
Trigger Approved count variance, identified damage, misplacement, or other correction requiring quantity change.
Business Process BP-14 — Stock Adjustment & Write-Off
Related Functional Requirements FR-035, FR-037
Related Business Rules BR-020 (Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes), BR-021 (Independent Approval for Material Adjustments), BR-022 (Investigate Before Adjusting)

UC-018 — Authorize and Process Inventory Write-Offs

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-018
Use Case Name Authorize and Process Inventory Write-Offs
Goal Formally remove inventory value for damaged, obsolete, or lost goods with documented evidence and authorized approval.
Primary Actor Operations Director
Supporting Actors Finance Manager, Inventory Controller, Warehouse Manager
Trigger Goods are confirmed damaged beyond resale, obsolete, expired, or lost and require permanent removal from inventory.
Business Process BP-14 — Stock Adjustment & Write-Off; BP-15 — Shrinkage & Loss Management
Related Functional Requirements FR-036
Related Business Rules BR-023 (Documented Write-Off Authorization), BR-020 (Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes)

UC-019 — Manage Quarantine and Hold Stock

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-019
Use Case Name Manage Quarantine and Hold Stock
Goal Place inventory under quality hold or regulatory restriction and exclude it from sellable availability until cleared or dispositioned.
Primary Actor Warehouse Manager
Supporting Actors Inventory Controller, Operations Director, Regulatory Authority
Trigger Quality concern, recall, customs hold, investigation requirement, or bonded inventory pending clearance.
Business Process BP-14 — Stock Adjustment & Write-Off; BP-20 — Outbound Exception Handling
Related Functional Requirements FR-038
Related Business Rules BR-013 (Quarantine Exclusion from Sellable Stock), BR-030 (Bonded Inventory Customs Clearance)

UC-020 — Analyze Shrinkage, Loss, and Obsolete Stock

Attribute Detail
Use Case ID UC-020
Use Case Name Analyze Shrinkage, Loss, and Obsolete Stock
Goal Identify shrinkage patterns, loss trends, and slow-moving or obsolete inventory to drive corrective action and working capital optimization.
Primary Actor Inventory Controller
Supporting Actors Finance Manager, Operations Director, Purchasing Manager, Warehouse Manager
Trigger Periodic shrinkage review, rising adjustment volumes, or aging inventory exceeds policy thresholds.
Business Process BP-15 — Shrinkage & Loss Management
Related Functional Requirements FR-039, FR-040
Related Business Rules BR-020 (Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes), BR-027 (No Reorder of Discontinued Products)

Primary Actor Customer Service Representative
Supporting Actors Sales Representative, Warehouse Manager, Warehouse Picker / Packer
Trigger Customer order is confirmed for fulfillment after availability validation.
