ADR-001: Modular Monolith as Deployment Topology

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-001
Title Modular Monolith as Deployment Topology
Status Accepted

Context

The IMS must support 13 bounded contexts, 18 aggregates, and 81 domain events while operating under a fixed initiative budget (BC-01) and limited internal IT capacity (ORC-04). The organization requires phased delivery (MVP Months 0–6) without operational shutdown at go-live (OC-01). Strategic domain design (SRS-DM-007) defines clear context boundaries, but bounded contexts are explicitly not microservice boundaries.

The team must choose a deployment topology that balances domain alignment, operational simplicity, Stock Position consistency, and a credible path to future scale.

Decision

Deploy the Inventory Management System as a single modular monolith — one deployable application composed of 13 loosely coupled modules aligned to bounded contexts, with compile-time boundary enforcement and a decomposition-ready interface surface.

Microservices are deferred until volume metrics and operational maturity justify selective extraction (Inventory Intelligence, integration gateway).

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Microservices (13 services) Distributed consistency risk on Stock Position; ops overhead exceeds ORC-04; premature with 16 open domain hotspots
Traditional layered monolith No bounded-context boundaries; high coupling; rules scatter across layers
Service-oriented (few coarse services) Arbitrary split; still distributed ops without clear domain mapping

Consequences

Positive

  • Single deployment pipeline and runtime — lower ops cost
  • ACID transactions within aggregate and in-process saga steps
  • Faster MVP delivery and cross-module refactoring
  • Module interfaces preserved for future extraction

Negative

  • Shared runtime blast radius — defect in one module can affect availability
  • Cannot independently scale Stock Position writes vs. reporting without read-side separation (mitigated by ADR-007)
  • Requires discipline to prevent module boundary erosion

Neutral

  • Team structure should align to core modules but shares one codebase

ADR-002: Domain-Driven Design with Bounded Context Modules

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-002
Title Domain-Driven Design with Bounded Context Modules
Status Accepted

Context

Domain analysis produced 13 bounded contexts, 18 aggregates, 24 domain services, 81 domain events, and 72 ubiquitous language terms. Business rules (BR-001 – BR-032) and segregation-of-duties requirements span multiple stakeholder functions (warehouse, purchasing, finance, marketing). A purely technical decomposition (UI / service / data layers only) cannot preserve domain integrity.

Decision

Adopt Domain-Driven Design (DDD) as the strategic and tactical design approach. Each bounded context maps 1:1 to a system module (M-01 through M-13). Aggregates define consistency boundaries. Cross-context integration uses published language identifiers, domain events, and application-layer ports — never shared mutable domain objects.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
CRUD-centric data model Cannot express 32 business rules, SoD, and event choreography
Transaction script pattern Business logic scatters; untestable rule enforcement
Anemic domain model with service layer only Invariants not protected at aggregate boundaries

Consequences

Positive

  • Direct traceability from BRD → domain model → modules → code
  • Independent change velocity per context (catalog vs. balance vs. governance)
  • Ubiquitous language (SRS-DM-008) drives API and code naming

Negative

  • Higher initial design investment; DDD skill required across squads
  • Cross-context workflows require explicit integration design (events, sagas)

Neutral

  • Generic subdomains (Identity) may use simpler patterns within DDD module structure

ADR-003: Clean/Hexagonal Internal Layer Structure

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-003
Title Clean/Hexagonal Internal Layer Structure
Status Accepted

Context

Each of the 13 modules requires internal organization that protects domain rules from infrastructure concerns (ORM, HTTP, SSO, messaging) while supporting testability and ACL adapters for external systems. Multiple layering models (Layered, Clean, Hexagonal, Onion) were evaluated (SRS-SA-002).

Decision

Apply Clean Architecture with Hexagonal ports and adapters inside every module:

  • Domain (center): aggregates, value objects, domain events, repository interfaces
  • Application: command/query handlers, sagas, authorization behaviors
  • Presentation (per module API package): REST controllers, DTOs
  • Infrastructure: JPA repositories, ACL adapters, event bus, cache

Dependency rule: source dependencies point inward only. Frameworks are details in infrastructure.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Layered only (UI → Service → DAO) Domain logic leaks; insufficient port/adapter isolation
Clean without hexagonal ports Weaker external integration boundary protection
No internal layers (flat packages) Unmaintainable at 13 modules × 48 use cases

Consequences

Positive

  • Domain testable without database or HTTP
  • ACL adapters cleanly isolated for CRM and Finance
  • Consistent structure across all squads

Negative

  • Mapping boilerplate (DTO ↔ command ↔ domain) — mitigated by MapStruct
  • Learning curve for teams accustomed to annotation-driven MVC only

ADR-004: Inventory Balance as Sole Quantity Authority

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-004
Title Inventory Balance as Sole Quantity Authority
Status Accepted

Context

The system's core value is answering what do we have, where, and what is available? Multiple modules mutate stock-related state (receiving, fulfillment, transfers, adjustments, returns, campaigns). Without a single authority, ATP can diverge — causing overselling (BR-001), audit failures (BO-19), and customer trust loss.

Domain model review (SRS-DM-009) confirms Stock Position as the core domain center of gravity.

Decision

Module M-04 (Inventory Balance) is the sole mutator of on-hand, reserved, quarantined, and ATP quantities. All other modules request quantity changes via commands, domain events, or sagas — they never write to balance tables or hold mutable quantity state.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Distributed quantity ownership (fulfillment owns reservation table, balance owns on-hand) Split-brain ATP; HS-007 reservation coordination risk
Shared stock tables accessed by all modules No aggregate protection; invariant violations
Event sourcing as sole write model Higher complexity; team maturity and BC-01 constraints

Consequences

Positive

  • Single mathematical invariant: ATP = on-hand − reserved − quarantined
  • Clear audit chain for all quantity changes
  • Contention localized to Stock Position aggregate (product-location scope)

Negative

  • M-04 becomes highest-contention module — requires optimistic locking and caching
  • All quantity workflows have dependency on Balance module availability

ADR-005: Event-Driven Cross-Module Integration

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-005
Title Event-Driven Cross-Module Integration
Status Accepted

Context

Event storming identified 81 domain events and 12 end-to-end lifecycles with policy chains (e.g., put-away → stock available → backorder fulfill). Synchronous coupling of all 13 modules would create fragile call chains, threaten NFR-PERF-002 (2s ATP), and embed reporting inside transactional paths.

Decision

Use domain event choreography as the primary cross-module state propagation mechanism. Modules publish domain events after successful aggregate commits. Subscribing modules react via application-layer event handlers. Synchronous cross-module calls are limited to read-only queries and saga command steps requiring immediate confirmation.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Pure synchronous orchestration Tight coupling; hot-path latency; cascading failures
Shared database triggers Hidden logic; untestable; violates module ownership
Central orchestration engine (ESB) Over-engineering; BC-01; ORC-04

Consequences

Positive

  • Loose coupling; new subscribers (Intelligence, alerts) without publisher changes
  • Natural audit trail from event stream
  • Aligns with ADR-007 CQRS projections

Negative

  • Eventual consistency between modules — requires saga compensation (ADR-008)
  • Event schema versioning discipline required
  • Debugging distributed flows harder than single call stack — mitigated by correlation IDs

ADR-006: Transactional Outbox for Reliable Event Delivery

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-006
Title Transactional Outbox for Reliable Event Delivery
Status Accepted

Context

NFR-REL-007 requires ≤15-minute recoverable data loss. NFR-BDR-001 requires continuous transaction protection. Publishing domain events after database commit creates a dual-write risk — crash between commit and publish loses events, causing Stock Position and Intelligence projections to diverge from operational truth.

Decision

Implement the transactional outbox pattern — domain events are persisted to an outbox table in the same database transaction as the aggregate save. A separate dispatcher publishes events after commit. Handlers must be idempotent (deduplicate by EventId).

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Publish-then-save Inconsistent on failure
XA two-phase commit Performance penalty; operational complexity
Change Data Capture (Debezium) Additional ops infrastructure for MVP

Consequences

Positive

  • At-least-once delivery with atomic write + event record
  • Outbox table in PostgreSQL — no additional broker required for MVP
  • Ready for external broker relay in Phase 2

Negative

  • Outbox table growth — requires archival job
  • Slight latency between commit and handler execution (acceptable per SRS-SA-005)

ADR-007: CQRS for Inventory Intelligence

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-007
Title CQRS for Inventory Intelligence
Status Accepted

Context

M-13 Inventory Intelligence owns dashboards, KPIs, movement history, audit trail, and valuation snapshots — with no write aggregates. Running reporting queries against transactional Stock Position tables risks dock performance degradation (AR-10) and violates NFR-PERF-002/PERF-004. Intelligence has fundamentally different read-heavy, eventually consistent NFR profile.

Decision

Apply Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS) for the Intelligence concern:

  • Commands mutate aggregates in transactional modules (M-01 – M-12)
  • Queries for dashboards, audit, KPIs, and ATP display read from dedicated read projections maintained by event handlers in M-13
  • Read models are rebuildable from domain event history

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Single model (JPA entities for everything) Reporting load on write tables
Database views only Limited application-level composition; coupling to write schema
Separate reporting database via ETL batch Stale data; complex pipeline for MVP

Consequences

Positive

  • Write path protected for fulfillment and receiving performance
  • Intelligence module extractable to separate service in Phase 3
  • Audit trail append-only and query-optimized

Negative

  • Eventual consistency on dashboards (seconds lag — acceptable)
  • Projection rebuild complexity on schema evolution
  • Second data access pattern (jOOQ) in Intelligence module

ADR-008: Saga Pattern for Cross-Module Workflows

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-008
Title Saga Pattern for Cross-Module Workflows
Status Accepted

Context

Business workflows span multiple aggregates and modules: order confirm → reserve stock, put-away → stock increase, transfer dispatch → source deduct + destination increase, physical count → freeze → adjust. DDD rule "one transaction, one aggregate" prohibits single ACID transaction across modules. Hotspot HS-007 highlights partial failure risk when order confirms but reservation fails.

Decision

Implement orchestrated sagas in the calling module's application layer for cross-module workflows. Each saga step is its own transaction. Define explicit compensation actions for each step failure. Critical sagas: SAG-01 (order confirm-reserve), SAG-04 (physical count-freeze), SAG-05 (opening balance go-live).

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Distributed two-phase commit Impractical across modules; performance and availability impact
Choreography only (no orchestrator) Hard to trace and compensate multi-step failures
Manual reconciliation Unacceptable for ATP integrity and customer orders

Consequences

Positive

  • Clear failure handling and compensation paths
  • Each step remains single-aggregate ACID
  • Testable with integration tests per saga

Negative

  • Saga state management adds application complexity
  • Compensation logic must be carefully designed to avoid orphaned state
  • Requires HS-007 workshop for reservation failure policy

ADR-009: Stock Position Identity per Product-Location

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-009
Title Stock Position Identity per Product-Location
Status Proposed

Context

Domain model review (P1-05) and hotspot HS-005 identify a fundamental fork: Stock Position identity as product + location with embedded Lot/Batch child entities, versus product + location + lot as separate positions. This decision affects reservation, pick, cycle count, transfer, and persistence design across all operational modules.

Decision

Adopt one Stock Position aggregate per product-location. Lot/Batch entities are child entities within the aggregate holding sub-quantities. ATP at root = sum of sellable lot quantities minus holds. Traceable products require lot capture on all movements (BR-017).

Pending confirmation at architecture gate workshop with Quality and Warehouse stakeholders.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
One Stock Position per product-location-lot Explosion of aggregates; complex network ATP aggregation
Lot-less Stock Position for all products Violates BR-017 for traceable products

Consequences

Positive

  • Single ATP query point per SKU per location
  • Lot quantities enforced to sum to on-hand invariant
  • Aligns with FEFO pick selection within aggregate

Negative

  • Larger aggregate for high-lot-count products — lock contention risk
  • Pending business confirmation — blocks detailed Balance module design until Accepted

ADR-010: Location Freeze Authority Split

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-010
Title Location Freeze Authority Split
Status Proposed

Context

BR-024 requires location freeze during wall-to-wall physical inventory count. Hotspot HS-003 and finding P1-03 identify dual ownership risk: Physical Inventory Count aggregate initiates freeze while Inventory Location aggregate also lists freeze enforcement. Two writers could cause race conditions at count certification.

Decision

Physical Inventory Count (M-09) initiates freeze via LocationFreezeImposed event. Inventory Location (M-02) holds the authoritative frozen flag and applies/releases state. All operational modules consult M-02 IsLocationFrozen query only — never M-09 directly.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Freeze owned only by Physical Count module Network module cannot enforce freeze for non-count scenarios
Freeze duplicated in both aggregates Race conditions; inconsistent state

Consequences

Positive

  • Single authoritative freeze read point (Freeze Guard DS-014)
  • Clear event-driven handoff between accuracy and network modules

Negative

  • Eventual consistency window between impose event and flag apply — must be sub-second
  • Emergency override policy still requires business workshop

ADR-011: Promotional Ring-Fence via Domain Events

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-011
Title Promotional Ring-Fence via Domain Events
Status Accepted

Context

Finding P1-02 and hotspot HS-004 identify dual ownership risk for promotional ATP segregation. Commercial Campaign and Inventory Balance both reference ring-fenced quantity. BR-029 requires ring-fencing during campaigns without corrupting general ATP.

Decision

M-11 Commercial Campaign owns allocation intent and lifecycle. M-04 Inventory Balance owns ATP mechanics. Campaign publishes PromotionalStockAllocated / PromotionalAllocationReleased events. Balance reacts by segregating/restoring ATP — never self-initiates ring-fence.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Ring-fence logic only in Stock Position Marketing lifecycle coupled to core domain
Shared mutable segregation table Dual writers; inconsistent ATP

Consequences

Positive

  • Clear ownership aligned to stakeholder functions (Marketing vs. Operations)
  • Phase 2 campaign module independently evolvable

Negative

  • Brief eventual consistency between allocation command and ATP segregation
  • Override rules (MR-10) require business policy workshop

ADR-012: Anti-Corruption Layers for External Systems

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-012
Title Anti-Corruption Layers for External Systems
Status Accepted

Context

IMS integrates with Sales/CRM (EXT-01), Finance ERP (EXT-02), Sales Channel (EXT-03), Marketing (EXT-07), and HR Directory (EXT-08). External systems have foreign domain models, lifecycles, and authority boundaries. BRD scope excludes full CRM and GL ownership from IMS. Absorbing foreign models corrupts fulfillment and balance domains.

Decision

Implement Anti-Corruption Layers (ACL) as infrastructure adapters at module boundaries:

External System ACL Location Translates To
Sales/CRM M-07 Fulfillment ImportCustomerOrder command
Finance ERP M-13 Intelligence Valuation snapshot export format
Finance ERP M-06 Inbound Match status (HS-014)
Marketing M-11 Campaign CreatePromotionalAllocation
HR Directory M-12 Identity ProvisionUserAccount

Foreign models never enter the domain layer.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Shared canonical enterprise data model Multi-year integration program; out of BC-01 scope
Direct CRM entity mapping to JPA Couples fulfillment to CRM schema changes
Point-to-point API calls without ACL Foreign concepts leak into application layer

Consequences

Positive

  • IMS domain remains stable when CRM or ERP changes
  • Phased integration depth (manual MVP → API Phase 2) without domain rewrite

Negative

  • ACL maintenance overhead per external system
  • Mapping logic requires tests and versioning

ADR-013: IMS as Operational System of Record

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-013
Title IMS as Operational System of Record
Status Accepted

Context

Hotspot HS-014 questions whether IMS or Finance ERP owns supplier invoicing, three-way match, and valuation. BRD positions IMS as inventory system of record (TEC-01). Finance owns GL and payment authority. ~8% current valuation variance must reduce to ≤2% (BO-18).

Decision

IMS is the operational system of record for stock quantities, movements, reservations, receipt facts, and operational match outcomes. Finance ERP remains financial system of record for GL postings and payment authorization. IMS publishes valuation snapshots and movement facts via ACL; Finance publishes GL balance for reconciliation.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
ERP owns all financial inventory IMS cannot enforce BR-004 – BR-008 at dock speed
IMS owns payment authorization Outside BRD scope; duplicates ERP

Consequences

Positive

  • Clear data ownership boundaries
  • Warehouse operations not blocked by ERP availability

Negative

  • Reconciliation workflow required (Phase 3 automation)
  • Temporary manual finance export in MVP (TEC-05)

ADR-014: Java Spring Boot Backend Stack

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-014
Title Java Spring Boot Backend Stack
Status Accepted

Context

Organization mandates Java and Spring. IMS requires enterprise-grade security, transaction management, REST APIs, and integration with PostgreSQL. Team hiring and supportability favor mainstream stack. Virtual threads in Java 21 benefit I/O-bound warehouse workloads.

Decision

Adopt Java 21 LTS with Spring Boot 3.x as the backend runtime — including Spring Web, Spring Security, Spring Data JPA, and Spring Modulith (ADR-015).

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Quarkus Less Modulith maturity; not mandated
.NET Diverges from Java mandate
Java EE/Jakarta EE standalone More ceremony than Spring Boot

Consequences

Positive

  • Mandate compliance; large hiring pool; mature ecosystem
  • Spring Boot Test, Actuator, and security integration

Negative

  • Heavier runtime than Quarkus — acceptable for enterprise deployment
  • Requires discipline to avoid Spring MVC + JPA anemic pattern

ADR-015: Spring Modulith for Module Boundary Enforcement

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-015
Title Spring Modulith for Module Boundary Enforcement
Status Accepted

Context

ADR-001 modular monolith requires enforceable boundaries between 13 bounded contexts. Package naming alone is insufficient — ArchUnit helps but Spring Modulith provides first-class module APIs, event publication, JDBC event registry, and ApplicationModuleTest verification.

Decision

Use Spring Modulith to structure the modular monolith — module definitions, allowed dependencies, module-scoped events, and integration with transactional outbox.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
ArchUnit only No built-in event/outbox support
OSGi Obsolete complexity
Manual package conventions Not compile-time verifiable

Consequences

Positive

  • Architecture enforced in CI via module tests
  • Event infrastructure aligned to DDD modules

Negative

  • Newer Spring project — smaller community reference base
  • Team training in Sprint 0 required

ADR-016: Angular SPA and PWA Frontend

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-016
Title Angular SPA and PWA Frontend
Status Accepted

Context

Organization mandates Angular. IMS serves 19 user roles across office and warehouse with 90 functional requirements. TEC-03 excludes offline MVP. Warehouse staff need mobile-friendly interfaces without maintaining separate native apps under BC-01.

Decision

Build a single Angular 19 SPA with Angular Material, lazy-loaded feature modules per bounded context, and PWA capabilities for warehouse mobile (installable, responsive, barcode-ready).

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
React Not mandated
Separate native mobile apps Cost and dual codebase
Server-rendered only (Thymeleaf) Poor mobile UX for warehouse

Consequences

Positive

  • One frontend codebase; mandate compliance; enterprise structure
  • OpenAPI-generated TypeScript clients possible

Negative

  • Large bundle — mitigated by lazy loading
  • PWA limitations on specialized scanner hardware — Capacitor in Phase 2 if needed

ADR-017: PostgreSQL as Primary Database

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-017
Title PostgreSQL as Primary Database
Status Accepted

Context

Organization mandates PostgreSQL. IMS requires ACID transactions for Stock Position, JSONB for event payloads, row-level locking for reservation contention, 7-year retention (NFR-COM-019), and ≤15-minute RPO (NFR-BDR-001). Fixed budget favors open-source database.

Decision

Use PostgreSQL 16 as the sole primary relational database for transactional writes, outbox, read projections, and audit storage.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
SQL Server / Oracle Licensing cost (BC-01)
MySQL Weaker JSON and constraint ecosystem
MongoDB Poor fit for ATP transactional integrity

Consequences

Positive

  • Mandate compliance; ACID; JSONB; logical replication for read scaling
  • Testcontainers parity in CI

Negative

  • Write scaling vertical — acceptable for MVP–Phase 2 scale
  • DBA tuning (vacuum, indexes) required for ATP hot paths

ADR-018: Schema-per-Module Database Organization

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-018
Title Schema-per-Module Database Organization
Status Accepted

Context

ADR-002 defines 13 modules with exclusive aggregate ownership. Module boundary rule MB-07 prohibits shared tables. Single PostgreSQL instance required for operational simplicity (ORC-04) and ACID within monolith.

Decision

Each module owns tables in a dedicated PostgreSQL schema (catalog, balance, fulfillment, etc.). Flyway migrations are per-module. No cross-schema foreign keys except shared kernel reference tables (product_sku, location_code).

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Single flat schema No ownership enforcement
Database per module Microservices ops overhead

Consequences

Positive

  • Clear data ownership; extraction-ready
  • Single backup and instance management

Negative

  • Cross-schema queries discouraged — use module ports
  • Migration coordination on shared kernel changes

ADR-019: JPA for Writes, jOOQ for Intelligence Reads

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-019
Title JPA for Writes, jOOQ for Intelligence Reads
Status Accepted

Context

ADR-007 CQRS separates write and read paths. Write side requires aggregate mapping with optimistic locking. Intelligence module requires complex KPI aggregations, audit search, and dashboard queries that should not load JPA entity graphs (AR-10).

Decision

Use Hibernate 6 / Spring Data JPA for transactional module write repositories only. Use jOOQ exclusively in M-13 Intelligence for read projections and reports.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
JPA for all queries Performance and coupling risk on reporting
jOOQ for all modules Verbose aggregate persistence; loses optimistic locking conventions
MyBatis Less Spring Boot native integration

Consequences

Positive

  • Right tool per path; type-safe SQL for reports
  • Domain layer remains ORM-free

Negative

  • Two data access patterns — confined to clear module boundary
  • jOOQ schema codegen pipeline required

ADR-020: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC with JWT Resource Server

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-020
Title OAuth 2.0 / OIDC with JWT Resource Server
Status Accepted

Context

NFR-SEC-001 requires unique user authentication. NFR-SEC-005 – SEC-009 require RBAC and location-scoped permissions. Enterprise IdP (SVC-01) expected. Angular SPA requires token-based API auth. 19 roles and 20 SoD rules must be enforced.

Decision

Integrate OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect with enterprise IdP. Spring Security JWT resource server validates bearer tokens on every API request. Angular uses angular-oauth2-oidc. Authorization enforced in application layer via M-12 Identity ports.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Session-only form login No SSO; poor SPA scaling
SAML only Heavier SPA integration than OIDC
API keys No user attribution

Consequences

Positive

  • Enterprise SSO; stateless API; horizontal scaling
  • Mandate-aligned security posture

Negative

  • Token revocation requires short TTL or blocklist on deprovision
  • IdP role mapping to 100 IMS permissions requires governance

ADR-021: Redis Cache for ATP Hot Path

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-021
Title Redis Cache for ATP Hot Path
Status Accepted

Context

NFR-PERF-002 requires ≥98% of ATP lookups within 2 seconds. Stock Position is high-read, high-write contention aggregate. CS and sales conduct live availability inquiries during customer calls (BO-16). PostgreSQL alone may insufficient under peak concurrent reads.

Decision

Deploy Redis as distributed cache for ATP by SKU/location. Cache invalidated on every Balance domain event affecting quantities. Cached responses include asOf timestamp. Cache miss falls through to authoritative read repository — never default to zero.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
In-process Caffeine only Invalid with multiple app instances
PostgreSQL materialized views only Refresh lag; write coupling
No cache Risk of NFR-PERF-002 breach at scale

Consequences

Positive

  • Sub-millisecond reads for hot SKUs
  • Event invalidation preserves BR-001 integrity

Negative

  • Additional infrastructure component
  • Staleness risk if invalidation fails — monitor and alert

ADR-022: In-Process Messaging for MVP

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-022
Title In-Process Messaging for MVP
Status Accepted

Context

ADR-005 event-driven integration requires message transport. ORC-04 limits ops capacity. MVP modular monolith does not require cross-process messaging. External CRM and channel integration deferred to Phase 2 (TEC-04).

Decision

Use Spring Application Events / Spring Modulith event API with transactional outbox for MVP internal messaging. Defer external message broker (RabbitMQ recommended) to Phase 2 when CRM API and channel feeds require cross-process async integration.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Kafka from day one Ops overhead; overkill for monolith MVP
RabbitMQ from day one Additional infra without external consumers
Synchronous only Violates ADR-005; couples modules

Consequences

Positive

  • Zero broker ops for MVP; simpler debugging
  • Outbox schema ready for broker relay

Negative

  • Cannot horizontally scale event consumers independently in MVP
  • Phase 2 migration requires broker introduction and handler compatibility testing

ADR-023: Published Language for Cross-Boundary References

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-023
Title Published Language for Cross-Boundary References
Status Accepted

Context

13 modules and external systems must reference products, locations, users, and orders without sharing domain entity types. DDD strategic design requires identity-only references between aggregates and contexts.

Decision

Define a shared kernel of immutable identifier value types: ProductSku, LocationCode, UserId, SupplierCode, and standard event envelope (EventId, CorrelationId, OccurredAt). All cross-module and ACL integrations use published language only — no foreign aggregate imports.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Shared entity library Couples module lifecycles; lazy-loading leaks
Primitive strings only No type safety; conflation of identifiers

Consequences

Positive

  • Compile-time type safety for identifiers
  • Modules evolve independently

Negative

  • Shared kernel must remain minimal — resist feature creep
  • Identifier format changes are organization-wide breaking changes

ADR-024: Centralized Audit Trail Projection

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-024
Title Centralized Audit Trail Projection
Status Accepted

Context

BO-19 requires 100% audit trail coverage. NFR-COM-010 requires immutable audit records. NFR review identified duplicate audit requirements across NFR-LOG, NFR-SEC, and NFR-COM. Per-module audit tables would fragment evidence and complicate 7-year retention.

Decision

Maintain a single authoritative audit trail projection in M-13 Intelligence, built from domain events and command audit context. Operational logs (NFR-LOG) remain separate diagnostic records. Auditor export via ExportAuditEvidencePackage query (NFR-PERF-026, NFR-COM-012).

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Per-module audit tables Fragmented; inconsistent schema
Operational logs as audit Insufficient structure and immutability
External SIEM only Business fact context missing

Consequences

Positive

  • Single query point for auditors
  • Event-sourced rebuild capability

Negative

  • Seconds-level lag on audit visibility — acceptable for compliance
  • Intelligence module becomes critical for audit access

ADR-025: Architecture Fitness Functions with ArchUnit

Field Detail
Decision ID ADR-025
Title Architecture Fitness Functions with ArchUnit
Status Accepted

Context

Modular monolith erosion is the primary long-term risk (AR-09). ADR-003 layer rules and ADR-002 module boundaries must survive team turnover and delivery pressure across 18 months. Manual architecture review alone is insufficient.

Decision

Implement ArchUnit fitness functions in CI enforcing:

  • Domain packages do not depend on infrastructure, application, or presentation
  • Modules do not import other modules' domain packages
  • JPA annotations absent from domain layer
  • Controllers do not access repositories directly

Complement with Spring Modulith ApplicationModuleTest.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative Reason Not Selected
Code review only Inconsistent enforcement
jQAssistant Heavier setup than needed

Consequences

Positive

  • Automated regression on architecture rules
  • Fast feedback on PRs

Negative

  • Rules require maintenance as packages evolve
  • False positives possible — tune carefully

ADR Governance

Process

Step Action Owner
1 Propose ADR via PR with context and alternatives Any architect or tech lead
2 Review with DDD architect and affected squad leads Solution Architect
3 Accept, reject, or mark Proposed pending workshop Steering committee / ARB
4 Update status when superseded Solution Architect
5 Link ADR in module README and relevant SRS docs Author

Review Schedule

ADR Next Review Trigger

ADR-010 HS-003 workshop completion

Document ID: SRS-SA-008 | Version 1.0 | July 6, 2026

Part VII — Database Design

Logical Data Model (ERD)

Inventory Management System

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-DB-001
Document Title Logical Data Model — Entity Relationship Diagram
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Senior Database Architect
Source Documents SRS-DM-001 (Domain Entities), SRS-DM-003 (Domain Aggregates), SRS-DM-004 (Entity Relationships), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rules), SRS-ARCH (System Architecture)
Date July 6, 2026
Scope Logical business data model only — no SQL, physical storage, indexes, or database-vendor specifics

Purpose

This document defines the Logical Data Model for the Inventory Management System. It translates the approved domain model, business rules, and aggregate boundaries into a conceptual entity-relationship structure suitable for data architecture review and physical design planning.

The model contains 40 transactional and reference entities aligned to domain entities, plus 4 derived/observability entities modeled as logical projections. Relationships express business collaboration — not implementation join strategies.

Design Principles

Principle Application
Domain fidelity Entity names and semantics follow SRS-DM-008 ubiquitous language
Aggregate awareness Each entity maps to a DDD aggregate root or child entity
Identity over navigation Cross-aggregate links are logical references by business identity (SKU, location code, order number)
Invariant visibility Business constraints from BR-001 – BR-032 are captured per entity
Logical only No data types, keys, partitions, or persistence technology

Cardinality Notation

Notation Meaning
1 Exactly one
0..1 Zero or one (optional)
1..* One or more (mandatory, many allowed)
0..* Zero or more
* Many (zero or more)

Relationship Type Legend

Type Meaning
Composition Child lifecycle bound to parent
Association Independent entities with ongoing business link
Reference Identity lookup without ownership
Modification Source operation changes target quantity or status
Derivation Target produced from or computed from source
Authorization Source gates or permits action on target
Verification Source validated against target before proceeding

Aggregate-to-Entity Map

Aggregate Aggregate Root Child / Member Entities
Product Catalog Product —
Inventory Location Inventory Location Storage Position
Supplier Supplier —
Inventory Governance Governance Policy Reason Code
Stock Position Stock Position Lot/Batch, Quarantine Hold
Stock Policy Stock Policy —
Purchase Requisition Purchase Requisition —
Purchase Order Purchase Order Expected Inbound Delivery
Goods Receipt Goods Receipt Receipt Discrepancy, Put-Away
Supplier Invoice Supplier Invoice —
Customer Order Fulfillment Customer Order Inventory Reservation, Fulfillment Execution, Backorder, Shipment
Stock Transfer Stock Transfer In-Transit Stock (Transfer Request is initial lifecycle state)
Cycle Count Cycle Count —
Physical Inventory Count Physical Inventory Count —
Inventory Adjustment Case Count Variance / Stock Adjustment Stock Adjustment, Inventory Write-Off
Customer Return Case Return Authorization Customer Return, Return Disposition
Promotional Stock Allocation Promotional Stock Allocation —
User Account User Account Role Assignment
(Derived — no aggregate) — Inventory Movement Record, Audit Trail Record, Operational Alert, Inventory Valuation Snapshot

Text-Based ERD — Core Inventory Hub

Stock Position is the central quantity authority. This diagram emphasizes modification paths.

     Quarantine Hold (-ATP)

Entity Catalog

Entities are grouped by business domain. Each entry includes business purpose, relationships, cardinality, owning aggregate, and governing constraints.

Domain 1: Master Data & Reference

1. Product

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Canonical stock-keeping unit (SKU) identity for all inventory operations — what the organization buys, holds, and sells across locations and channels.
Related Aggregate Product Catalog (root)
Relationships → Stock Position (Association); → Stock Policy (Association); → Lot/Batch (Composition); referenced by procurement, fulfillment, transfer, count, and return line items
Cardinality Product 1 → Stock Position 0..*; Product 1 → Stock Policy 0..*; Product 1 → Lot/Batch 0..*
Important Business Constraints SKU must be unique. Name and unit of measure are mandatory. Discontinued products must not appear on new POs or requisitions (BR-027). Traceable products must declare lot requirement and rotation policy (FIFO/FEFO). ABC classification must be A, B, or C when assigned (BR-032).

2. Inventory Location

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Physical site in the distribution network where stock is received, stored, counted, and fulfilled.
Related Aggregate Inventory Location (root)
Relationships → Storage Position (Composition); → Stock Position (Association); → Inventory Location parent (Hierarchy Association); → Physical Inventory Count (Association); referenced as receiving, fulfillment, and transfer endpoint
Cardinality Location 1 → Storage Position 1..*; Location 1 → Stock Position 0..*; Child Location 0..1 → Parent Location 1
Important Business Constraints Location cannot be its own ancestor. Deactivated/closing locations must not accept new receipts, reservations, or fulfillments. Physical inventory freeze (BR-024) blocks movements while wall-to-wall count is active. Closure blocked while on-hand stock remains without disposition plan.

3. Storage Position

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Designated storage area (zone, aisle, bin) within a location for put-away placement and pick path guidance.
Related Aggregate Inventory Location (child of Inventory Location aggregate)
Relationships ← Inventory Location (Composition); → Put-Away (Association); → Fulfillment Execution (Reference); → Cycle Count (optional Reference)
Cardinality Storage Position 1 → Inventory Location 1; Storage Position 1 → Put-Away 0..*; Put-Away 1 → Storage Position 1
Important Business Constraints Cannot exist outside parent location. Put-away must assign storage position before stock becomes available (BR-005). Rotation placement (FIFO/FEFO) applied at put-away (BR-014, BR-015). Put-away suspended during location freeze (BR-024).

4. Stock Policy

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Replenishment thresholds (reorder level, minimum, safety stock) for a product at a specific location.
Related Aggregate Stock Policy (root)
Relationships → Product (Reference); → Inventory Location (Reference); → Operational Alert (Derivation); verified by Transfer Request
Cardinality Stock Policy 1 → Product 1; Stock Policy 1 → Inventory Location 1; Product + Location uniquely identifies policy; Stock Policy 1 → Operational Alert 0..*
Important Business Constraints Reorder, minimum, and safety stock must be non-negative. Minimum must not exceed reorder level unless explicitly authorized. Replenishment triggers when ATP reaches reorder level (BR-009). Safety stock must not be bypassed without approval (BR-010). Source minimum constrains transfer quantity (BR-012).

5. Reason Code

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Standardized categorized explanation for adjustments, write-offs, and receipt exceptions.
Related Aggregate Inventory Governance (child of Governance Policy aggregate)
Relationships → Stock Adjustment (Authorization); → Inventory Write-Off (Authorization); → Receipt Discrepancy (Association)
Cardinality Reason Code 1 → Stock Adjustment 0..*; Stock Adjustment 1 → Reason Code 1; Write-Off 1 → Reason Code 1
Important Business Constraints Reason codes must be unique. Retired codes not selectable for new transactions. Mandatory on every adjustment and write-off (BR-020, BR-023).

6. Governance Policy

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Organization-wide control policies — approval thresholds, tolerance limits, segregation-of-duties rules, and exception handling.
Related Aggregate Inventory Governance (root)
Relationships → Stock Adjustment (Verification); → Count Variance (Verification); → Goods Receipt (Verification); contains Reason Code
Cardinality Governance Policy 1 → Stock Adjustment 0..*; Governance Policy 1 → Count Variance 0..*; Governance Policy 1 → Goods Receipt 0..*
Important Business Constraints Only one effective policy version per parameter at any time. Adjustments above threshold require independent approval (BR-021). Counter must not approve own count variances (BR-019). PO required for supplier receipt except approved ad-hoc exception (BR-007).

Domain 2: Inventory State & Balance

7. Stock Position

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Authoritative inventory balance for a product at a location — on-hand, reserved, and available-to-promise (ATP).
Related Aggregate Stock Position (root)
Relationships → Product, Inventory Location, Stock Policy (Reference); → Lot/Batch, Quarantine Hold (Composition); modified by Reservation, Shipment, GR/Put-Away, Transfer, Adjustment, Write-Off, Return Disposition, Promotional Allocation
Cardinality Stock Position 1 → Product 1; Stock Position 1 → Inventory Location 1; Stock Position 1 → Stock Policy 0..1; Stock Position 1 → Lot/Batch 0..*; Stock Position 1 → Quarantine Hold 0..*
Important Business Constraints On-hand never negative. ATP = on-hand − reserved − quarantined (BR-001, BR-013). ATP never exceeds on-hand. Consignment stock not owned until consumption (BR-031). All mutations produce Inventory Movement Record. Location freeze blocks changes except authorized count adjustments (BR-024).

8. Lot / Batch

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Traceable production or receipt grouping enabling recall, FEFO rotation, and regulatory compliance.
Related Aggregate Stock Position (child when product is traceable)
Relationships ← Product (Composition); ← Stock Position (Composition); → Supplier (Reference); referenced on GR, Put-Away, Fulfillment, Transfer, Quarantine Hold
Cardinality Product 1 → Lot/Batch 0..*; Stock Position 1 → Lot/Batch 0..*; Lot/Batch 0..1 → Supplier 1
Important Business Constraints Lot identity captured at receipt and all movements for traceable products (BR-017). FEFO pick by expiration (BR-014). MRSL validated at receipt (BR-016).

9. Quarantine Hold

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Inventory physically on-hand but excluded from sellable ATP due to quality, regulatory, recall, or customs hold.
Related Aggregate Stock Position (child)
Relationships ← Stock Position (Composition); → Lot/Batch (Reference); derived from Return Disposition; may derive Adjustment or Write-Off on release
Cardinality Stock Position 1 → Quarantine Hold 0..*; Quarantine Hold 0..1 → Lot/Batch 1
Important Business Constraints Held quantity excluded from ATP (BR-013). Bonded inventory held until customs clearance (BR-030). Release restores ATP only after clearance confirmed.

10. Promotional Stock Allocation

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Ring-fenced inventory for promotional campaigns or product launches, protected from general demand.
Related Aggregate Promotional Stock Allocation (root)
Relationships → Product (Reference); → Inventory Location 1..* (Reference); → Stock Position (Modification); → Operational Alert (Derivation)
Cardinality Allocation 1 → Product 1; Allocation 1 → Location 1..*; Allocation 0..* → Stock Position 1
Important Business Constraints Ring-fenced quantity must not serve non-promotional orders without commercial approval (BR-029). Allocation cannot exceed available stock at allocation time. Inactive outside campaign period. Unconsumed allocation released after campaign end.

Domain 3: Procurement & Inbound Supply

11. Supplier

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose External vendor — commercial counterparty for procurement, receipt, and payment.
Related Aggregate Supplier (root)
Relationships → Purchase Order (Association); → Supplier Invoice (Association); referenced by Goods Receipt and Lot/Batch
Cardinality Supplier 1 → Purchase Order 0..*; Supplier 1 → Supplier Invoice 0..*
Important Business Constraints Supplier code unique. Must be active for new POs. Consignment indicator governs ownership at receipt (BR-031). Payment terms required before PO issuance.

12. Purchase Requisition

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Internal request to procure stock, preceding formal PO creation with approval workflow.
Related Aggregate Purchase Requisition (root)
Relationships → Product 1..* (Reference); → Inventory Location (Reference); → Purchase Order (Derivation); → Operational Alert (Reference)
Cardinality Requisition 1 → Product 1..*; Requisition 1 → Location 1; Requisition 1 → Purchase Order 0..1; Alert 0..1 → Requisition 0..1
Important Business Constraints Lines must reference active products — discontinued prohibited (BR-027). Network availability evaluated before approval (BR-011). Safety stock not implicitly bypassed (BR-010). Must be approved before PO conversion.

13. Purchase Order

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Authorized commercial commitment to a supplier specifying products, quantities, prices, and delivery terms.
Related Aggregate Purchase Order (root)
Relationships → Supplier, Inventory Location, Product (Reference); → Expected Inbound Delivery (Composition); → Goods Receipt (Authorization); → Supplier Invoice (Verification)
Cardinality PO 1 → Supplier 1; PO 1 → Location 1; PO 1 → Product 1..*; PO 1 → Expected Delivery 0..*; PO 1 → Goods Receipt 0..*
Important Business Constraints Valid PO required before supplier receipt except approved exception (BR-007). Discontinued products prohibited (BR-027). Received qty per line within tolerance or discrepancy workflow. Status: open → partial → closed/cancelled.

14. Expected Inbound Delivery

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Planned or confirmed supplier shipment communicating anticipated arrival for receiving preparation.
Related Aggregate Purchase Order (child)
Relationships → Purchase Order (Reference); → Stock Position (Derivation — informational inbound expected); → Operational Alert (Derivation)
Cardinality Expected Delivery 1 → Purchase Order 1; Expected Delivery 0..* → Stock Position 1
Important Business Constraints Expected quantities must not exceed remaining open PO line quantities. Inbound expected is informational only — does not increase ATP until put-away (BR-005). Delays trigger replenishment notifications.

15. Goods Receipt

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Business event of accepting verified inbound goods into inventory control after dock verification.
Related Aggregate Goods Receipt (root)
Relationships → Purchase Order (Verification); → Supplier, Inventory Location (Reference); → Receipt Discrepancy, Put-Away (Composition); → Stock Position (Modification on put-away completion); → Lot/Batch (Derivation)
Cardinality Goods Receipt 0..* → Purchase Order 0..1; GR 1 → Supplier 1; GR 1 → Location 1; GR 1 → Discrepancy 0..*; GR 1 → Put-Away 1..*
Important Business Constraints Verify quantity, product, condition before acceptance (BR-004). PO required except exception (BR-007). Discrepancies documented before acceptance (BR-006). MRSL met for shelf-life products (BR-016). Lot captured for traceable products (BR-017). Receipt blocked during location freeze (BR-024).

16. Receipt Discrepancy

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Documented difference between expected and actual receipt (short, over, wrong item, damage, shelf-life failure).
Related Aggregate Goods Receipt (child)
Relationships → Goods Receipt (Composition); → Reason Code (Association)
Cardinality Discrepancy 1 → Goods Receipt 1; Goods Receipt 1 → Discrepancy 0..*
Important Business Constraints Must be recorded before acceptance of affected quantities (BR-006). Unresolved discrepancies affect three-way match (BR-008). Shelf-life non-compliance recorded as discrepancy (BR-016).

17. Put-Away

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Confirmation that received goods are moved from receiving area to storage position and are operationally available.
Related Aggregate Goods Receipt (child)
Relationships → Goods Receipt (Reference); → Storage Position (Association); → Stock Position (Modification — triggers on-hand/ATP increase)
Cardinality Put-Away 1 → Goods Receipt 1; Put-Away 1 → Storage Position 1
Important Business Constraints ATP not increased until put-away confirmed (BR-005). Rotation placement applied (BR-014, BR-015). Bonded goods to hold storage until customs clearance (BR-030).

18. Supplier Invoice

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Supplier billing document — financial leg of three-way match against PO and goods receipt.
Related Aggregate Supplier Invoice (root)
Relationships → Supplier, Purchase Order (Reference); → Goods Receipt (Verification); → Inventory Valuation Snapshot (Derivation)
Cardinality Invoice 1 → Supplier 1; Invoice 1 → Purchase Order 1; Invoice 1 → Goods Receipt 0..*
Important Business Constraints Three-way match within tolerance before payment (BR-008). Payment prohibited for unordered, unreceived, or mispriced goods. Match exceptions require resolution or waiver.

Domain 4: Order Fulfillment

19. Customer Order

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Customer demand triggering availability confirmation, reservation, picking, and shipment.
Related Aggregate Customer Order Fulfillment (root)
Relationships → Stock Position (Reference for ATP); → Inventory Reservation, Fulfillment Execution, Backorder, Shipment (Composition); → Return Authorization (Association)
Cardinality Order 1 → Reservation 0..*; Order 1 → Fulfillment 0..*; Order 1 → Backorder 0..*; Order 1 → Shipment 0..*; Order 1 → Stock Position 1..*
Important Business Constraints Commit only against ATP, not total on-hand (BR-001). Reserve at confirmation (BR-002). Respect promotional ring-fence (BR-029). Order line reconciliation: requested = reserved + fulfilled + backordered + cancelled.

20. Inventory Reservation

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Operational hold on stock for a confirmed order line, reducing ATP until fulfillment or release.
Related Aggregate Customer Order Fulfillment (child)
Relationships → Customer Order (Reference); → Product, Inventory Location (Reference); → Stock Position (Modification); consumed by Shipment
Cardinality Reservation 1 → Customer Order 1; Reservation 1 → Product 1; Reservation 0..* → Stock Position 1
Important Business Constraints Created at order confirmation (BR-002). Must not consume below safety stock without exception (BR-010). Promotional ring-fence respected (BR-029). Released on cancellation; consumed on shipment.

21. Fulfillment Execution

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Warehouse pick, verify, and pack work bridging reservation to shipment.
Related Aggregate Customer Order Fulfillment (child)
Relationships → Customer Order (Reference); → Inventory Location, Storage Position, Lot/Batch (Reference); → Shipment (Derivation)
Cardinality Fulfillment 1 → Customer Order 1; Fulfillment 1 → Location 1; Fulfillment 1 → Shipment 0..1
Important Business Constraints Verified pick required before shipment (BR-003). FEFO/FIFO applied during pick (BR-014, BR-015). Lot captured on pick for traceable products (BR-017). Blocked at frozen location (BR-024).

22. Backorder

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Customer-agreed delay for unfulfilled order line quantity when full ATP unavailable.
Related Aggregate Customer Order Fulfillment (child)
Relationships → Customer Order (Reference); → Product (Reference)
Cardinality Backorder 1 → Customer Order 1; Backorder 1 → Product 1
Important Business Constraints Explicit customer acknowledgment required before recording (BR-028). May convert to reservation when stock arrives. Replenishment priority may apply.

23. Shipment

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Confirmed dispatch of fulfilled goods — inventory deduction and delivery promise activation.
Related Aggregate Customer Order Fulfillment (child)
Relationships → Customer Order, Fulfillment Execution (Reference); → Inventory Reservation (Modification); → Stock Position (Modification)
Cardinality Shipment 1 → Fulfillment Execution 1; Shipment 0..* → Reservation 1; Shipment 0..* → Stock Position 1
Important Business Constraints Only after verified pick (BR-003). Deducts on-hand and consumes reservation (BR-002). Creates outbound movement record.

Domain 5: Network Balance

24. Transfer Request

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Formal request to move stock between locations to resolve shortage or rebalance network before new procurement.
Related Aggregate Stock Transfer (initial lifecycle state within Stock Transfer aggregate)
Relationships → Inventory Location source and destination (Reference); → Product 1..* (Reference); → Stock Policy source (Verification); → Stock Transfer (Derivation)
Cardinality Request 1 → Source Location 1; Request 1 → Destination Location 1; Request 1 → Product 1..*; Request 1 → Stock Transfer 0..1
Important Business Constraints Must not deplete source below minimum (BR-012). Network check before purchase alternative (BR-011). Safety stock at source protected (BR-010). Source and destination must be distinct active locations.

25. Stock Transfer

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Executed inter-location stock movement from dispatch through destination receipt.
Related Aggregate Stock Transfer (root)
Relationships → Transfer Request (Reference); → In-Transit Stock (Composition); → Stock Position source and destination (Modification); → Lot/Batch (Reference)
Cardinality Transfer 0..1 → Transfer Request 1; Transfer 1 → In-Transit Stock 1..*; Transfer 1 → Stock Position 2 per product line
Important Business Constraints Source not depleted below minimum (BR-012). Lot captured for traceable products (BR-017). Blocked during location freeze (BR-024). In-transit excluded from both endpoints' ATP until receipt.

26. In-Transit Stock

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Pipeline inventory that left source but is not yet received at destination.
Related Aggregate Stock Transfer (child)
Relationships → Stock Transfer (Composition); references Product, source and destination locations
Cardinality In-Transit 1 → Stock Transfer 1; Transfer 1 → In-Transit 1..*
Important Business Constraints Excluded from source and destination ATP until receipt confirmed. Delayed/lost in-transit triggers exception alerts.

Domain 6: Inventory Control & Accuracy

27. Cycle Count

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Scheduled partial physical count on rotating basis without full warehouse shutdown.
Related Aggregate Cycle Count (root)
Relationships → Product, Inventory Location (Reference); → Storage Position (optional Reference); → Count Variance (Derivation); → User Account counter (Reference)
Cardinality Cycle Count 1 → Product 1; Cycle Count 1 → Location 1; Cycle Count 0..1 → Storage Position 1; Cycle Count 1 → Count Variance 0..1
Important Business Constraints Blind count — counter must not see system quantity (BR-018). Class A highest frequency (BR-032). Does not directly mutate Stock Position — spawns Adjustment Case on variance. Counter ≠ approver (BR-019).

28. Physical Inventory Count

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Comprehensive wall-to-wall count at a location for audit-mandated accuracy baseline.
Related Aggregate Physical Inventory Count (root)
Relationships → Inventory Location (Association); → Count Variance 0..* (Derivation)
Cardinality Physical Count 1 → Location 1; Location 1 → Physical Count 0..*; Physical Count 1 → Count Variance 0..*
Important Business Constraints Location freeze during count — no receiving, shipping, transfers, or adjustments (BR-024). Full location scope required. Certification requires variances routed to adjustment cases.

29. Count Variance

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Identified difference between system and physical quantity requiring investigation before correction.
Related Aggregate Inventory Adjustment Case (root when originating from count)
Relationships → Cycle Count or Physical Inventory Count (Reference); → Stock Position (Reference); → Stock Adjustment (Derivation); → User Account approver (Reference); verified by Governance Policy
Cardinality Variance 1 → exactly one count origin; Variance 1 → Stock Position 1; Variance 1 → Stock Adjustment 0..1
Important Business Constraints Investigate before adjusting (BR-022). Counter must not approve own variance (BR-019). Independent approval above threshold (BR-021).

30. Stock Adjustment

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Corrective change to recorded inventory quantity with mandatory reason and authorization.
Related Aggregate Inventory Adjustment Case (child)
Relationships → Stock Position (Modification); → Count Variance (optional Reference); → Reason Code (Reference); → User Account initiator and approver (Reference); verified by Governance Policy
Cardinality Adjustment 0..1 → Count Variance 1; Adjustment 1 → Reason Code 1; Adjustment 0..* → Stock Position 1
Important Business Constraints Mandatory reason code (BR-020). Independent approval above threshold (BR-021). Investigate when from count (BR-022). Must not drive stock negative.

31. Inventory Write-Off

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Formal authorized permanent removal of inventory value for damaged, obsolete, expired, or lost goods.
Related Aggregate Inventory Adjustment Case (child)
Relationships → Stock Position (Modification); → Reason Code (Reference); → Return Disposition (Reference); → User Account authorizer (Authorization)
Cardinality Write-Off 0..* → Stock Position 1; Write-Off 1 → Reason Code 1; Disposition 0..1 → Write-Off 1
Important Business Constraints Documented evidence and authorization required (BR-023). Mandatory reason code (BR-020). Terminal — quantity permanently removed.

Domain 7: Returns Management

32. Return Authorization

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Approved permission (RMA) for customer return linked to original order before warehouse acceptance.
Related Aggregate Customer Return Case (root)
Relationships → Customer Order (Verification); → Product 1..* (Reference); → Customer Return (Authorization)
Cardinality RMA 1 → Customer Order 1; RMA 1 → Product 1..*; RMA 1 → Customer Return 0..1
Important Business Constraints Required before warehouse acceptance (BR-025). Must link to original order. RMA expiration enforced. Returned products must match authorized lines.

33. Customer Return

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Physical receipt of customer-returned goods at warehouse, initiating inspection workflow.
Related Aggregate Customer Return Case (child)
Relationships → Return Authorization (Verification); → Inventory Location (Reference); → Return Disposition (Composition)
Cardinality Return 1 → RMA 1; Return 1 → Location 1; Return 1 → Disposition 1..*
Important Business Constraints No receipt without valid RMA (BR-025). Verify quantity and product on receipt (BR-004). Inspection mandatory before disposition (BR-026).

34. Return Disposition

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Business decision on returned goods — restock, quarantine, or write-off based on condition.
Related Aggregate Customer Return Case (child)
Relationships → Customer Return (Reference); → Stock Position (Modification on restock); → Quarantine Hold, Inventory Write-Off (Derivation)
Cardinality Disposition 1 → Customer Return 1; Disposition 0..1 → Stock Position 1; Disposition 0..1 → Quarantine Hold 0..1; Disposition 0..1 → Write-Off 1
Important Business Constraints Inspect before restock (BR-026). Restock only when condition confirms resale quality. Damaged goods to quarantine or write-off — never direct to ATP.

Domain 8: Accountability & Oversight

35. Inventory Movement Record

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Immutable documented change in inventory position — operational history of every stock activity.
Related Aggregate (Derived — append-only event log; not an aggregate consistency boundary)
Relationships → Stock Position (Association); → originating business document (Reference); → User Account (Reference); → Lot/Batch, Reason Code (optional Reference)
Cardinality Movement 0..* → Stock Position 1; Movement 1 → originating document 1; Movement 1 → User Account 1
Important Business Constraints Every stock mutation must produce a movement record. Lot on movement for traceable products (BR-017). Reason code on adjustment movements (BR-020). Immutable after creation.

36. Audit Trail Record

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Governance-grade record of material changes with user identity, timestamp, and before/after state.
Related Aggregate (Derived — compliance log; not an aggregate consistency boundary)
Relationships → governed entity (Association); → Inventory Movement Record (Association); → User Account (Reference)
Cardinality Audit 0..* → governed entity 1; Audit 0..1 → Movement Record 1; Audit 1 → User Account 1
Important Business Constraints Supports segregation-of-duties verification (BR-019, BR-021). Immutable after write. Material changes require both movement and audit records.

37. Operational Alert

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Proactive notification of conditions requiring human review — low stock, pending approval, exceptions.
Related Aggregate (Derived — read model / notification projection)
Relationships derived from Stock Position + Stock Policy; Transfer Request; Promotional Allocation; Expected Inbound Delivery
Cardinality Alert 0..* → Stock Position 1; Alert 0..* → Transfer Request 0..1; Alert 0..* → Promotional Allocation 0..1
Important Business Constraints Reorder-level breach triggers same-day replenishment review (BR-009). Class A products generate higher-priority alerts (BR-032). Campaign readiness alerts before launch commitment (BR-029).

38. User Account

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Identified individual authorized to perform inventory operations within role and location scope.
Related Aggregate User Account (root)
Relationships → Role Assignment (Composition); associated with Cycle Count, Goods Receipt, Adjustments, Movement and Audit records
Cardinality User Account 1 → Role Assignment 1..*
Important Business Constraints User identifier unique. At least one role required to transact. Conflicting duty combinations blocked — counter + approver (BR-019, BR-021). Deactivated accounts cannot perform actions.

39. Role Assignment

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Delegation of business permissions to a user with location scope and segregation-of-duties enforcement.
Related Aggregate User Account (child)
Relationships → User Account (Composition); → Inventory Location 0..* (Reference for scope)
Cardinality Role Assignment 1 → User Account 1; Role Assignment 1 → Location 0..*
Important Business Constraints SoD conflicts blocked at assignment. Location scope enforced on transactions. Effective-dated with history retained. Empty scope may mean network-wide for executive roles.

Domain 9: Financial Alignment

40. Inventory Valuation Snapshot

Aspect Detail
Business Purpose Point-in-time inventory value summary by product and location for finance reconciliation and month-end close.
Related Aggregate (Derived — reporting read model; rebuilt from Stock Position events and matched costs)
Relationships derived from Stock Position, Product, Inventory Location; references Supplier Invoice costs, Inventory Write-Off
Cardinality Snapshot 1 → Stock Position 0..*; Snapshot 1 → Product 0..*; Snapshot 1 → Location 0..*
Important Business Constraints Consignment stock excluded from owned valuation (BR-031). Quarantined and in-transit stock excluded per policy. Three-way matched invoice costs authoritative for received inventory (BR-008).

Relationship Summary Matrix

From Entity To Entity Type Cardinality Governing Rules

Product Stock Policy Association 1 : 0..* BR-009, BR-032
Inventory Location Storage Position Composition 1 : 1..* BR-005, BR-024
Inventory Location Stock Position Association 1 : 0..* BR-012, BR-024

Put-Away Stock Position Modification 0..* : 1 BR-005

Shipment Stock Position Modification 0..* : 1 BR-003

Full relationship catalog: SRS-DM-004 (REL-001 – REL-134).

Cross-Aggregate Reference Model

Aggregates coordinate through identity references and domain events — not shared mutable structures.

┌──────────────────┐   PutAwayCompleted    ┌──────────────────┐
│  Goods Receipt   │ ─────────────────────►│  Stock Position  │
│  (Aggregate 9)   │                       │  (Aggregate 5)   │
└──────────────────┘                       └────────▲─────────┘
                                                  │
┌──────────────────┐   ReservationCommitted       │
│ Customer Order   │ ───────────────────────────┤
│ Fulfillment (11)│   ShipmentDispatched        │
└──────────────────┘ ───────────────────────────┘

┌──────────────────┐   TransferDispatched/Received
│  Stock Transfer  │ ───────────────────────────► Stock Position
│  (Aggregate 12)  │
└──────────────────┘

┌──────────────────┐   AdjustmentApproved
│ Adjustment Case  │ ───────────────────────────► Stock Position
│  (Aggregate 15)  │
└──────────────────┘

┌──────────────────┐   RestockApproved
│ Customer Return  │ ───────────────────────────► Stock Position
│  Case (16)       │
└──────────────────┘
Interaction Rule Description
One transaction, one aggregate Stock deduction and PO creation never share a consistency boundary
Reference by identity Cross-aggregate links use SKU, location code, order number — not object graphs
Consult, don't couple Transfer consults Stock Policy and Stock Position by identity for source minimum
Governance consultation Adjustment aggregates consult Inventory Governance for thresholds and reason codes
Catalog validation Procurement and fulfillment consult Product Catalog for lifecycle status

Entity Integrity Rules (Logical Level)

Rule ID Rule Entities Affected
LDM-01 ATP = on-hand − reserved − quarantined; ATP ≤ on-hand Stock Position, Quarantine Hold, Inventory Reservation
LDM-02 Stock availability increases only after Put-Away completion Goods Receipt, Put-Away, Stock Position
LDM-03 Shipment decreases on-hand only after verified Fulfillment Execution Fulfillment Execution, Shipment, Stock Position
LDM-04 Product + Location uniquely identifies Stock Position and Stock Policy Stock Position, Stock Policy
LDM-05 Discontinued Product prohibited on new PO, Requisition, and Reservation lines Product, Purchase Order, Purchase Requisition, Inventory Reservation
LDM-06 Counter User Account ≠ Approver User Account on same Count Variance Cycle Count, Count Variance, User Account
LDM-07 Customer Return requires valid Return Authorization Return Authorization, Customer Return
LDM-08 In-transit quantity excluded from both endpoint Stock Positions' ATP In-Transit Stock, Stock Transfer, Stock Position
LDM-09 Physical Inventory Count imposes freeze on all Inventory Location movements Physical Inventory Count, Inventory Location
LDM-10 Every Stock Position mutation produces Inventory Movement Record Stock Position, Inventory Movement Record
