Document ID: SRS-DB-004 | Version 1.0 | July 6, 2026

Database Indexing Strategy

Inventory Management System — PostgreSQL

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-DB-005
Document Title Database Indexing Strategy
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Database Performance Specialist
Source Documents SRS-DB-002 (Physical Data Model), SRS-DB-003 (Database Keys), SRS-DB-004 (Database Constraints)
Target Platform PostgreSQL 15+
Date July 6, 2026
Scope Index design and justification — no DDL/SQL statements

Purpose

This document defines the indexing strategy for the Inventory Management System. Indexes are chosen only where they support real query patterns from business operations — not as a default on every column. Each index includes junior-friendly performance explanation.

Part 1: Indexing Principles (Junior Guide)

What is an index?

An index is a sorted lookup structure (like a book index) that helps PostgreSQL find rows quickly without scanning the entire table.

Without index With index
Full table scan — reads every row Index seek — jumps to matching rows
Fast on tiny tables Essential on large tables (millions of rows)
OK for rare admin queries Required for high-frequency operational queries

Why indexes matter in IMS

The hottest path is: "How much of product X is available at location Y?" — asked on every order confirmation, reservation, and replenishment check. That query runs thousands of times per hour. A missing index here blocks the whole warehouse.

How PostgreSQL uses an index

  1. Query arrives: WHERE product_id = 42 AND location_id = 7
  2. Planner checks: is there an index on (product_id, location_id)?
  3. If yes → Index Scan — reads only matching pages (milliseconds)
  4. If no → Seq Scan — reads all stock position rows (seconds at scale)

Column order matters in composite indexes: (product_id, location_id) helps WHERE product_id = ? and WHERE product_id = ? AND location_id = ?, but is weaker for WHERE location_id = ? alone. Design indexes to match real WHERE clauses.

Costs of too many indexes

Benefit Cost
Faster SELECT Slower INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (every index must be updated)
Faster JOIN More disk space
Faster ORDER BY More memory during maintenance (VACUUM, REINDEX)

Rule: Index for queries that run often and filter/join on the indexed columns. Do not index "just in case."

Index types used in this system

Type When to use IMS example
B-tree (default) Equality, range, sorting, most FK lookups stock_positions (product_id, location_id)
Partial B-tree Frequent queries on a subset of rows Active reservations only: WHERE reservation_status = 'ACTIVE'
BRIN Very large time-ordered tables (append-only logs) movement_timestamp on movement records
GIN JSONB containment queries (rare) audit_trail_records.before_state — only if JSON search needed

Not used: Hash indexes (no advantage over B-tree in modern PostgreSQL), GiST (no spatial data in IMS).

Part 2: Index Tiers

Tier Purpose Count Maintenance
Tier 1 — Critical Hot-path operational queries; system fails SLA without these 18 Monitor weekly
Tier 2 — Operational High-volume workflows; noticeable slowdown if missing 22 Monitor monthly
Tier 3 — Reporting & audit Dashboards, history, compliance; tolerates slightly slower reads 12 Review quarterly
Implicit (UNIQUE/PK) Created automatically by constraints — do not duplicate ~75 Maintained with constraints

Total explicit indexes defined: 52 (excluding PK/UK implicit indexes)

Part 3: Tier 1 — Critical Indexes

These support the highest-frequency queries. Deploy in the initial migration.

IDX-001

Attribute Detail
Table inventory.stock_positions
Indexed columns (product_id, location_id)
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via uk_stock_positions_product_location)
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM stock_positions WHERE product_id = ? AND location_id = ?
Business justification Central ATP lookup for order confirmation (BR-001), reservation (BR-002), and replenishment (BR-009). One row per SKU per site.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Every order check asks "do we have stock here?" How: UNIQUE constraint automatically creates this B-tree index — PostgreSQL finds the single matching row in O(log n) time instead of scanning all balances. Do not create a duplicate non-unique index on the same columns.

IDX-002

Attribute Detail
Table catalog.products
Indexed columns sku
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via uk_products_sku)
Expected query pattern SELECT id FROM products WHERE sku = ?
Business justification SKU is the ubiquitous lookup key at receipt, pick, and catalog integration.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: External systems and scanners send SKU strings, not internal id. How: UNIQUE index on sku converts string lookup to fast seek before any stock operation.

IDX-003

Attribute Detail
Table catalog.product_identifiers
Indexed columns (identifier_type, identifier_value)
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via UK)
Expected query pattern SELECT product_id FROM product_identifiers WHERE identifier_type = 'BARCODE' AND identifier_value = ?
Business justification Barcode scan at receiving dock and pick face (BR-004). Wrong index = slow scan response.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Warehouse staff scan barcodes, not SKUs. How: Composite UK lets PostgreSQL resolve barcode → product_id in one index lookup.

IDX-004

Attribute Detail
Table fulfillment.inventory_reservations
Indexed columns (stock_position_id) WHERE reservation_status = 'ACTIVE'
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM inventory_reservations WHERE stock_position_id = ? AND reservation_status = 'ACTIVE'
Business justification Only active reservations affect ATP; released/fulfilled rows are historical noise (BR-002).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Table grows with all historical reservations but queries care about ACTIVE rows only. How: Partial index stores only active rows — smaller, faster, cheaper to maintain than a full composite index on (stock_position_id, reservation_status). Note: Do not also create a non-partial index on the same columns — one index only.

IDX-005

Attribute Detail
Table inventory.lot_batches
Indexed columns (stock_position_id, expiration_date)
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM lot_batches WHERE stock_position_id = ? ORDER BY expiration_date ASC LIMIT 1
Business justification FEFO pick — earliest expiring lot first at a specific bin (BR-014).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Picker needs "which lot expires first at this bin?" How: Index sorted by expiration_date within each stock_position_id avoids sorting thousands of lots at pick time.

IDX-006

Attribute Detail
Table inventory.lot_batches
Indexed columns (product_id, expiration_date)
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM lot_batches WHERE product_id = ? AND expiration_date > CURRENT_DATE ORDER BY expiration_date
Business justification Network-wide FEFO and recall scope queries across locations.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Quality team asks "all lots of product X expiring soon network-wide." How: Product_id narrows scope; expiration_date supports range scan and ORDER BY.

IDX-008

Attribute Detail
Table fulfillment.customer_orders
Indexed columns (order_status, order_date DESC)
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM customer_orders WHERE order_status IN ('CONFIRMED','PARTIAL') ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 50
Business justification Open order queue for warehouse dashboard and fulfillment planning.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Warehouse managers view "orders needing action today." How: order_status filters open orders; order_date DESC returns newest first without separate sort step.

IDX-009

Attribute Detail
Table fulfillment.customer_orders
Indexed columns order_number
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via UK)
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM customer_orders WHERE order_number = ?
Business justification Customer service and integration lookup by order number.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Call center searches by order number constantly. How: UK provides index automatically — no extra index needed.

IDX-010

Attribute Detail
Table network.inventory_locations
Indexed columns location_code
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via UK)
Expected query pattern SELECT id FROM inventory_locations WHERE location_code = ?
Business justification Location code used in UI, reports, and cross-system references.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Users think in "WH-01" not internal id 7. How: UK on location_code — implicit index, do not duplicate.

IDX-011

Attribute Detail
Table inventory.stock_positions
Indexed columns (location_id, stock_status) WHERE stock_status IN ('LOW_STOCK','OUT_OF_STOCK')
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM stock_positions WHERE location_id = ? AND stock_status IN ('LOW_STOCK','OUT_OF_STOCK')
Business justification Low-stock alert generation and replenishment review (BR-009, BR-032).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Replenishment team monitors exceptions, not every IN_STOCK row. How: Partial index includes only alert-worthy rows — tiny index, fast scan per location. Most rows are IN_STOCK and excluded.

IDX-012

Attribute Detail
Table procurement.purchase_orders
Indexed columns po_number
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via UK)
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM purchase_orders WHERE po_number = ?
Business justification PO lookup at receiving dock and three-way match (BR-007, BR-008).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Receiver scans/types PO number on every inbound shipment. How: UK provides index — no duplicate needed.

IDX-013

Attribute Detail
Table inbound.goods_receipts
Indexed columns purchase_order_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM goods_receipts WHERE purchase_order_id = ?
Business justification "What has been received against this PO?" — receiving and match workflows.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Three-way match joins invoice → PO → all receipts for that PO. How: FK column is not auto-indexed in PostgreSQL — explicit index required for JOIN performance.

IDX-014

Attribute Detail
Table procurement.purchase_order_lines
Indexed columns (purchase_order_id, product_id)
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM purchase_order_lines WHERE purchase_order_id = ? AND product_id = ?
Business justification Receipt verification against specific PO line (BR-004, BR-007).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Receiver confirms "PO line for SKU X." How: Composite index matches both filter columns — one seek instead of fetching all PO lines.

IDX-015

Attribute Detail
Table fulfillment.customer_order_lines
Indexed columns customer_order_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM customer_order_lines WHERE customer_order_id = ?
Business justification Load all lines when opening an order for reservation and fulfillment.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Every order detail screen loads header + lines. How: Index on FK parent id — classic parent-child pattern. Without it, full scan of all order lines in the system.

IDX-016

Attribute Detail
Table fulfillment.inventory_reservations
Indexed columns order_line_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM inventory_reservations WHERE order_line_id = ?
Business justification Find reservation for order line during ship and cancellation.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Shipment consumes reservation per order line. How: Direct lookup by line id when processing fulfillment.

IDX-017

Attribute Detail
Table inventory.stock_policies
Indexed columns (product_id, location_id)
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via UK)
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM stock_policies WHERE product_id = ? AND location_id = ?
Business justification Threshold lookup paired with stock position for reorder alerts (BR-009).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: ATP status compared to reorder level on same product+location key. How: UK mirrors stock_positions key — often joined together; both have implicit indexes.

IDX-018

Attribute Detail
Table identity.user_accounts
Indexed columns user_identifier
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via UK)
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM user_accounts WHERE user_identifier = ?
Business justification Login and attribution on every transactional row.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Every operation records "who did it." How: UK on login id — implicit index at authentication time.

Part 4: Tier 2 — Operational Indexes

High-volume workflows beyond the absolute hot path.

IDX-019

Attribute Detail
Table inbound.goods_receipt_lines
Indexed columns goods_receipt_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM goods_receipt_lines WHERE goods_receipt_id = ?
Business justification Load receipt lines for verification and put-away.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Parent-child document pattern. How: Index on receipt header FK — same pattern as order lines.

IDX-020

Attribute Detail
Table inbound.put_aways
Indexed columns goods_receipt_line_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM put_aways WHERE goods_receipt_line_id = ?
Business justification Check put-away completion before ATP increase (BR-005).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: System asks "is this receipt line put away yet?" How: Direct lookup on receipt line FK.

IDX-021

Attribute Detail
Table procurement.purchase_orders
Indexed columns (supplier_id, po_status) WHERE po_status IN ('OPEN','PARTIAL')
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM purchase_orders WHERE supplier_id = ? AND po_status IN ('OPEN','PARTIAL')
Business justification Open PO list per supplier for receiving and AP.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Buyers care about open POs, not 5 years of closed history. How: Partial index shrinks size by excluding CLOSED/CANCELLED rows.

IDX-022

Attribute Detail
Table finance.supplier_invoices
Indexed columns purchase_order_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM supplier_invoices WHERE purchase_order_id = ?
Business justification Three-way match PO leg (BR-008).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: AP clerk finds invoices for a PO. How: FK index for JOIN in match workflow.

IDX-023

Attribute Detail
Table finance.supplier_invoices
Indexed columns (supplier_id, invoice_number)
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via UK)
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM supplier_invoices WHERE supplier_id = ? AND invoice_number = ?
Business justification Duplicate invoice detection.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: UK enforces uniqueness and serves lookup — no extra index.

IDX-024

Attribute Detail
Table finance.invoice_goods_receipt_match
Indexed columns goods_receipt_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM invoice_goods_receipt_match WHERE goods_receipt_id = ?
Business justification Reverse lookup: which invoices matched this receipt.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: UK covers (supplier_invoice_id, goods_receipt_id) but queries from receipt side need goods_receipt_id leading column. How: Second index justified — different access path than UK.

IDX-025

Attribute Detail
Table fulfillment.fulfillment_executions
Indexed columns customer_order_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM fulfillment_executions WHERE customer_order_id = ?
Business justification Pick queue per order.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Warehouse loads pick work for one order. How: Standard FK parent index.

IDX-026

Attribute Detail
Table fulfillment.fulfillment_executions
Indexed columns (fulfillment_location_id, pick_verification_status) WHERE pick_verification_status = 'PENDING'
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM fulfillment_executions WHERE fulfillment_location_id = ? AND pick_verification_status = 'PENDING'
Business justification Warehouse pick queue by location.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Pickers see only pending work at their site. How: Partial index on PENDING rows only — verified picks are dead for queue purposes.

IDX-027

Attribute Detail
Table fulfillment.shipments
Indexed columns customer_order_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM shipments WHERE customer_order_id = ?
Business justification Order tracking and shipment history.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Customer service views shipments for an order. How: FK index on order.

IDX-028

Attribute Detail
Table fulfillment.backorders
Indexed columns (resolution_status, product_id) WHERE resolution_status = 'OPEN'
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM backorders WHERE resolution_status = 'OPEN' AND product_id = ?
Business justification Replenishment priority for open backorders (BR-028).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Planners ask "what SKUs have open backorders?" How: Partial index on OPEN only — fulfilled backorders excluded.

IDX-029

Attribute Detail
Table transfer.stock_transfers
Indexed columns (destination_location_id, transfer_status) WHERE transfer_status = 'IN_TRANSIT'
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM stock_transfers WHERE destination_location_id = ? AND transfer_status = 'IN_TRANSIT'
Business justification Expected inbound transfers at destination (BR-012).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Destination warehouse prepares for incoming transfers. How: Small partial index — few IN_TRANSIT rows at any time.

IDX-030

Attribute Detail
Table transfer.in_transit_stock
Indexed columns stock_transfer_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM in_transit_stock WHERE stock_transfer_id = ?
Business justification Pipeline detail for active transfer.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Child rows of transfer header. How: FK index — composition pattern.

IDX-031

Attribute Detail
Table inventory.quarantine_holds
Indexed columns (stock_position_id) WHERE hold_status = 'ACTIVE'
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT SUM(held_qty) FROM quarantine_holds WHERE stock_position_id = ? AND hold_status = 'ACTIVE'
Business justification ATP calculation excludes active holds (BR-013).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Same pattern as reservations — only ACTIVE holds reduce ATP. How: Partial index for sum aggregation per stock position.

IDX-032

Attribute Detail
Table network.storage_positions
Indexed columns (location_id, position_code)
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via UK)
Expected query pattern SELECT id FROM storage_positions WHERE location_id = ? AND position_code = ?
Business justification Put-away and pick bin lookup.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: "Put this in bin A-01-03 at WH-01." How: UK provides composite index — no duplicate.

IDX-033

Attribute Detail
Table network.inventory_locations
Indexed columns parent_location_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM inventory_locations WHERE parent_location_id = ?
Business justification Hierarchy roll-up — list child sites under region.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Reports aggregate by region. How: Index on self-referencing FK — tree traversal from parent to children.

IDX-034

Attribute Detail
Table accuracy.cycle_counts
Indexed columns (location_id, count_status, schedule_date) WHERE count_status IN ('SCHEDULED','IN_PROGRESS')
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM cycle_counts WHERE location_id = ? AND count_status IN ('SCHEDULED','IN_PROGRESS') ORDER BY schedule_date
Business justification Counter work queue (BR-018).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Counters see today's assignments at their warehouse. How: Partial index excludes completed historical counts.

IDX-035

Attribute Detail
Table accuracy.count_variances
Indexed columns (approval_status, investigation_status) WHERE approval_status = 'PENDING'
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM count_variances WHERE approval_status = 'PENDING' ORDER BY created_at
Business justification Approver work queue (BR-019, BR-021).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Managers approve pending variances — not thousands of old approved rows. How: Partial index on PENDING only.

IDX-036

Attribute Detail
Table accuracy.stock_adjustments
Indexed columns (approval_status) WHERE approval_status = 'PENDING'
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM stock_adjustments WHERE approval_status = 'PENDING'
Business justification Adjustment approval queue (BR-021).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Same approval-queue pattern as variances. How: Tiny partial index of pending items.

IDX-037

Attribute Detail
Table returns.return_authorizations
Indexed columns customer_order_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM return_authorizations WHERE customer_order_id = ?
Business justification RMA history per order (BR-025).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Customer service checks return eligibility on original order. How: FK index.

IDX-038

Attribute Detail
Table returns.return_authorizations
Indexed columns rma_number
Index type B-tree UNIQUE (implicit via UK)
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM return_authorizations WHERE rma_number = ?
Business justification Warehouse scans RMA at return dock.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: UK on rma_number — implicit index, no duplicate.

IDX-039

Attribute Detail
Table procurement.purchase_requisitions
Indexed columns (approval_status) WHERE approval_status IN ('SUBMITTED','APPROVED')
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM purchase_requisitions WHERE approval_status = 'SUBMITTED'
Business justification Buyer approval queue.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Buyers approve submitted requisitions — not drafts or converted. How: Partial index on workflow-active states.

IDX-040

Attribute Detail
Table transfer.transfer_requests
Indexed columns (request_status) WHERE request_status = 'SUBMITTED'
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM transfer_requests WHERE request_status = 'SUBMITTED'
Business justification Transfer approval queue (BR-012).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Operations director approves pending transfers. How: Partial index — small pending set.

Part 5: Tier 3 — Reporting & Audit Indexes

IDX-041

Attribute Detail
Table audit.inventory_movement_records
Indexed columns (stock_position_id, movement_timestamp DESC)
Index type B-tree (per monthly partition)
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM inventory_movement_records WHERE stock_position_id = ? ORDER BY movement_timestamp DESC LIMIT 100
Business justification Stock position history for investigation and audit (BO-19).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: "Show me last 100 movements for this SKU at this site." How: Composite index with DESC timestamp — PostgreSQL reads index backward for recent-first without sort. Partition note: Create this index on each monthly partition, not only parent table.

IDX-042

Attribute Detail
Table audit.inventory_movement_records
Indexed columns movement_timestamp
Index type BRIN
Expected query pattern SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory_movement_records WHERE movement_timestamp BETWEEN ? AND ?
Business justification Time-range reporting on very large append-only log (10M+ rows/year).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: BRIN is tiny compared to B-tree on timestamp — stores min/max per block range. How: Perfect for append-only data inserted in time order. When NOT to use: Point lookups by stock_position_id — use IDX-041 instead. BRIN complements, does not replace IDX-041.

IDX-043

Attribute Detail
Table audit.audit_trail_records
Indexed columns (affected_entity_type, affected_entity_id, event_timestamp DESC)
Index type B-tree (per monthly partition)
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM audit_trail_records WHERE affected_entity_type = 'stock_adjustments' AND affected_entity_id = ? ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC
Business justification Compliance audit trail per entity (BR-019, BO-19).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Auditor asks "full history of changes to adjustment #12345." How: Polymorphic lookup by type + id, sorted by time.

IDX-044

Attribute Detail
Table audit.operational_alerts
Indexed columns (acknowledgment_status, alert_type, severity) WHERE acknowledgment_status = 'OPEN'
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM operational_alerts WHERE acknowledgment_status = 'OPEN' ORDER BY severity DESC, alert_date
Business justification Alert dashboard and replenishment review (BR-009, BR-032).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Users see open alerts only — resolved alerts purged after 90 days. How: Partial index keeps dashboard query fast as alert table grows.

IDX-045

Attribute Detail
Table audit.inventory_valuation_snapshots
Indexed columns (valuation_date DESC, location_scope)
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM inventory_valuation_snapshots WHERE location_scope = 'NETWORK' ORDER BY valuation_date DESC LIMIT 12
Business justification Month-end valuation history (BR-031, BP-30).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Finance views last 12 monthly snapshots — low volume table, simple index sufficient.

IDX-046

Attribute Detail
Table audit.inventory_valuation_lines
Indexed columns snapshot_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM inventory_valuation_lines WHERE snapshot_id = ?
Business justification Load snapshot detail lines for reconciliation report.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Parent-child report pattern. How: FK index on snapshot header.

IDX-047

Attribute Detail
Table inventory.stock_policy_history
Indexed columns (stock_policy_id, effective_from DESC)
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM stock_policy_history WHERE stock_policy_id = ? ORDER BY effective_from DESC
Business justification Threshold change audit for replenishment analysis.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Planner reviews "when did reorder level change?" How: History lookup by policy id, recent first.

IDX-048

Attribute Detail
Table identity.role_assignments
Indexed columns (user_account_id) WHERE assignment_status = 'ACTIVE'
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM role_assignments WHERE user_account_id = ? AND assignment_status = 'ACTIVE'
Business justification Authorization check on every API request.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Login loads active roles only — not historical inactive assignments. How: Partial index for permission resolution.

IDX-049

Attribute Detail
Table identity.role_assignment_locations
Indexed columns role_assignment_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT location_id FROM role_assignment_locations WHERE role_assignment_id = ?
Business justification Location scope check for warehouse operations.
Performance clarity (junior) Why: After loading roles, load scoped locations. How: FK child index.

IDX-050

Attribute Detail
Table commercial.promotional_stock_allocations
Indexed columns (product_id, readiness_status) WHERE readiness_status IN ('PLANNED','READY','ACTIVE')
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM promotional_stock_allocations WHERE product_id = ? AND readiness_status = 'ACTIVE'
Business justification Campaign readiness review (BR-029).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Small table, few active campaigns — partial index for active/planned only.

IDX-051

Attribute Detail
Table commercial.promotional_allocation_locations
Indexed columns stock_position_id
Index type B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM promotional_allocation_locations WHERE stock_position_id = ?
Business justification Check ring-fence when reserving stock (BR-029).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Reservation service asks "is this balance ring-fenced for a campaign?" How: Reverse lookup from stock position to active allocation.

IDX-052

Attribute Detail
Table governance.governance_policies
Indexed columns (policy_type, effective_from DESC) WHERE is_active = TRUE AND effective_to IS NULL
Index type Partial B-tree
Expected query pattern SELECT * FROM governance_policies WHERE policy_type = 'APPROVAL_THRESHOLD' AND is_active = TRUE AND effective_to IS NULL
Business justification Load current effective policy for approval threshold check (BR-021).
Performance clarity (junior) Why: Only current active policies matter at runtime — not retired versions. How: Partial index on "currently effective" rows.

Part 6: Indexes Explicitly NOT Created

Avoiding unnecessary indexes is as important as creating the right ones.

Table / Column Why NOT indexed Junior explanation
products.description Never in WHERE/JOIN; TEXT search not required in IMS Full table scan on description search would need full-text (GIN) only if search feature added later
products.category_code Low-selectivity filter alone; network reports use stock_positions join Index on low-cardinality column alone rarely helps unless combined in composite with high-selectivity column
Every FK automatically PostgreSQL does not auto-index FKs Only index FKs that appear in JOIN/WHERE on the child side of frequent queries
stock_positions.product_id alone Covered by UK (product_id, location_id) leftmost prefix Composite UK already helps WHERE product_id = ? — separate single-column index is redundant
customer_orders.customer_reference Optional, low-cardinality, rare lookup Add only if CRM integration requires frequent search by customer_reference
shipments.tracking_identifier Lookup only after ship; nullable; not hot path Index when carrier tracking portal integration is confirmed
goods_receipts.supplier_id Receipts usually found by PO or GR number, not supplier Supplier performance reports are batch — acceptable sequential scan with date filter
audit_trail_records.before_state (JSONB) No JSON containment queries in scope GIN index is large — add only if "search audit JSON" feature is built
Duplicate index on reservation_status alone Low cardinality (3 values) without leading selective column Always combine with stock_position_id in partial index
inventory_write_offs, stock_adjustments by stock_position_id Low volume; approval queues use status partial indexes Historical adjustment lookup is rare — add if investigation tool requires it
All created_at columns Rarely filtered alone; use composite with status WHERE created_at > ? alone causes large index — prefer (status, created_at) if date filtering needed

Part 7: Index Maintenance Guide (Junior)

Monitoring

Check Tool Frequency
Unused indexes pg_stat_user_indexes where idx_scan = 0 Monthly
Bloated indexes pgstatindex or pg_repack Quarterly
Slow queries missing indexes pg_stat_statements, EXPLAIN ANALYZE Weekly on Tier 1

When INSERT/UPDATE feels slow

Ask: did we add an index we don't use? Each extra index adds write cost. Check idx_scan — if zero after 30 days in production, drop the index.

Partial index reminder

-- Conceptual example (not DDL for deployment)
Index: reservations WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'
Stores: only active rows
Query must include: reservation_status = 'ACTIVE' (or equivalent) for index to be used

If the query omits the WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' predicate, PostgreSQL cannot use the partial index.

Partitioned tables

inventory_movement_records and audit_trail_records are partitioned by month. Indexes must exist on each partition (PostgreSQL 11+ can create on parent and propagate). BRIN on movement_timestamp works well inside each partition.

inventory 4 1 1 3
procurement 2 2 0 4
inbound 1 2 0 1
finance 0 3 0 1
fulfillment 4 5 0 1
transfer 0 2 0 1
accuracy 0 3 0 4
returns 0 1 0 1
commercial 0 0 2 1
identity 1 0 2 2
governance 0 0 1 2
audit 0 0 6 2
Total explicit 16 21 12 ~28 used

Note: Several Tier 1 entries document implicit UK/PK indexes only. Total explicit indexes to CREATE: 49.

Part 9: Query Pattern → Index Quick Reference

Document ID: SRS-DB-005 | Version 1.0 | July 6, 2026

Database Audit Strategy

Inventory Management System — PostgreSQL

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-DB-006
Document Title Database Audit Strategy
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Database Architect
Source Documents SRS-DB-002 (Physical Data Model), SRS-DB-004 (Database Constraints), SRS-DM-006 (Domain Events), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rules), ADR-024 (Centralized Audit Trail Projection), Cross-Cutting Concerns §7
Target Platform PostgreSQL 15+
Date July 6, 2026
Scope Audit design, field standards, table classification, event catalog, retention — no DDL/SQL statements

Purpose

This document defines the database audit strategy for the Inventory Management System. Auditing supports traceability (who changed what, when, where, and why) and compliance (COSO internal control, financial record alignment, lot recall, segregation of duties). The strategy avoids audit sprawl: not every table receives the same treatment — audit depth matches business materiality.

Part 1: Audit Architecture Overview

1.1 Three-Layer Audit Model

Layer Mechanism Purpose Immutability
L1 — Row attribution Standard and entity-specific columns on transactional tables Current-state accountability; lightweight trace on every mutable row Mutable table rows can UPDATE; attribution columns capture last actor where applicable
L2 — Movement log audit.inventory_movement_records Append-only record of every stock quantity change with before/after quantities Append-only — no UPDATE/DELETE
L3 — Governance trail audit.audit_trail_records Before/after snapshots for material entity and policy changes Append-only — no UPDATE/DELETE

Supporting projections (not primary audit evidence):

Artifact Table Role
Threshold history inventory.stock_policy_history Dedicated history for replenishment policy changes
Operational alerts audit.operational_alerts Derived notifications — trace to source entity, not standalone evidence
Financial snapshots audit.inventory_valuation_snapshots + inventory_valuation_lines Point-in-time valuation evidence for reconciliation (BP-30)

1.2 Architectural Rules (from ADR-024, AUD-01–AUD-05)

Rule Requirement
AUD-01 Audit store records are append-only — application role has INSERT only on L2/L3 tables
AUD-02 Governance trail retained ≥ 7 years (NFR-COM-019, NFR-COM-020)
AUD-03 Single authoritative audit projection — no per-module duplicate audit tables
AUD-04 Domain events are the primary audit source; database audit tables are the persistence projection
AUD-05 Auditor evidence export within 15 minutes (NFR-PERF-026, NFR-COM-012)

1.3 What Auditing Is Not

Not audit Instead
Application debug logs Operational logging (NFR-LOG) — diagnostic, shorter retention
updated_at alone Insufficient for compliance — no actor, no before state, no reason
Duplicating movement + trail for every SELECT Read operations are authorized via security logs, not business audit trail
Indexing JSONB audit fields for ad-hoc search Structured query dimensions (affected_entity_type, user_id, event_timestamp)

Part 2: Standard Audit Fields

2.1 Platform-Wide Columns (L1)

Applied per SRS-DB-002 conventions on mutable tables.

Field Data Type Tables Business Purpose
created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() All mutable tables When the record was first persisted (UTC)
updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() Mutable tables with UPDATE lifecycle Last modification timestamp — maintained by application/trigger
version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 Transactional headers with concurrent updates Optimistic locking — detects lost updates; audit-relevant as conflict signal

2.2 Attribution Columns (L1 — actor tracking)

Field Data Type When Required Business Purpose
created_by BIGINT FK → identity.user_accounts Document creation (requisitions, receipts, orders) Who initiated the business document
initiated_by BIGINT FK Adjustments, write-offs, count workflows Who started a correction requiring approval
approved_by BIGINT FK Any approval-gated action (BR-019, BR-021, BR-023) Who authorized — SoD verification (must ≠ initiator/counter)
authorized_by BIGINT FK Quarantine release, write-off authorization Formal authorization for irreversible or high-risk actions
performed_by BIGINT FK Put-away, movement source events Who executed the physical operation
prepared_by BIGINT FK Valuation snapshots Who certified the financial snapshot

2.3 Workflow and Context Columns (L1 — traceability enrichment)

Field Data Type Tables Business Purpose
reason_code_id BIGINT FK → governance.reason_codes Adjustments, write-offs, some movements Why the change occurred (BR-020)
adjustment_reference / *_reference VARCHAR(64) Headers across domains Human-readable business key for external audit correspondence
qty_before / qty_after NUMERIC(18,4) Adjustments, movement records Quantity state transition evidence
approval_status VARCHAR(32) Gated documents Workflow state at time of audit
approval_chain_ref VARCHAR(128) Audit trail records Link to workflow engine instance
evidence_reference VARCHAR(128) Write-offs, variances External evidence (photo, inspector report)

2.4 L2 Movement Record Fields

Every stock mutation produces one row in audit.inventory_movement_records:

Field Purpose
movement_reference Correlates to source document line or transaction ID
movement_type RECEIPT, SHIPMENT, TRANSFER, ADJUSTMENT, WRITE_OFF, RESERVATION, RETURN, PUT_AWAY
stock_position_id, product_id, location_id Where and what changed (denormalized for query performance)
quantity_change, qty_before, qty_after What changed numerically
lot_batch_id Lot traceability (BR-017)
reason_code_id Why for adjustments and write-offs
source_document_type, source_document_id Originating document — receipt, shipment, adjustment, etc.
performed_by Who executed
movement_timestamp When (partition key)

2.5 L3 Audit Trail Record Fields

Material non-movement or co-material changes produce rows in audit.audit_trail_records:

Field Purpose
audit_event_reference Unique business event ID (correlates to domain event / outbox message)
affected_entity_type Logical table or entity name (e.g. stock_adjustments, products)
affected_entity_id PK of governed record
action_performed CREATE, UPDATE, APPROVE, CANCEL
user_id Actor
role_at_action Role at time of action — supports SoD retrospective review
before_state / after_state JSONB snapshots of changed attributes
approval_chain_ref Workflow reference when approval involved
movement_record_id Optional FK linking governance trail to L2 movement when both apply
event_timestamp When (partition key)

2.6 Recommended Application Audit Context (not stored on every row)

Passed from application layer to audit writer on each command — may be embedded in before_state/after_state or logged to security audit:

Context Field Purpose
correlation_id Traces one user action across multiple tables/events
session_id Links to authentication session
client_ip / user_agent Security investigation (security log primary; optional in trail)
location_scope Location context of the acting user
command_name Application command that triggered the change

Part 3: Tables Requiring Auditing

Tables are classified by audit tier. Higher tiers require more layers.

3.1 Tier Definitions

Tier L1 Columns L2 Movement L3 Trail Rationale
T0 — Audit store N/A (is audit) — Self Append-only audit tables
T1 — Stock mutation Full attribution Required on every qty change Required on approval/status transitions Financial and operational materiality
T2 — Governance & master created_at/updated_at + actor on change If qty affected Required on CREATE/UPDATE/DEACTIVATE Master data and policy integrity
T3 — Transactional document Full attribution on header Via lines/execution On status transitions (submit, approve, cancel, ship) Document lifecycle traceability
T4 — Line / child created_at only Via parent workflow Only if line is approval point Inherits header audit chain via FK
T5 — Reference / junction created_at only No No — parent audited Low independent materiality
T6 — Derived / snapshot created_at + prepared_by where applicable No No — immutable snapshot IS the record Point-in-time evidence

3.2 Complete Table Classification (59 tables)

T0 — Audit Store (5 tables)

Table Audit Treatment
audit.inventory_movement_records Append-only; DB role INSERT-only; monthly partition
audit.audit_trail_records Append-only; DB role INSERT-only; monthly partition
audit.operational_alerts Mutable status (ACKNOWLEDGED/RESOLVED); derived — not primary evidence
audit.inventory_valuation_snapshots Immutable after publish; financial evidence
audit.inventory_valuation_lines Immutable child of snapshot

T1 — Stock Mutation (11 tables)

Table L1 Fields L2 L3 Events
inventory.stock_positions created_at, updated_at, version, last_movement_at Every qty change Status/ownership changes
inventory.lot_batches created_at, updated_at Qty changes per lot Quality status, expiration corrections
inventory.quarantine_holds authorized_by, hold/release timestamps Hold apply/release qty CREATE, RELEASE, DISPOSE
fulfillment.inventory_reservations created_at, updated_at Reserve/release/fulfill Status transitions
inbound.put_aways performed_by ATP increase on completion Completion event
fulfillment.shipments created_at, updated_at Ship qty deduction Ship confirm, cancel
transfer.stock_transfers created_at, updated_at Transfer in/out Status transitions
transfer.in_transit_stock created_at, updated_at In-transit qty tracking Receive, loss, exception
accuracy.stock_adjustments initiated_by, approved_by, qty_before/after, reason_code_id On APPROVED PENDING→APPROVED/REJECTED
accuracy.inventory_write_offs initiated_by, authorized_by, reason_code_id On authorization CREATE, AUTHORIZE
returns.return_dispositions created_at, updated_at Restock/scrap qty Disposition decision

T2 — Governance & Master Data (11 tables)

Table L1 Fields L3 Events
catalog.products created_at, updated_at, created_by ProductRegistered, ProductStatusChanged, ABC classification
catalog.product_identifiers created_at, updated_at Identifier add/change (barcode integrity)
network.inventory_locations created_at, updated_at LocationActivated, LocationDeactivated
network.storage_positions created_at, updated_at StoragePositionConfigured
governance.governance_policies created_at, updated_at Policy threshold changes
governance.reason_codes created_at, updated_at Reason code add/deactivate
procurement.suppliers created_at, updated_at, is_active Supplier activation/deactivation
inventory.stock_policies created_at, updated_at Threshold create/update — also writes stock_policy_history
inventory.stock_policy_history Dedicated history table Is the audit artifact for policy changes
identity.user_accounts created_at, updated_at, account_status Account create, suspend, deactivate
identity.role_assignments created_at, updated_at, effective_from/to Role grant/revoke — security-critical

T3 — Transactional Documents (16 tables)

Table L1 Fields L3 Events
procurement.purchase_requisitions created_by, approved_by, version Submit, approve, reject, convert
procurement.purchase_orders created_at, updated_at, version Place, amend, cancel, close
inbound.goods_receipts created_at, updated_at, version Receive, close, discrepancy
inbound.receipt_discrepancies created_at, updated_at Discrepancy resolution
finance.supplier_invoices created_at, updated_at Register, match, authorize payment
finance.invoice_goods_receipt_match created_at Three-way match outcome (BR-008)
fulfillment.customer_orders created_at, updated_at, version Confirm, cancel, complete
fulfillment.fulfillment_executions created_at, updated_at Pick start, complete, exception
fulfillment.backorders created_at, updated_at Backorder create, fulfill, cancel
transfer.transfer_requests created_at, updated_at, approved_by Request, approve, reject
accuracy.cycle_counts created_at, updated_at Schedule, start, complete
accuracy.physical_inventory_counts created_at, updated_at Count certification (BR-024 freeze)
accuracy.count_variances initiated_by, approved_by Variance identification, approval (BR-019)
returns.return_authorizations created_at, updated_at, version RMA issue, cancel, expire
returns.customer_returns created_at, updated_at Return receipt
commercial.promotional_stock_allocations created_at, updated_at Campaign allocation create/amend (BR-029)

T4 — Line / Child Tables (15 tables)

Inherit audit chain from parent header via FK. L3 trail written at header level unless line is the approval point.

Table Parent Line-Level L3 When
catalog.product_identifiers products Barcode change (also T2)
procurement.purchase_requisition_lines purchase_requisitions —
procurement.purchase_order_lines purchase_orders —
procurement.expected_inbound_deliveries — Status changes
procurement.expected_inbound_delivery_lines expected_inbound_deliveries —
inbound.goods_receipt_lines goods_receipts Lot capture (BR-017)
finance.supplier_invoice_lines supplier_invoices —
fulfillment.customer_order_lines customer_orders —
fulfillment.fulfillment_pick_lines fulfillment_executions Pick confirmation
fulfillment.shipment_lines shipments —
transfer.transfer_request_lines transfer_requests —
transfer.stock_transfer_lines stock_transfers —
returns.return_authorization_lines return_authorizations —
returns.customer_return_lines customer_returns —
commercial.promotional_allocation_locations promotional_stock_allocations —

T5 — Junction / Scope (1 table)

Table Treatment

T6 — Derived Snapshots (2 tables — also in T0)

Table Treatment
audit.inventory_valuation_snapshots Immutable financial point-in-time; prepared_by required
audit.inventory_valuation_lines Immutable detail; no UPDATE after snapshot publish

3.3 Tables Explicitly NOT Requiring L3 Trail

Table Reason
identity.role_assignment_locations Junction — parent role assignment carries audit
All T4 line tables (unless noted) Parent document audit + movement log captures qty impact
audit.operational_alerts Derived notification — auditors trace via source_entity_type/id to source

Part 4: Audit Tables

4.1 Primary Audit Tables

audit.inventory_movement_records — Operational Quantity Audit

Aspect Detail
Purpose Immutable log of every stock quantity change
Populated by Domain event handlers after successful stock mutation commit
Cardinality 1+ per stock mutation; links to source document
Growth Very high (10M–100M+/year)
Partitioning Monthly range on movement_timestamp
Permissions Application role: INSERT only
Linked from audit.audit_trail_records.movement_record_id when co-material

audit.audit_trail_records — Governance Compliance Audit

Aspect Detail
Purpose Before/after snapshots for material entity and policy changes
Populated by M-13 Intelligence projection from domain events + command audit context
Cardinality 0–1 per material command; may pair with movement record
Growth Very high (proportional to governed mutations)
Partitioning Monthly range on event_timestamp
Permissions Application role: INSERT only
JSONB scope Changed attributes only — not full row dump unless material

inventory.stock_policy_history — Dedicated Policy History

Aspect Detail
Purpose Threshold change history without polluting operational stock tables
Populated by Trigger or application on stock_policies UPDATE
Retention Align with governance trail (7 years)

4.2 Supporting Audit Artifacts

Table Audit Role Retention
audit.operational_alerts Exception and threshold notification trail Purge resolved > 90 days
audit.inventory_valuation_snapshots Financial reconciliation evidence (BP-30) 7 years
audit.inventory_valuation_lines Snapshot detail 7 years (with parent)

4.3 Audit Write Flow

User Command
    │
    ├─► [Application] Enrich AuditContext (user, role, correlation, reason)
    │
    ├─► [Domain] Mutate aggregate + raise domain event
    │
    ├─► [DB Transaction] UPDATE transactional table (L1 columns)
    │                      INSERT movement record (L2) if qty changed
    │
    └─► [Post-commit Handler] INSERT audit_trail_record (L3) from event payload

Rule: L2 and L3 writes occur in the same database transaction as the stock mutation when possible. L3 from async projection is acceptable only for non-qty master data changes with eventual consistency ≤ 5 seconds.

4.4 Before/After Snapshot Guidelines (JSONB)

Entity Type Include in before_state / after_state
stock_positions on_hand_qty, reserved_qty, quarantined_qty, atp_qty, stock_status, ownership_type
stock_adjustments adjustment_qty, approval_status, reason_code_id, initiated_by, approved_by
products sku, product_status, abc_classification, is_traceable, unit_of_measure
inventory_locations location_code, operational_status, location_type
role_assignments role_name, assignment_status, effective_from, effective_to, sod_compliant
supplier_invoices invoice_status, match_status, total_amount, authorization_status
governance_policies Policy type, threshold values, effective dates

Exclude: Large TEXT blobs, redundant denormalized fields already on movement record, PII beyond user_id reference.

Part 5: Business Events to Audit

Events map to domain events (SRS-DM-006). Each material event produces at minimum L1 update; stock events also produce L2; governance events produce L3.

5.1 Stock & Balance Events (L2 + L3)

Event ID Domain Event Source Table(s) Movement Type L3 Action
AE-001 StockIncreased (receipt) goods_receipts, put_aways, stock_positions RECEIPT / PUT_AWAY APPROVE on put-away complete
AE-002 StockReserved inventory_reservations, stock_positions RESERVATION UPDATE
AE-003 ReservationReleased inventory_reservations RESERVATION (negative) UPDATE
AE-004 StockShipped shipments, shipment_lines SHIPMENT APPROVE
AE-005 StockTransferred stock_transfers, in_transit_stock TRANSFER UPDATE
AE-006 TransferReceived stock_transfers, in_transit_stock TRANSFER APPROVE
AE-007 StockAdjusted stock_adjustments ADJUSTMENT APPROVE
AE-008 StockWrittenOff inventory_write_offs WRITE_OFF APPROVE
AE-009 StockQuarantined quarantine_holds ADJUSTMENT (quarantine bucket) CREATE
AE-010 QuarantineReleased quarantine_holds ADJUSTMENT UPDATE
AE-011 ReturnRestocked return_dispositions, customer_returns RETURN APPROVE
AE-012 LotQuantityChanged lot_batches Per parent movement UPDATE if lot attrs change

5.2 Inbound & Procurement Events (L3; L2 on receipt)

Event ID Domain Event Source Table(s) L3 Action
AE-020 PurchaseRequisitionSubmitted purchase_requisitions UPDATE
AE-021 PurchaseRequisitionApproved purchase_requisitions APPROVE
AE-022 PurchaseOrderPlaced purchase_orders CREATE
AE-023 PurchaseOrderCancelled purchase_orders CANCEL
AE-024 GoodsReceived goods_receipts CREATE
AE-025 ReceiptDiscrepancyIdentified receipt_discrepancies CREATE
AE-026 PutAwayCompleted put_aways APPROVE

5.3 Fulfillment Events (L2 + L3)

Event ID Domain Event Source Table(s) L3 Action
AE-030 CustomerOrderConfirmed customer_orders UPDATE
AE-031 CustomerOrderCancelled customer_orders CANCEL
AE-032 FulfillmentStarted fulfillment_executions UPDATE
AE-033 PickConfirmed fulfillment_pick_lines UPDATE
AE-034 ShipmentDispatched shipments APPROVE
AE-035 BackorderCreated backorders CREATE

5.4 Inventory Control Events (L2 + L3 — SoD critical)

Event ID Domain Event Source Table(s) L3 Action Compliance Note
AE-040 CycleCountStarted cycle_counts UPDATE —
AE-041 PhysicalInventoryCountCertified physical_inventory_counts APPROVE BR-024 freeze evidence
AE-042 CountVarianceIdentified count_variances CREATE Counter recorded
AE-043 CountVarianceApproved count_variances APPROVE Approver ≠ counter (BR-019)
AE-044 AdjustmentApproved stock_adjustments APPROVE Approver ≠ initiator (BR-021)
AE-045 WriteOffAuthorized inventory_write_offs APPROVE Dual authorization (BR-023)

5.5 Financial & Governance Events (L3)

Event ID Domain Event Source Table(s) L3 Action Compliance Note
AE-050 ThreeWayMatchCompleted invoice_goods_receipt_match APPROVE BR-008 payment gate
AE-051 InvoicePaymentAuthorized supplier_invoices APPROVE Financial control
AE-052 GovernancePolicyChanged governance_policies UPDATE Threshold audit
AE-053 ReasonCodeDeactivated reason_codes UPDATE Prevents orphan reasons
AE-054 ValuationSnapshotPublished inventory_valuation_snapshots CREATE BP-30 reconciliation

5.6 Master Data & Security Events (L3)

Event ID Domain Event Source Table(s) L3 Action Compliance Note
AE-060 ProductStatusChanged products UPDATE BR-027 discontinued
AE-061 InventoryLocationDeactivated inventory_locations UPDATE Closure authorization
AE-062 SupplierDeactivated suppliers UPDATE Procurement block
AE-063 RoleAssigned role_assignments CREATE Access control
AE-064 RoleRevoked role_assignments UPDATE Access control
AE-065 UserAccountDeactivated user_accounts UPDATE Security
AE-066 SoDViolationAttemptBlocked — (security log + L3) CREATE BR-019, BR-021

5.7 Traceability-Specific Events (Lot Recall)

Event ID Domain Event Tables Audit Requirement
AE-070 LotCapturedAtReceipt goods_receipt_lines, lot_batches L2 with lot_batch_id; L3 on lot create
AE-071 LotMovedWithTransfer stock_transfer_lines, lot_batches L2 must carry lot_batch_id
AE-072 LotShippedToCustomer shipment_lines, lot_batches L2 for recall forward trace
AE-073 LotRecalled quarantine_holds, lot_batches L3 + L2; hold_type = RECALL

Recall query pattern: Forward trace from lot_batches → inventory_movement_records by lot_batch_id; backward from shipment to receipt via movement chain.

5.8 Events NOT Written to L3 Trail

Event / Operation Reason
Read-only queries (ATP lookup, dashboards) Not a state change — security log only if required
Alert generation Derived — source condition already audited
Cache invalidation Infrastructure — not business audit
Failed validation (pre-commit) No state change — operational log
Optimistic lock retry (success) Only final successful commit audited

Part 6: Retention Policy Considerations

6.1 Retention Tiers

Tier Storage Access Pattern Technology
Hot 0–24 months Sub-second operational queries PostgreSQL primary — partitioned
Warm 25 months–7 years Auditor search, compliance export PostgreSQL archive schema or read replica
Cold 7+ years (if mandated beyond) Legal hold, rare retrieval Object storage (Parquet/CSV), compressed
Purge After retention expiry None Secure deletion per legal approval

6.2 Table-Specific Retention

Table / Data Class Hot (online) Total Retention Purge Rule Regulatory Driver
audit.inventory_movement_records 24 months 7 years total Archive partition to warm/cold; drop after 7 years Financial records alignment (NFR-COM-020); lot traceability (BR-017)
audit.audit_trail_records 24 months 7 years minimum Tiered archive; legal hold overrides purge COSO, external audit (BO-19, NFR-COM-010)
inventory.stock_policy_history Full period 7 years Archive with governance trail Replenishment decision audit
audit.inventory_valuation_snapshots + lines 36 months 7 years Archive with finance records Month-end close, BP-30
Security audit events (login, SoD) 24 months 7 years Separate security log store NFR-COM-020
audit.operational_alerts 90 days resolved 90 days after RESOLVED Scheduled purge job Operational — not compliance primary
Transactional documents (closed PO, orders) 36 months 7 years Archive closed documents Commercial dispute resolution
identity.user_accounts (deactivated) Active + 36 months 7 years after deactivation Pseudonymize PII per legal matrix GDPR vs audit (C-05) — legal sign-off required
Operational application logs 90 days 1 year Standard log rotation NFR-LOG — not compliance audit

6.3 Partitioning and Archival Mechanics

Table Partition Key Archival Action
inventory_movement_records movement_timestamp (monthly) DETACH PARTITION → export to cold → DROP from hot after 24 months
audit_trail_records event_timestamp (monthly) Same; retain detached partitions in warm store until year 7
Others Not partitioned Row-level archive job by created_at / status

6.4 Legal Hold and Compliance Overrides

Scenario Action
Active litigation / regulatory investigation Suspend purge for affected lot_batch_id, product_id, date range, or user_id
Recall event (AE-073) Extend movement retention for affected lots — no purge until recall closed
GDPR erasure request (C-05) Pseudonymize user_accounts.display_name/email; retain user_id in audit trail for compliance
External auditor export (AUD-05) Hot+warm data exportable within 15 minutes — pre-built evidence package views

6.5 Immutability Enforcement

Control Implementation
Database permissions audit_writer role: INSERT on L2/L3 only; no UPDATE/DELETE
Application No ORM update paths to audit tables
Trigger guard (optional) BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE → RAISE EXCEPTION on audit tables
Monitoring Alert on any DDL against audit schema
Hash chain (future) Optional record_hash + previous_hash on L3 for tamper evidence — not in v1.0

6.6 Storage Growth Estimates (Planning)

Table Annual Rows (est.) Row Size (est.) 7-Year Storage (est.)
inventory_movement_records 50M ~500 bytes ~175 GB + indexes
audit_trail_records 10M ~2 KB (JSONB) ~140 GB + indexes
operational_alerts 2M (rolling) ~300 bytes < 1 GB (purged)

Implication: Hot PostgreSQL cannot hold 7 years of movement data at scale — tiered architecture is mandatory (ADR-026, Architecture Review G-05).

Part 7: Segregation of Duties (SoD) Audit Requirements

Business Rule Audit Evidence Required Tables
BR-019 Counter ≠ variance approver count_variances.initiated_by vs approved_by + L3 trail
BR-021 Initiator ≠ adjustment approver stock_adjustments.initiated_by vs approved_by + L3 trail
BR-023 Write-off requires authorization inventory_write_offs.initiated_by vs authorized_by
BR-008 Three-way match before payment invoice_goods_receipt_match + L3 APPROVE
Identity SoD Role conflict blocked role_assignments.sod_compliant, AE-066 on violation attempt

Auditor query pattern: Join L3 audit_trail_records where action_performed = 'APPROVE' and compare user_id to before_state.initiated_by.

Part 8: Implementation Checklist

# Task Owner
1 Apply L1 audit columns per table tier in migrations DBA
2 Create audit_writer DB role with INSERT-only on L2/L3 DBA
3 Implement movement record writer in stock mutation transaction Backend
4 Implement audit trail projection handler (M-13) Backend
5 Map domain events AE-001–AE-073 to audit writers Backend
6 Configure monthly partitions on movement and trail tables DBA
7 Build partition detach/archive job (hot → warm) DevOps
8 Define legal hold flag and purge suspension Legal + DBA
9 Privacy matrix for GDPR vs 7-year retention (G-09) Legal
10 Auditor export views / evidence package (AUD-05) Intelligence module

Part 9: Summary Matrix

Audit Layer Tables Write Trigger Retention
L1 Row attribution 54 mutable tables Every INSERT/UPDATE Life of row
L2 Movement log Stock mutations (11 source tables) Every qty change 7 years (tiered)
L3 Governance trail 35 material tables/events Material commands 7 years (tiered)
Policy history stock_policy_history Policy UPDATE 7 years
Financial snapshot Valuation tables Period close 7 years

Document ID: SRS-DB-006 | Version 1.0 | July 6, 2026

Database Naming Conventions

Inventory Management System — PostgreSQL

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-DB-008
Document Title Database Naming Conventions
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Database Architect
Source Documents SRS-DB-002 (PDM), SRS-DB-003 (Keys), SRS-DB-004 (Constraints), SRS-DB-005 (Indexing), SRS-DB-006 (Audit)
Target Platform PostgreSQL 15+
Date July 6, 2026
Scope Naming standards for all database objects — no DDL/SQL statements

Purpose

This document defines consistent, scalable naming conventions for the Inventory Management System database. All new objects — tables, columns, keys, constraints, indexes, sequences, and views — must follow these standards. Conventions align with existing SRS-DB artifacts and PostgreSQL identifier limits (63 characters).

Global Rules

Rule Standard
Case Lowercase only — snake_case for all identifiers
Characters Letters, digits, underscores; start with a letter
Length Target ≤ 40 characters; hard limit 63 (PostgreSQL)
Reserved words Avoid PostgreSQL reserved words (user, order, position) — qualify with schema or use plural/descriptive names (user_accounts, customer_orders, storage_positions)
Abbreviations Use only approved abbreviations (see Appendix A); prefer full words for clarity
Pluralization Tables: plural nouns (products, stock_positions). Columns: singular attribute names (product_id, order_date)
Language American English spelling in identifiers (canceled → use domain value CANCELLED in data, not in object names)
Bounded context Schema name reflects domain module — not dbo or public for application tables

1. Schemas

1.1 Naming Pattern

{bounded_context_noun}
Rule Detail
Format Single lowercase noun or compound noun — no prefix/suffix
Count One schema per bounded context (14 schemas in IMS)
public Reserved for extensions only — application tables do not use public

1.2 Approved Schemas

Schema Purpose
catalog Product master data
network Locations and storage positions
governance Policies and reason codes
inventory Stock balances, lots, holds, policies
procurement Suppliers, requisitions, purchase orders
inbound Goods receipt, discrepancies, put-away
finance Supplier invoices and three-way match
fulfillment Customer orders, reservations, picks, shipments
transfer Inter-location transfers
accuracy Cycle counts, adjustments, write-offs
returns RMA and customer returns
commercial Promotional allocations
identity Users and role assignments
audit Movement log, audit trail, alerts, valuation

1.3 Fully Qualified References

Always use schema-qualified names in documentation, migrations, and cross-schema FK definitions:

inventory.stock_positions
fulfillment.customer_orders

2. Tables

2.1 Naming Pattern

{entity_noun_plural}

or for associative / junction tables:

{parent_a}_{parent_b}          -- when relationship is the entity
{parent_entity}_{role_noun}      -- e.g. stock_policy_history, invoice_goods_receipt_match
Rule Detail
Plural Tables hold collections — products, not product
Prefix No tbl_, t_, or module prefix — schema provides context
Suffix Avoid _table; use _history, _lines, _match only when semantically required
Line tables Parent name + _lines — purchase_order_lines, goods_receipt_lines
Header documents Domain noun — purchase_orders, goods_receipts, customer_orders
Log / audit tables _records suffix for append-only logs — inventory_movement_records, audit_trail_records
Max length ≤ 40 characters recommended

2.2 Examples

Good Bad Reason
stock_positions StockPosition Must be snake_case lowercase
inventory_reservations inv_res No unapproved abbreviations
invoice_goods_receipt_match inv_gr_match_tbl No tbl_ prefix; spell out
user_accounts users Avoid reserved word user
put_aways putaway Compound operations use underscore

2.3 Table Partition Naming (High-Volume Tables)

{parent_table}_{partition_bound}
Partition Type Pattern Example
Monthly range {table}_y{YYYY}m{MM} inventory_movement_records_y2026m07
Yearly archive {table}_y{YYYY} customer_orders_y2023

Partition child tables inherit parent naming root. Partition key column: movement_timestamp, event_timestamp.

3. Columns

3.1 General Rules

Rule Detail
Format snake_case, singular attribute name
Boolean Prefix is_ or has_ — is_active, has_sod_conflict, pack_confirmed
Timestamps Suffix _at for point-in-time — created_at, reserved_at, released_at
Dates Suffix _date for calendar date — order_date, expiration_date
Quantities Suffix _qty — on_hand_qty, reserved_qty, adjustment_qty
Amounts Suffix _amount or _value — total_amount, financial_value, line_amount
Status Suffix _status — order_status, approval_status, match_status
Type / category Suffix _type — movement_type, hold_type, ownership_type
Codes Suffix _code — reason_code, category_code, currency_code
References Suffix _reference or _ref — movement_reference, approval_chain_ref
Counts Suffix _count — total_variances (exception: use _number for business document numbers)

3.2 Standard Platform Columns

Apply consistently per table type (see SRS-DB-002):

Column Type Tables Meaning
id BIGINT All Surrogate primary key
version INTEGER Mutable transactional headers Optimistic lock counter
is_active BOOLEAN Master / reference data Soft-delete flag
created_at TIMESTAMPTZ Mutable tables Row creation timestamp (UTC)
updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ Mutable tables with UPDATE Last modification timestamp
created_by BIGINT Document headers Creating user FK
line_number INTEGER Document line tables Sequence within parent document

3.3 Foreign Key Column Naming

{referenced_table_singular}_id
Referenced Table FK Column Notes
products product_id Singular entity + _id
inventory_locations location_id Drop redundant prefix when unambiguous in context
stock_positions stock_position_id Full entity name when abbreviation is ambiguous
user_accounts user_id or role-specific — see below

Role-specific user FKs (when multiple users on one row):

Column Meaning
created_by Record creator
initiated_by Workflow initiator
approved_by Approver
authorized_by Formal authorizer
performed_by Physical executor
prepared_by Snapshot preparer
counter_id Cycle count performer
inspector_id Return inspector
receiving_clerk_id Receipt operator
assigned_picker_id Pick assignee
approver_id Variance approver (when approved_by not used)

Do not use user_id when a role-specific name is clearer.

3.4 Business Key Columns

Natural identifiers use domain terms — not business_key or code alone:

Entity Column
Product sku
Location location_code
Purchase order po_number
Customer order order_number
Goods receipt gr_number
Shipment shipment_number
RMA rma_number

3.5 Denormalized Columns

When FK target is duplicated for query performance, use same name as canonical FK:

product_id    -- denormalized on lot_batches, movement_records
location_id   -- denormalized on movement_records

Comment in data dictionary: "(denormalized)" — do not use product_id_dup or product_id_fk2.

3.6 Anti-Patterns

Avoid Use Instead
desc description
amt amount
qty1, qty2 qty_before, qty_after
status1 approval_status, order_status
data, info, misc Domain-specific name
Hungarian notation (strName, iCount) product_name, line_count

4. Primary Keys

4.1 Column Standard

Attribute Standard
Column name id — always, on every table
Data type BIGINT
Generation GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY (preferred over sequences)
Nullability NOT NULL
Uniqueness Single-column primary key only — no composite PKs

4.2 Constraint Naming

pk_{table_name}

{table_name} is the table name without schema prefix.

Table PK Constraint Name
catalog.products pk_products
inventory.stock_positions pk_stock_positions
audit.inventory_movement_records pk_inventory_movement_records

4.3 Rationale

  • Surrogate id is stable across business key changes (sku format evolution).
  • Narrow BIGINT PK optimizes FK indexes and joins.
  • Single-column PK simplifies ORM mapping and partition key design.
  • Business uniqueness enforced via unique constraints, not composite PKs.

5. Foreign Keys

5.1 Column Standard

See §3.3. Every FK column references parent id unless documented otherwise.

5.2 Constraint Naming

fk_{child_table}_{parent_entity_or_role}
Rule Detail
Prefix fk_
Child Child table name (without schema)
Parent Parent table singular noun or role qualifier
Length Truncate parent qualifier if > 63 chars — keep child table name intact

5.3 Examples

Child Table Column FK Constraint Name
product_identifiers product_id fk_product_identifiers_product
stock_positions product_id fk_stock_positions_product
stock_positions location_id fk_stock_positions_location
products created_by fk_products_created_by
purchase_requisitions triggering_alert_id fk_purchase_requisitions_alert
audit_trail_records movement_record_id fk_audit_trail_movement

5.4 Self-Referencing FKs

fk_{table}_{relationship_role}
Table Column Constraint Name
inventory_locations parent_location_id fk_inventory_locations_parent

5.5 Cross-Schema FKs

Permitted and named identically. Schema qualification appears in DDL target, not constraint name:

fk_goods_receipts_purchase_order   → procurement.purchase_orders(id)
fk_stock_adjustments_reason_code   → governance.reason_codes(id)

5.6 Index Requirement

PostgreSQL does not auto-index FK columns. Create supporting index per SRS-DB-005 when column appears in JOIN/WHERE. Index name follows §7 — not the FK constraint name.

6. Constraints

6.1 Naming Pattern

{type_prefix}_{table_name}_{column_or_scope}

6.2 Type Prefixes

Constraint Type Prefix Example
Primary key pk_ pk_products
Foreign key fk_ fk_products_created_by
Unique uk_ uk_products_sku
Check chk_ chk_products_lifecycle_status
Not null nn_ nn_products_sku
Default def_ def_products_created_at

Note: PostgreSQL merges NOT NULL and DEFAULT into column definitions — nn_ and def_ names are logical/documentation identifiers used in SRS-DB-004; use in migration comments or extended property metadata.

6.3 Unique Constraint Naming

uk_{table}_{column}
uk_{table}_{col1}_{col2}        -- composite; omit redundant table prefix on columns
Table Column(s) Constraint Name
products sku uk_products_sku
stock_positions (product_id, location_id) uk_stock_positions_product_location
product_identifiers (identifier_type, identifier_value) uk_product_identifiers_type_value
supplier_invoices (supplier_id, invoice_number) uk_supplier_invoices_supplier_number
audit_trail_records (audit_event_reference, event_timestamp) uk_audit_trail_ref_ts

6.4 Check Constraint Naming

chk_{table}_{column_or_rule}
Scope Pattern Example
Single column domain chk_{table}_{column} chk_products_lifecycle_status
Cross-column rule chk_{table}_{rule_short_name} chk_stock_positions_atp_formula
Shared domain (reusable) chk_domain_{domain_name} chk_domain_approval_status

Shared domain checks — when identical value sets apply across tables, use chk_domain_* prefix and document in SRS-DB-004 Appendix. Table-level checks may alias the same rule.

6.5 Composite Constraint Scope Abbreviations

When column list exceeds name length, use semantic scope:

Scope Token Meaning
product_location (product_id, location_id)
type_value (identifier_type, identifier_value)
ref_ts (reference, timestamp) partition uniqueness
atp_formula atp_qty = on_hand_qty - reserved_qty - quarantined_qty

7. Indexes

7.1 Naming Pattern

idx_{table}_{column_or_scope}[_{suffix}]
Rule Detail
Prefix idx_ — distinguishes from unique constraints (uk_)
Table Child table name without schema
Columns Leading column names joined by underscore; omit _id suffix on single FK when clear
Suffix Optional qualifier for special index types

7.2 Index Type Suffixes

Index Type Suffix Example
B-tree (default) (none) idx_reservations_stock_position
Partial index _partial_{predicate_short} idx_reservations_stock_position_partial_active
BRIN _brin idx_movement_records_brin
GIN (JSONB) _gin idx_audit_trail_before_state_gin
DESC sort _desc on column idx_movement_records_position_timestamp_desc

7.3 Examples

Table Index Columns Index Name
stock_positions (location_id, stock_status) partial LOW/OUT idx_stock_positions_location_status_partial_low
inventory_reservations (stock_position_id) WHERE ACTIVE idx_reservations_stock_position_partial_active
inventory_movement_records (stock_position_id, movement_timestamp DESC) idx_movement_records_position_timestamp_desc
inventory_movement_records movement_timestamp BRIN idx_movement_records_brin
goods_receipts purchase_order_id idx_goods_receipts_purchase_order
customer_orders (order_status, order_date DESC) idx_customer_orders_status_date_desc

7.4 Rules

Rule Detail
UK/PK indexes Do not create duplicate idx_ when uk_ or pk_ already provides the index
FK indexes Name after FK column, not FK constraint name
Max length Abbreviate column scope tokens (§6.5) before truncating table name
Partitioned tables Index on parent propagates to partitions — name on parent only
One partial per predicate Do not create both full and partial index on same columns

7.5 Strategy Document Cross-Reference

Logical index IDs in SRS-DB-005 (IDX-001 – IDX-052) map to physical names during DDL generation:

IDX-004 → idx_reservations_stock_position_partial_active
IDX-005 → idx_lot_batches_position_expiration

8. Sequences

8.1 Preferred Approach — Identity Columns

IMS does not use standalone sequences for primary keys. All tables use:

id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY

Implicit sequence names are PostgreSQL-generated ({table}_id_seq) — do not rename unless required for replication tooling.

8.2 When Standalone Sequences Are Permitted

Use only for business reference number generation outside PK identity:

Use Case Example
Document number pools PO number series per location
External-facing reference ranges Movement reference batch

8.3 Sequence Naming Pattern

seq_{purpose}_{scope}
Rule Detail
Prefix seq_
Purpose Document or reference type
Scope Optional location or year qualifier

8.4 Examples

Sequence Name Purpose
seq_movement_reference Global movement reference counter
seq_po_number_wh01 PO numbers scoped to location WH-01
seq_audit_event_y2026 Annual audit event reference partition

8.5 Business Reference Column Naming

Generated business references use _reference or domain-specific _number — not the sequence name:

Sequence Populates Column
seq_movement_reference movement_reference
seq_po_number_wh01 po_number

9. Views

9.1 Naming Pattern

vw_{purpose}_{entity_or_scope}
Rule Detail
Prefix vw_ — distinguishes from tables
Purpose rpt_ segment optional for reporting — vw_rpt_open_orders
Materialized Prefix mvw_ — mvw_dashboard_atp_summary
No v_ Use vw_ consistently (two-letter prefix improves readability)

9.2 Schema Placement

View Type Schema Example
Operational read models Same schema as source or audit audit.vw_rpt_open_alerts
Cross-domain reporting audit (M-13 Intelligence) audit.vw_rpt_atp_by_location
Auditor export (AUD-05) audit audit.vw_export_audit_evidence
Application convenience Avoid — prefer explicit queries or ORM projections

9.3 Examples

View Name Purpose
vw_rpt_stock_position_atp ATP summary with product and location names
vw_rpt_open_purchase_orders Open PO dashboard
vw_rpt_pending_approvals Cross-table approval queue
vw_rpt_movement_history Movement log with denormalized product SKU
mvw_rpt_low_stock_alerts Materialized low-stock dashboard (refreshed on schedule)
vw_export_audit_trail Auditor evidence package source

9.4 Column Naming in Views

Rule Detail
Inherit Use source column names unchanged when exposing base columns
Computed snake_case descriptive — days_until_expiry, is_below_reorder
Alias prefix Do not prefix with vw_ — vw_atp_qty is wrong; use atp_qty
Consistency Same business term as base table — sku, not product_sku_code

9.5 View Object Comments

Every view must have a COMMENT ON VIEW describing purpose, refresh policy (if materialized), and source tables.

10. Additional Database Objects

10.1 Triggers

trg_{table}_{timing}_{event}_{purpose}
Example Event
trg_stock_policies_after_update_history Append stock_policy_history on policy change
trg_audit_trail_records_before_update_block Prevent UPDATE on audit tables
trg_stock_positions_before_update_timestamp Maintain updated_at

Timing: before / after. Event: insert / update / delete.

10.2 Functions and Procedures

fn_{verb}_{entity}          -- returns scalar or set
sp_{verb}_{entity}          -- procedure (side effects)
Example Purpose
fn_calculate_atp ATP derivation
sp_archive_movement_partition Partition detach and archive

10.3 Database Roles

ims_{module}_{access_level}
Example Purpose
ims_app_readwrite Application DML role
ims_audit_writer INSERT-only on audit tables
ims_reporting_read SELECT-only for BI
ims_migration_admin DDL migration role

10.4 Enum Types (If Used)

Prefer VARCHAR(32) + CHECK constraints in IMS. If native PostgreSQL enums are introduced:

{schema}.{domain}_enum

Example: inventory.ownership_type_enum — use only when value set is truly immutable.

11. Scalability Guidelines

11.1 Adding New Tables

  1. Assign to correct schema (bounded context).
  2. Use plural table name ≤ 40 characters.
  3. Include id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY as PK.
  4. Apply standard audit columns per table tier (SRS-DB-006).
  5. Name constraints and indexes before first deployment — renaming in production is costly.

11.2 Adding New Columns

  1. Follow suffix conventions (§3.1).
  2. FK columns: {entity}_id referencing parent id.
  3. Add nn_, chk_, fk_ constraints with names per §6.
  4. Add index per §7 if column is filtered or joined frequently.
  5. Update SRS-DB-007 Data Dictionary.

11.3 Name Collision Resolution

Situation Resolution
Same entity name in two schemas Schema qualifies — catalog.products vs external erp.products (avoid — use erp_product_id FK column instead)
Long composite UK name Abbreviate scope tokens (§6.5), not table name
Index name > 63 chars Drop _id suffixes from column tokens first, then abbreviate scope

11.4 Prohibited Practices

Practice Reason
Hungarian notation Reduces readability for BAs and developers
Single-letter column names Not self-documenting
Duplicate indexes (UK + idx) Wastes write performance and storage
Renaming id to {table}_id on PK Breaks ORM and convention consistency
Mixed case identifiers PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase — use snake_case explicitly
Quotes in identifiers Requires quoted SQL everywhere — avoid

fifo first in first out Domain values

desc Never — use description —

Part VIII — API Design

REST API Catalog

Inventory Management System

Document Information

Attribute Detail
Document ID SRS-API-001
Document Title REST API Catalog — Inventory Management System
Version 1.0
Status Draft
Document Owner Senior Backend Architect
Source Documents BRD-IMS-001 (v1.0), SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog), SRS-DM-003 (Domain Aggregates), SRS-ES-002 (Domain Commands), SRS-ES-005 (Read Models), SRS-SA-003 (System Modules Design), SRS-SA-005 (Integration Architecture Design), SRS-DB (Database Design)
Date July 6, 2026
Scope REST API identification only — endpoints, methods, purpose, and traceability. Request/response structures are out of scope.

Purpose

This catalog identifies all REST APIs required to support the Inventory Management System. Each API is traced to a business module, use case, and domain aggregate derived from approved business and architecture artifacts. APIs align with the 13 logical system modules (M-01–M-13) and expose the published commands and queries defined in the System Modules Design.

API Conventions

Convention Rule
Base path /api/v1
Resource naming Plural nouns, kebab-case path segments
Identifiers ProductSku, LocationCode, and other published-language identifiers in path or query
Command actions POST to sub-resource action paths (e.g., /orders/{id}/confirm)
Queries GET with filter query parameters
Idempotency Safe retries on PUT and idempotent POST where saga compensation applies
Authorization All endpoints require authenticated session (SVC-01 IdP); location-scoped RBAC enforced per UC-045

Reference Meaning

M-xx Business Module (SRS-SA-003)
CMD-xxx Domain Command (SRS-ES-002) — write API origin
RM-xxx Read Model (SRS-ES-005) — query API origin
