Charts require labels and patterns. Export actions need descriptive names, not generic icon-only controls.

Inventory Valuation Reconciliation

Compare operational valuation with finance records, investigate differences, and finalize reconciliation status.

Period selector and summary cards at top, side-by-side valuation comparison area, notes panel, and supporting variance tables.

Reports & Analytics > Valuation Reconciliation, with contextual links to variance drill-down and finance evidence.

5. Components
Summary cards, comparison panel, notes form, report viewer, export actions, status badges.

6. Tables
Valuation comparison table and adjustment/variance detail table.

7. Forms
Period end date, variance threshold percent, reconciliation notes, finalization status.

8. Buttons
Load Period, Add Note, Finalize Reconciliation, Export.

9. Icons
Finance/ledger icon, compare icon, variance warning icon, finalize/check icon.

Require period end date; validate threshold range and preserve notes on failures.

12. Loading State
Summary cards, comparison blocks, and note shell skeletonize.

Reconciliation notes saved successfully. and Reconciliation finalized successfully.

UI-046 Promotional Stock Readiness

1. Screen Name
Promotional Stock Readiness

Assess promotional stock readiness, ring-fenced allocations, and launch risk.

Campaign selector, readiness summary cards, campaign product readiness grid, and gap/escalation section.

4. Navigation
Reports & Analytics > Promotional Readiness, with connections to campaign allocation records.

5. Components
Campaign selector, summary cards, readiness table, gap panel, escalation actions, status badges.

6. Tables
Campaign product readiness table with allocated quantity, target quantity, ATP, inbound support, and readiness state.

Campaign, launch date, location scope, readiness status, escalation reason, release or override inputs.

8. Buttons
Check Readiness, Confirm Readiness, Escalate Gap, Release Allocation.

Campaign/megaphone icon, readiness check, at-risk warning, release icon.

Validate dates, allocated quantity against stock, and required authorization/justification for overrides.

Readiness confirmed successfully. or Allocation updated successfully.

UI-047 Audit and Control Review Workspace

Audit and Control Review Workspace

Allow auditors to define scope, inspect transactions and approvals, test controls, document findings, and export evidence.

Scope setup area, sample/review workspace, transaction table, findings panel, and export actions.

Governance & Audit > Audit Workspace, with contextual path to audit trail query and exports.

Scope form, reviewed-transactions table, findings table, evidence panel, export action group, status strip.

Reviewed transactions table and findings table.

Scope dates, location, transaction type, reviewer, finding type, severity, note, and evidence reference.

Start Review, Record Finding, Export Evidence, Complete Review.

Audit/search icon, evidence/attachment icon, finding/warning icon, export icon.

Search immutable audit records and inspect before/after values by entity, actor, date, and action.

Query filter panel at top or left, results table in the main region, and selected record before/after detail panel.

Governance & Audit > Audit Trail Query, with drill-in to related records when allowed.

Query form, results table, audit record viewer, export actions, metadata footer.

Audit trail results table.

Entity type, entity ID, user, date range, action type.

Run Query, Open Record, Export Results.

Audit/log icon, compare/before-after icon, export icon, filter icon.

Query completed successfully. and Audit results exported successfully. when relevant.

Desktop-first investigative screen. Tablet summary review acceptable. Mobile should be read-only or unsupported.

16. Accessibility Notes
Before/after views must use explicit labels and a logical reading order. Exports and record-opening controls must be clearly named.

UI-049 User Account Management

1. Screen Name
User Account Management

2. Purpose
Provision, update, suspend, deactivate, and review user accounts and role assignments.

3. Layout Structure
User directory list, account detail panel, and role assignment section with status and audit metadata.

4. Navigation
Administration > User Accounts, with contextual links to access scope and role assignment details.

5. Components
Users table, detail panel, role assignment widget, status badges, confirmation dialogs, metadata strip.

6. Tables
Users table and role assignments table.

7. Forms
User ID, email, display name, initial roles, role code, location codes, effective dates, suspension reason, deactivation reason.

8. Buttons
Create User, Save, Suspend, Deactivate, Sync Users.

9. Icons
User/profile icon, role/shield icon, suspend/pause icon, deactivate/warning icon, sync icon.

10. Validation
Validate user ID pattern, email format, required display name, at least one role, effective dates, SoD conflicts, and action-specific reasons.

11. Empty State
No user accounts are available in this view. Offer Create User if allowed.

12. Loading State
Directory skeleton and account-detail placeholder.

13. Error State
User accounts could not be loaded. Preserve assignments and notes on save, suspend, or deactivate failure.

14. Success State
User account saved successfully. User suspended successfully. or User deactivated successfully.

15. Responsive Behavior
Desktop/tablet supported. Mobile should be limited to lookup and simple status actions if any.

16. Accessibility Notes
High-priority admin screen. Role assignments must be grouped accessibly, and confirmation dialogs for suspension or deactivation must manage focus correctly.

UI-050 Role and Access Control Administration

1. Screen Name
Role and Access Control Administration

2. Purpose
Configure role permissions, location scope rules, and access enforcement behavior.

3. Layout Structure
Role list on the left, permission matrix/detail panel in the main region, location scope rules section, and conflict warning area.

4. Navigation
Administration > Roles & Access Control, with links to user accounts and SoD evaluation context.

5. Components
Roles table, permission matrix, scope selector, conflict warning panel, save/reset actions, validation banner.

6. Tables
Roles table and permissions matrix table.

7. Forms
Role name or selected role context, permission group assignments, location scope rules, initiator/approver fields for SoD evaluation, transaction type.

8. Buttons
Edit Role, Save Permissions, Validate SoD, Reset Changes.

9. Icons
Shield/permissions icon, matrix/grid icon, warning/conflict icon, validation/check icon.

10. Validation
At least one permission required, SoD rule checks, transaction type validation for evaluation, role assignment authorization rules.

11. Empty State
No role configuration is available in this view.

12. Loading State
Role list and permission matrix show skeletons.

13. Error State
Role and access settings could not be loaded. Preserve matrix edits where possible.

14. Success State
Permissions updated successfully. and Segregation-of-duties validation completed.

15. Responsive Behavior
Desktop-only or desktop-first. Tablet should be read-only at most. Mobile not recommended due to matrix density.

16. Accessibility Notes
High-priority accessibility screen. Permission matrix requires explicit row and column headers, keyboard traversal model, and non-color-only conflict indicators.

Device Support Matrix

This matrix is included to make the responsive intent explicit for AI-generated design concepts.

Screen Group Desktop Tablet Mobile
Authentication Full Full Full
Dashboards and notifications Full Full Summary-friendly
Master data management Full Limited editing Mostly read-only
Procurement planning and PO editing Full Moderate Limited
Warehouse workbenches Full Full for selected tasks Selective only
Inventory monitoring and lookup Full Full Lookup-friendly
Analytics and finance Full Summary review Read-only or unsupported
Audit and admin configuration Full Limited review Unsupported

AI Design Output Guidance

When using this specification with Figma AI or similar tools:

  • Generate desktop-first layouts at 1440px width.
  • Also generate a tablet adaptation at 1024px.
  • Only generate mobile versions for:
    • UI-001
    • UI-002
    • UI-004
    • UI-021
    • UI-034
    • UI-036
    • UI-039 simplified
    • UI-042
  • Use a consistent design system with enterprise data tables, dense but readable forms, clear badges, and accessible status cues.
  • Favor practical enterprise UX over marketing-style layouts.
  • Keep interaction patterns consistent across queue screens, list-detail screens, and analytics screens.

Final Design Intent Summary

The IMS UI should feel:

  • operational
  • structured
  • trustworthy
  • fast to scan
  • keyboard efficient
  • role-aware
  • audit-friendly
  • accessible

It should prioritize clarity, speed, and controlled transactional accuracy over decorative complexity.

Inventory Management System Design System

Purpose

This document defines the design system for the Inventory Management System (IMS). It is intended to support product design, UI design, frontend implementation, QA review, and AI-assisted design generation.

The system should reflect a modern enterprise dashboard style similar to ERP platforms: structured, dense but readable, highly scannable, role-aware, operationally efficient, and accessible.

Design Principles

  • Clarity first: prioritize operational readability over decoration.
  • Enterprise density: support complex workflows without visual clutter.
  • Consistency at scale: shared patterns across inventory, procurement, warehouse, fulfillment, audit, and admin.
  • Action hierarchy: always make the next action obvious.
  • Accessible by default: target WCAG 2.2 AA.
  • Desktop-first, responsive second: optimize heavy workflows for lg and xl, simplify intelligently on smaller screens.

Foundations

Colors

Color Strategy

Use a restrained enterprise palette built around cool neutrals, clear semantic states, and strong contrast. Most screens should feel calm and structured, with status colors used sparingly for alerts, approvals, risks, and workflow states.

State Color Notes

Draft / In Review neutral low emphasis but visible
Approved success for approvals and certifications
Rejected / Failed danger for rejected decisions and blocking failures

Color Usage Rules

  • Never use color as the only indicator of state.
  • Text on primary surfaces should meet a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
  • Use semantic backgrounds in banners, chips, badges, and alert cards, not full-page saturation.
  • Dark sidebar + light content is the default enterprise shell.

Typeface Recommendation

Use a neutral, modern UI sans-serif such as:

  • Inter

Typography Rules

Enterprise Dashboard Style Notes

To keep the IMS visually aligned with modern ERP systems:

  • Use generous structure, not excessive decoration.
  • Keep surfaces mostly neutral with brand color used as an accent.
  • Favor bordered cards and clean panel separation over strong shadows.
  • Use clear iconography and visible labels for operational scanning.
  • Maintain a compact but readable density model.
  • Prioritize data clarity, state clarity, and action clarity over visual novelty.

Recommended Design Tokens Summary

Core Tokens

  • colors: brand, neutral, semantic, surface
  • typography: headings, body, label, mono
  • spacing: 4px-based scale
  • radius: 6 / 8 / 12 / 16 / pill
  • layout: 12-column desktop grid
  • shell: 248px sidebar, 64px header

Default Component Sizes

  • button height: 40px
  • input height: 40px
  • badge height: 24px
  • chip height: 28px to 32px
  • table row height: 48px
  • card padding: 16px or 24px

Usage Guidance for AI Design Tools

When using this design system in Figma AI or similar tools:

  • Generate a desktop-first ERP dashboard design.
  • Use a dark left sidebar and light content area.
  • Use white cards on a soft neutral app background.
  • Use blue as the main action color.
  • Use green, amber, red, and purple for semantic enterprise states.
  • Use Inter or a similar neutral enterprise sans-serif.
  • Favor bordered cards, compact tables, structured forms, and high-scannability layouts.
  • Avoid consumer-app aesthetics such as oversized hero sections, playful gradients, oversized rounded blobs, or excessive illustration.

Final Design Intent

The IMS design system should feel like a modern, dependable enterprise operating environment:

  • precise
  • calm
  • efficient
  • informative
  • role-aware
  • scalable
  • accessible

It should support fast daily execution for warehouse and operations users while still feeling robust enough for finance, audit, and administrative control workflows.

Part X — Frontend Architecture

Inventory Management System Frontend Architecture Mapping

Purpose

This document maps the approved UI design, API design, domain model, and system architecture into a clean Angular frontend architecture. It focuses on feature decomposition, module boundaries, routing, services, DTO usage, and state ownership. It intentionally does not generate Angular code.

Frontend Architecture Principles

  • Organize the Angular app by business capability, not by technical artifact type.
  • Mirror the approved bounded contexts and system modules in the frontend feature structure.
  • Keep route-level pages thin; move orchestration into facades and application services.
  • Prefer standalone routed features or lazy-loaded feature areas with clear public entry points.
  • Separate core, shared, and features concerns:
    • core: app shell, auth/session, guards, interceptors, global layout, permission evaluation.
    • shared: reusable UI components, pipes, directives, presentational widgets, common DTO mappers.
    • features: business workflows aligned to modules such as inventory, procurement, inbound, fulfillment, and administration.
  • Use a facade-first UI architecture:
    • components handle rendering and user interaction
    • facades coordinate page state and commands
    • API services encapsulate HTTP contracts
    • mappers adapt DTOs into frontend view models
  • Keep state ownership explicit:
    • global state only for session, navigation context, notification counts, and app-wide preferences
    • feature state for work queues, filters, selected records, wizard progress, and long-running workflows
    • transient form state stays local to the page or child form components

Recommended State Management Strategy

  • Use Angular Signals for simple shared UI state and session context.
  • Use ComponentStore or a feature-scoped signal store for page/workbench state.
  • Reserve NgRx-style global state only for truly cross-application concerns:
    • authenticated session and user context
    • permission catalog and location scope
    • notification/task counts
    • shell navigation state
  • Treat server data as query-driven state behind facades with caching per feature.
  • Avoid a single monolithic global store for all CRUD screens.

Cross-Cutting Shared Components

Use these shared components consistently across the application:

  • App shell and navigation: GlobalHeader, MainNavigationBar, SecondaryNavigationPanel, BreadcrumbTrail, PageTitleBar, SessionContextBadge
  • Querying and list management: FilterBar, DateRangePicker, SavedViewSelector, DataTable, RowActionMenu, DetailPanel, QueueList
  • Workflow and feedback: StepProgressIndicator, ApprovalDecisionPanel, StatusTimeline, ConfirmationDialog, SuccessWarningErrorBanner, EmptyStatePanel, LoadingSkeleton
  • Forms and auditability: StandardFormSection, LineItemEditor, ValidationMessageBlock, RecordMetadataBlock, EvidenceAttachmentPanel, AuditRecordViewer, PermissionMatrix

Screen-to-Architecture Mapping

UI-001 Sign In / Session Entry

  • Angular feature module: core/auth
  • Main page component: SignInPageComponent
  • Child components: SignInFormComponent, SessionContextPanelComponent
  • Shared components: GlobalHeader, ValidationMessageBlock, SuccessWarningErrorBanner
  • Required Angular services: AuthFacade, SessionService, SessionContextService
  • Required DTOs: SessionResponse, LogoutCommandResultResponse
  • Related API endpoints: GET /api/v1/auth/session, POST /api/v1/auth/logout
  • Required permissions: authenticated session bootstrap only
  • Application routes: /auth/sign-in
  • State management responsibility: local form state plus global session state in core/session

UI-002 Operational Home Dashboard

  • Angular feature module: home
  • Main page component: OperationalDashboardPageComponent
  • Child components: DashboardKpiGridComponent, StockHealthBoardComponent, AlertSummaryWidgetComponent, QuickActionsPanelComponent, MyTasksWidgetComponent
  • Shared components: GlobalHeader, MainNavigationBar, KpiSummaryCard, SummaryStatisticStrip, QuickActionTile, TaskApprovalShortcutWidget, FilterBar
  • Required Angular services: DashboardFacade, DashboardApiService, AlertApiService, TaskInboxService
  • Required DTOs: dashboard and stock-status summary responses from APIs 150, 151, 152, 158
  • Related API endpoints: GET /api/v1/intelligence/dashboard, GET /api/v1/intelligence/stock-status/summary, GET /api/v1/intelligence/stock-status/board, GET /api/v1/intelligence/alerts
  • Required permissions: PERM-083, PERM-085, PERM-064
  • Application routes: /home/operations
  • State management responsibility: feature dashboard state for filters, selected widgets, and refresh cadence

UI-003 Executive KPI Dashboard

  • Angular feature module: reports
  • Main page component: ExecutiveKpiDashboardPageComponent

  • Required Angular services: ExecutiveKpiFacade, ExecutiveKpiApiService
  • Required DTOs: KPI dashboard query DTOs and KpiReportResponse
  • Related API endpoints: GET /api/v1/intelligence/kpis

Routing Recommendation

  • Top-level route groups should mirror business navigation:
    • /home
    • /inventory
    • /products
    • /locations
    • /procurement
    • /inbound
    • /fulfillment
    • /transfers
    • /returns
    • /reports
    • /governance
    • /admin
  • All route groups except /auth should be lazy loaded.
  • Use route guards for:
    • authenticated session
    • permission-based access
    • location-scope validation where a route carries locationCode
  • Prefer route resolvers only for lightweight reference data; main business data should load through facades to preserve retry, skeleton, and refresh behavior.

Service Layer Recommendation

  • ApiService per business sub-domain for HTTP communication.
  • Facade per screen or tightly related screen cluster for orchestration and view-model assembly.
  • LookupService for reusable lists such as locations, reason codes, suppliers, and users.
  • Mapper layer to convert backend DTOs into:
    • list row models
    • detail view models
    • command payloads
    • workflow step summaries

Shared DTO Organization Recommendation

Organize frontend DTO contracts under feature folders, not a single giant shared folder:

features/
  inventory/
    data-access/
      dto/
      mappers/
      services/
  procurement/
    data-access/
      dto/
      mappers/
      services/

Use shared/models/common only for:

  • pagination wrappers
  • command result wrappers
  • audit metadata
  • quantity and monetary primitives
  • session and permission primitives

Clean Architecture Alignment for Angular

  • feature/ui: page components and presentational components
  • feature/application: facades, workflow coordinators, permission orchestration
  • feature/domain: business-oriented frontend models, enums, policy helpers, display rules
  • feature/data-access: HTTP services, DTOs, mappers, repository-style adapters

This keeps Angular aligned with the approved backend architecture while remaining idiomatic for a SPA.

Frontend Risks and Notes

  • Requisition browsing depends on the missing requisition list endpoint identified in API review item C-03. Screens UI-013 and UI-037 should be planned with an API dependency note.
  • Pick/pack/ship workbench completeness depends on the missing location-level pick queue endpoint identified in API review item C-01.
  • Returns receipt should standardize on POST /api/v1/returns/{returnId}/receive as the canonical user-facing path, with POST /api/v1/inbound/return-receipts treated as infrastructure or transitional support.
  • Permission checks should be enforced both at route entry and action level. A visible screen does not imply all commands on that screen are available.

Recommendation Summary

  • Build the Angular app as a capability-aligned modular SPA.
  • Use lazy-loaded feature areas that mirror the 13 approved backend modules, consolidated into practical frontend feature groups.
  • Keep components focused on rendering, facades focused on orchestration, and API services focused on contracts.
  • Use local and feature-scoped state by default, with small global state reserved for session, permissions, shell, and notifications.
  • Standardize shared workflow components for queues, approvals, timelines, filters, and auditability to reduce duplication across the 50 screens.
